ITQAN:v4p335/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p335/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p335/r3.claim: The Qur'an contains dialectical tools—proofs, premises, conclusions, counterargument—and Abraham's disputation with Nimrod and his people.
ITQAN:v4p335/r3.anchor: وأما الجدل فقد حوت آياته من البراهين والمقدمات والنتائج والقول بالموجب والمعارضة

DAMGHANI:v1p189/r1.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p189/r1.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p189/r1.claim: A-lam tara can mean “have you not been told?”; the entry groups examples about Abraham, the people of the elephant, and fallen people.

BURSEVI:v1p337/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p337/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p337/r4.claim: The phrase 'or like the one' coordinates with the preceding 'did you not see'; it means 'or did you see someone like this,' using comparison because many reject resurrection and even more doubt how it occurs.
BURSEVI:v1p337/r4.anchor: عطف على قوله ألم تر وتقديره أو رأيت مثل الذي فعل كذا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p621#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p621#2/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p621#2/r1.claim: “Bahata” means to be bewildered or stunned; it may be transitive or intransitive, and related forms can mean confronting someone with a lie.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p621#2/r1.anchor: بهت: تحير ودهش، ويكون متعديا على وزن فعل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p621#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p621#2/r2.speaker: حديث
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p621#2/r2.claim: A hadith characterizes the Jews as a people prone to falsehood.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p621#2/r2.anchor: وفي الحديث إن اليهود قوم بهت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p624/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p624/r1.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p624/r1.claim: Ali reads “alam tara” with a quiescent final rāʾ, applying pause pronunciation across a connection.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p624/r1.anchor: وقرأ علي بن أبي طالب: ألم تر، بسكون الراء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p624/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p624/r2.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة والربيع والسدي وابن إسحاق وزيد بن أسلم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p624/r2.claim: These authorities identify the disputant as Nimrod son of Canaan son of Cush son of Shem, a ruler associated with the fire and the mosquito.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p624/r2.anchor: قاله مجاهد، وقتادة، والربيع، والسدي، وابن إسحاق، وزيد بن أسلم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p624/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p624/r3.speaker: ابن جريج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p624/r3.claim: Ibn Jurayj says Nimrod was the first king on earth; Ibn Atiyya rejects that claim.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p624/r3.anchor: وقال ابن جريج: هو أول ملك في الأرض، ورده ابن عطية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p624/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p624/r4.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p624/r4.claim: Qatada calls Nimrod the first tyrant and owner of Babylon’s tower; another report says he ruled the entire world.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p624/r4.anchor: وقال قتادة: هو أول من تجبر، وهو صاحب الصرح ببابل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p624/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p624/r5.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p624/r5.claim: Mujahid divides world-rulers into two believing kings, Solomon and Dhu al-Qarnayn, and two unbelieving kings, Nimrod and Nebuchadnezzar.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p624/r5.anchor: وقال مجاهد: ملك الأرض مؤمنان: سليمان وذو القرنين، وكافران: نمروذ

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p624/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p624/r6.speaker: السهيلي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p624/r6.claim: Al-Suhayli gives a different lineage and associates Nimrod with the Sudanese king al-Dahhak, later killed by Afridun; Abu Tammam likens a patron to Afridun in a poem.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p624/r6.anchor: وحكى السهيلي أنه: النمروذ بن كوش بن كنعان بن حام بن نوح

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p624/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p624/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p624/r7.claim: “He disputed with Abraham about his Lord” can mean he countered Abraham’s proof, brought a rebuttal, or sought to prevail in argument.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p624/r7.anchor: ومعنى: حاج إبراهيم في ربه أي: عارض حجته بمثلها، أو: أتى على الحجة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p624/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p624/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p624/r8.claim: One account places the debate after Abraham broke the idols during a festival; when asked whom he worshipped, he named the Lord who gives life and death.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p624/r8.anchor: قيل: خرجوا إلى عيد لهم، فدخل إبراهيم على أصنامهم فكسرها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p625/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p625/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p625/r1.claim: Other accounts place the dispute in Nimrod’s grain-rationing court: visitors prostrated to receive food, while Abraham refused and named his Lord; another says Nimrod routinely asked each visitor to acknowledge him as lord.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p625/r1.anchor: وفي قوله: إنه كان كلما جاء قوم قال من ربكم وإلهكم؟

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p625/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p625/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p625/r2.claim: A further report says the debate followed Abraham’s escape from the fire: denied food, he carried sand home, where it became excellent food by God’s provision; a variant says red sand became red wheat.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p625/r2.anchor: وقيل: كانت المحاجة بعد أن خرج من النار التي ألقاه فيها النمروذ

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p625/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p625/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p625/r3.claim: The pronoun in “about his Lord” most naturally refers to Abraham, though it could refer to Nimrod.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p625/r3.anchor: في: ربه، يحتمل أن يعود الضمير على إبراهيم، وأن يعود على النمروذ، والظاهر الأول.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p625/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p625/r4.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p625/r4.claim: The majority take the pronoun in “when God gave him kingship” to refer to the disputant; the causal phrase means kingship made him arrogant, or that he challenged God instead of showing gratitude for it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p625/r4.anchor: الظاهر أن الضمير في: آتاه، عائد على: الذي حاج، وهو قول الجمهور

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p625/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p625/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p625/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhshari proposes a temporal reading, “at the time He gave him kingship”; Abu Hayyan finds it strained unless time means a broad period, and rejects treating the clause itself as a temporal noun.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p625/r5.anchor: وأجاز الزمخشري أن يكون التقدير: حاج وقت أن آتاه الله الملك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p625/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p625/r6.speaker: المهدوي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p625/r6.claim: Al-Mahdawi allows the pronoun to refer to Abraham, meaning God gave him the kingship of prophethood.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p625/r6.anchor: وقال المهدوي: يحتمل أن يعود الضمير على إبراهيم: أي آتاه ملك النبوة.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p626/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p626/r1.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p626/r1.claim: Ibn Atiyya calls al-Mahdawi’s interpretation an overstrained reading; the view that Abraham received kingship is associated with the Muʿtazila, who cite God’s covenant and the great kingdom given to Abraham’s family.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p626/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطية: وهذا تحامل من التأويل. انتهى. وما ذكره المهدوي احتمالا هو قول المعتزلة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p626/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p626/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p626/r2.claim: Abu Hayyan rejects the proposed objections to Abraham’s kingship: spiritual authority as prophethood can coexist with Nimrod’s worldly power, wealth, and coercive rule.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p626/r2.anchor: ولا يرد على المعتزلة بهذه الأوجه، لأن إثبات ملك النبوة لإبراهيم لا ينافي ملك الكافر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p626/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p626/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p626/r3.claim: Asked why God gives kingship to an unbeliever, al-Zamakhshari answers that worldly assets and followers were given, or that kingship tested people; Abu Hayyan detects Muʿtazilite doctrine in denying divine enabling of domination.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p626/r3.anchor: قال الزمخشري: فإن قلت: كيف جاز أن يؤتي الله الملك الكافر؟

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p626/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p626/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p626/r4.claim: Abraham’s statement that his Lord gives life and death answers the disputant’s prior question about who his Lord is; it would not begin an unprompted exchange.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p626/r4.anchor: هذا من إبراهيم عن سؤال سبق من الكافر، وهو أن قال: من ربك؟

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p626/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p626/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p626/r5.claim: Abraham invokes life and death because they are among God’s most original, renowned signs of power; the “when” clause grammatically attaches to “disputed.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p626/r5.anchor: واختص إبراهيم من آيات الله بالإحياء والإماتة لأنهما أبدع آيات الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p626/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p626/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p626/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhshari’s proposal that the “when” clause substitutes for “when He gave him kingship” is weak because the two events occurred at different times; Abraham’s wording also supports taking “his Lord” as Abraham’s Lord.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p626/r6.anchor: وقد ذكرنا ضعف ذلك، وأيضا فالظرفان مختلفان إذ وقت إيتاء الملك ليس وقت قوله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p628/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p628/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p628/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says Abraham could have answered Nimrod by asking him to revive a killed man; one report says he did, then added the sun argument to end debate rather than from weakness.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p628/r1.anchor: ومعنى قول الزمخشري: وكان الاعتراض عتيدا: أي من إبراهيم، لو أراد أن يعترض عليه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p628/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p628/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p628/r2.claim: On one account Nimrod claimed divinity and pretended that killing one man and sparing another meant he gave life and death; Abraham then challenged him to bring the sun from the west, exposing his inability.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p628/r2.anchor: وقيل: كان نمروذ يدعي الربوبية، فلما قال له: إبراهيم ربي الذي يحيي ويميت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p628/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p628/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p628/r3.claim: Another account says Nimrod challenged Abraham to prove he had seen resurrection; Abraham moved to a clearer sign visible to both men.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p628/r3.anchor: وقيل: لما قال: ربي الذي يحيي ويميت قال له النمروذ: وأنت رأيت هذا؟

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p628/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p628/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p628/r4.claim: A further explanation says Abraham chose the sun because his interlocutors revered it, showing that it too was subject to God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p628/r4.anchor: كانوا يعظمون الشمس، فأشار إلى أنها لله عز وجل مقهورة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p629/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p629/r1.speaker: المحققون
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p629/r1.claim: The conjunction implies an omitted conditional challenge; Abu Hayyan reconstructs it as Abraham saying that if Nimrod claimed such power, God brings the sun as described.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p629/r1.anchor: وتقدير الجملة، والله أعلم قال إبراهيم إن زعمت ذلك أو موهت بذلك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p629/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p629/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p629/r2.claim: The conjunction in “for God brings the sun” implies an omitted prior conditional thought, such as “if you claim that, then God brings the sun”; the preposition makes the sun the object moved, and مِن marks origin.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p629/r2.anchor: ومجيء الفاء في: فإن، يدل على جملة محذوفة قبلها، إذ لو كانت هي المحكية فقط

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p629/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p629/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p629/r3.claim: Most reciters read “fa-buhita” passively; its omitted agent is Abraham or his utterance. Other readings are active: Ibn al-Sumayfiʿ may mean Abraham stunned the unbeliever, the unbeliever insulted Abraham, or the unbeliever uttered falsehood; Abu Haywa and a reading reported by al-Akhfash vary the vowel.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p629/r3.anchor: فبهت الذي كفر قراءة الجمهور مبنيا لما لم يسم فاعله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p629/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p629/r4.speaker: ابن السميفع
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p629/r4.claim: Ibn al-Sumayfiʿ reads the verb actively with fatḥa on both letters; interpretations include Abraham stunning the unbeliever, the defeated unbeliever insulting Abraham, or the unbeliever speaking falsely.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p629/r4.anchor: وقرأ ابن السميفع: فبهت، بفتح الباء والهاء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p629/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p629/r5.speaker: أبو حيوة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p629/r5.claim: Abu Haywa reads the verb with fatḥa on bāʾ and ḍamma on hāʾ; al-Akhfash also reports a kasra reading.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p629/r5.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة: فبهت، بفتح الباء وضم الهاء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p629/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p629/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p629/r6.claim: “God does not guide the unjust” has been restricted to guidance in argument, entry to reward or Paradise, or divine inspiration and enabling; some restrict “unjust” to those who die as unbelievers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p629/r6.anchor: فما ذكر في الهداية الخاصة أنه لا يرشدهم في حجتهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p629/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p629/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p629/r7.claim: Abu Hayyan takes the statement to concern those decreed to persist as unbelievers, who cannot receive guidance; the claim to divine power is blatant injustice, and God leaves Nimrod stunned to honor Abraham and manifest the truth.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p629/r7.anchor: والذي يظهر أن هذا إخبار من الله بأن من حكم عليه، وقضى بأن يكون ظالما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p630/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p630/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p630/r1.claim: One explanation says Nimrod did not claim to control sunrise because his subjects knew the sun preceded him, nor sunset because he knew he could not do it; he fell silent.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p630/r1.anchor: وقيل: إنما لم يدع أنه هو الذي يأتي بها من المشرق، لظهور كذبه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p649/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p649/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p649/r1.claim: The three stories use eloquent question-and-answer dialogue with repeated قال and little coordination: when meaning itself connects successive clauses, an added conjunction is better omitted.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p649/r1.anchor: وقد تضمنت هذه القصص الثلاث، من فصيح المحاورة بذكر: قال، سؤالا وجوابا،

AKHFASH:v1p196#2/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p196#2/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p196#2/r1.claim: In فبهت الذي كفر, Abraham stunned the disbeliever; the form بهت is better and more common.
AKHFASH:v1p196#2/r1.anchor: أي: بهته إبراهيم و {بهت} أجود وأكثر.

FARRA:v1p168/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p168/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p168/r1.claim: كأين and كم are dialectal forms with the same meaning; أبي's reading كأين is another form.
FARRA:v1p168/r1.anchor: وفي قراءة أبي كأين من فئة قليلة غلبت وهما لغتان

FARRA:v1p168/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p168/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p168/r2.claim: After كم without من, the indefinite noun may be accusative by the original interrogative and number explanation, genitive by an understood من, or nominative through the verb; the cited poetry illustrates the alternatives.
FARRA:v1p168/r2.anchor: فمن نصب قال: كان أصل كم الاستفهام، وما بعدها من النكرة مفسر كتفسير العدد

FARRA:v1p168/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p168/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p168/r3.claim: A nominative noun after كم can reflect an understood fronted verb, as in امرؤ القيس's line; indefinites do not normally precede their governing verbs.
FARRA:v1p168/r3.anchor: وقال امرؤ القيس: تبوص وكم من دونها من مفازة

FARRA:v1p168/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p168/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p168/r4.claim: Arabs add إلى after ترى to express amazement; the sense is have you seen such a person, which aligns the two examples beginning with أو.
FARRA:v1p168/r4.anchor: وإدخال العرب (إلى) في هذا الموضع على جهة التعجب

FARRA:v1p168/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p168/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p168/r5.claim: The parallel questions about who owns the earth and who rules the heavens show that a response may be supplied after the question rather than repeated in its opening form.
FARRA:v1p168/r5.anchor: قل لمن الأرض ومن فيها إن كنتم تعلمون. سيقولون لله

ALUSI-FULL:v3p24/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p24/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p24/r10.claim: The disputant may be Nimrod, the commanding soul that argues against Abraham’s sacred spirit; the granted kingdom symbolizes bodily powers and this low world, or the account is historical.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p24/r10.anchor: وهو نمروذ النفس الأمارة الجادلة لإبراهيم الروح القدسية التى ألقيت في نار الطبيعة

ALUSI-FULL:v3p25/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p25/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p25/r1.claim: Abraham can signify the spirit or the historical patriarch; Nimrod’s claim to give life and death allegorizes diverting powers into pleasure or temporarily withholding them, alongside pardon and killing.

ALUSI-FULL:v3p25/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p25/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p25/r2.claim: God brings the sun of gnosis from its eastern source; the demand to bring it from the west either tests Nimrod or asks the spirit to return after setting in the body.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p25/r2.anchor: من مشرقها ) وهو جانب المبدأ الفياض

MAJAZ:v1p79/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p79/r3.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p79/r3.claim: Bahita means he was confounded and his argument gone; bahuta can also mean he spoke at length.
MAJAZ:v1p79/r3.anchor: «فبهت» (258) : انقطع، وذهبت حجته، وبهت: أكثر الكلام، وبهت إن شئت.

DURR-FULL:v2p25/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p25/r1.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v2p25/r1.claim: Mujahid says Nimrod’s claim to give life and death meant that he could kill whom he wished and spare whom he wished; he also lists four rulers of the earth, two believers and two unbelievers.
DURR-FULL:v2p25/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {قال أنا أحيي وأميت} قال: أقتل من شئت واستحيي من شئت

DURR-FULL:v2p25/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p25/r2.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v2p25/r2.claim: Al-Suddī says Nimrod claimed to give life by feeding two starving prisoners and death by leaving two others unfed; Abraham answered that God brings the sun from the east, challenging him to reverse its course, and Nimrod called Abraham mad.
DURR-FULL:v2p25/r2.anchor: عن السدي قال: لما خرج إبراهيم من النار أدخلوه على الملك ولم يكن قبل ذلك دخل عليه

DURR-FULL:v2p25/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p25/r3.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v2p25/r3.claim: Al-Suddī interprets God’s not guiding wrongdoers as not guiding them to faith.
DURR-FULL:v2p25/r3.anchor: عن السدي {والله لا يهدي القوم الظالمين} قال: إلى الإيمان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p31/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p31/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p31/r1.claim: Abraham's disputation is the first and most comprehensive example of the preceding believer-guidance and disbeliever-misguidance, containing both sides.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p31/r1.anchor: ساق ثلاثة شواهد على ذلك هذا أولها وأجمعها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p31/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p31/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p31/r2.claim: The scene exemplifies polytheists arguing with the Prophet about resurrection; the following comparison with one who passed a town supports this reading.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p31/r2.anchor: تمثيل حال المشركين في مجادلتهم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في البعث

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p31/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p31/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p31/r3.claim: The question ألم تر is figurative and conveys astonishment, as discussed at the earlier story of those who left their homes.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p31/r3.anchor: والاستفهام في { ألم تر } مجازي متضمن معنى التعجيب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p31/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p31/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p31/r4.claim: The argument establishes God's oneness and rejects other gods because God alone gives life and death and creates the world visible to people.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p31/r4.anchor: لإثبات الوحدانية لله تعالى وإبطال إلاهية غيره لانفراده بالإحياء والإماتة ، وانفراده بخلق العوالم المشهودة للناس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p31/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p31/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p31/r5.claim: Ḥājja means to dispute and is a form-III verb without a known simple-stem counterpart or known etymological root.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p31/r5.anchor: ومعنى { حاج } خاصم ، وهو فعل جاء على زنة المفاعلة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p31/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p31/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p31/r6.claim: Although ḥujjah means a proof, ḥājja usually means contentious, often false, disputation, as shown by several Qur'anic parallels.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p31/r6.anchor: ومن العجيب أن الحجة في كلام العرب البرهان المصدق للدعوى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p332#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p332#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p332#2/r1.claim: The opening question expresses amazement at Nimrod's disputation about God and his disbelief.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p332#2/r1.anchor: تعجيب من محاجة نمروذ في الله وكفره به

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p332#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p332#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p332#2/r2.claim: The grant of kingship may explain his dispute because it made him arrogant and tyrannical, or because he perversely disputed instead of thanking God for the gift.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p332#2/r2.anchor: ايتاء الملك أبطره واورثه الكبر والعتو

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p332#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p332#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p332#2/r3.claim: Alternatively, the phrase means that Nimrod disputed at the time God gave him kingship.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p332#2/r3.anchor: والاني حاج وقت أن آتاه الله الملك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p332#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p332#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p332#2/r4.claim: God's granting kingship to an unbeliever may mean granting the wealth, servants, and followers by which he became dominant, without divine empowerment to prevail.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p332#2/r4.anchor: آتاه ما غلب به وتسلط من المال والخدم والأتباع

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p332#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p332#2/r5.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p332#2/r5.claim: Another view says God made him king as a test for His servants.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p333/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p333/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p333/r1.claim: The time clause إذ قال is governed by حاج, or it substitutes for the time clause in آتاه because آتاه is construed as a time expression.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p333/r1.anchor: نصب بحاج أو بدل من آتاه اذ جعل بمعنى الوقت

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p333/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p333/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p333/r2.claim: Nimrod's claim to give life and death means that he pardons one condemned to die and kills another.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p333/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p333/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p333/r3.claim: Ibrahim changed to a proof Nimrod could not answer after hearing his foolish reply, demonstrating that a debater may move from one argument to another.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p333/r3.anchor: وهذا دليل على جواز الانتقال للمجادل من حجة إلى حجة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p333/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p333/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p333/r4.claim: A reading of فبهت is explained as Ibrahim having defeated the unbeliever.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p333/r4.anchor: وقرىء ( فبهت الذي كفر ) أي فغلب إبراهيم الكافر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p333/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p333/r5.speaker: أبو حيوة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p333/r5.claim: Abu Haywa read فبهت on the pattern of qaruba; another explanation takes it to mean that the unbeliever was confounded.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p333/r5.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة ( فبهت ) بوزن قرب وقيل كانت هذه المحاجة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p333/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p333/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p333/r6.claim: One account dates the dispute to after Abraham broke the idols and Nimrod imprisoned him, then released him to be burned and asked who his Lord was.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p333/r6.anchor: كانت هذه المحاجة حين كسر الأصنام وسجنه نمروذ

RAZI-FULL:v7p19/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p19/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p19/r1.claim: The passage presents three stories: the first establishes the Creator, the second establishes resurrection, and the first is Abraham's debate with his contemporary ruler.
RAZI-FULL:v7p19/r1.anchor: إعلم أنه تعالى ذكر هاهنا قصصا ثلاثة : الأولى : منها في بيان إثبات العلم بالصانع

RAZI-FULL:v7p19/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p19/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p19/r2.claim: Alam tara is grammatically a question used to arrest attention and express amazement, as in asking whether one has seen someone act a certain way.
RAZI-FULL:v7p19/r2.anchor: فهي كلمة يوقف بها المخاطب على تعجب منها ، ولفظها لفظ الاستفهام

RAZI-FULL:v7p19/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p19/r3.speaker: مجاهد
RAZI-FULL:v7p19/r3.claim: Mujahid identifies the challenger as Nimrod son of Canaan, the first tyrant to claim divinity.
RAZI-FULL:v7p19/r3.anchor: فقال مجاهد : هو نمروذ بن كنعان ، وهو أول من

RAZI-FULL:v7p19/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p19/r4.speaker: مقاتل
RAZI-FULL:v7p19/r4.claim: One report from Muqatil places the debate after Abraham broke the idols but before he was thrown into the fire; others place it afterward.
RAZI-FULL:v7p19/r4.anchor: قيل : إنه عند كسر الأصنام قبل الإلقاء في النار عن مقاتل

RAZI-FULL:v7p19/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p19/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p19/r5.claim: Muhajjaja means to contend or overcome in argument.

RAZI-FULL:v7p19/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p19/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p19/r6.claim: The pronoun in regarding his Lord most likely refers to Abraham, as in the verse about Abraham's people disputing with him concerning God.
RAZI-FULL:v7p19/r6.anchor: والأول أظهر ، كما قال : { وحاجه قومه قال أتحاجونى فى الله }

RAZI-FULL:v7p19/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p19/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p19/r7.claim: One interpretation makes the pronoun in when God gave him kingship refer to Abraham.
RAZI-FULL:v7p19/r7.anchor: أن الهاء في آتاه عائد إلى إبراهيم

RAZI-FULL:v7p19/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p19/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p19/r8.claim: The Abraham reading cites the verse saying Abraham's family received Scripture, wisdom, and great dominion, understood as prophetic authority.
RAZI-FULL:v7p19/r8.anchor: { فقد ءاتينا ءال إبراهيم الكتاب والحكمة وءاتيناهم ملكا عظيما }

RAZI-FULL:v7p19/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p19/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p19/r9.claim: The Abraham reading argues that God would not give kingship to unbelievers who claim divinity.
RAZI-FULL:v7p19/r9.anchor: أنه تعالى لا يجوز أن يؤتي الملك الكفار ، ويدعي الربوبية لنفسه

RAZI-FULL:v7p19/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p19/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p19/r10.claim: The Abraham reading also invokes the grammatical preference for returning a pronoun to the nearest antecedent.
RAZI-FULL:v7p19/r10.anchor: أن عود الضمير إلى أقرب المذكورين واجب

RAZI-FULL:v7p19/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p19/r11.speaker: جمهور المفسرين
RAZI-FULL:v7p19/r11.claim: The majority of exegetes take the pronoun to refer to the man who argued with Abraham, namely the king.
RAZI-FULL:v7p19/r11.anchor: وهو قول جمهور المفسرين : أن الضمير عائد إلى ذلك الإنسان الذي حاج إبراهيم

RAZI-FULL:v7p20/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p20/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p20/r1.claim: The Abraham reading's first proof establishes dominion for Abraham's family, not for Abraham himself.
RAZI-FULL:v7p20/r1.anchor: بأن هذه الآية دالة على حصول الملك لآل إبراهيم ، وليس فيها دلالة على حصول الملك

RAZI-FULL:v7p20/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p20/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p20/r2.claim: The opposing reading understands kingship as worldly power and capability, which experience shows God may grant to an unbeliever; the king might also have received it before later disbelief.
RAZI-FULL:v7p20/r2.anchor: بأن المراد من الملك هاهنا التمكن والقدرة والبسطة في الدنيا

RAZI-FULL:v7p20/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p20/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p20/r3.claim: Although Abraham is the nearest antecedent, many reports identify the challenger as the king, outweighing proximity.
RAZI-FULL:v7p20/r3.anchor: الروايات الكثيرة واردة بأن الذي حاج إبراهيم كان هو الملك

RAZI-FULL:v7p20/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p20/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p20/r4.claim: The phrase because God gave him kingship supports the king reading: power made him arrogant enough to contend with Abraham.
RAZI-FULL:v7p20/r4.anchor: أن إيتاء الملك أبطره وأورثه الكبر والعتو فحاج لذلك

RAZI-FULL:v7p20/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p20/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p20/r5.claim: Another reading portrays the challenge as the king's inverted response to God's favor, like repaying kindness with hostility; such arrogance suits a tyrant, not a prophet.
RAZI-FULL:v7p20/r5.anchor: جعل محاجته في ربه شكرا على أن آتاه ربه الملك

RAZI-FULL:v7p20/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p20/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p20/r6.claim: The king was the challenger because Abraham's public call to truth is more impressive when he faces a powerful unbelieving sovereign than when he himself is king.
RAZI-FULL:v7p20/r6.anchor: ومتى كان الكافر سلطانا مهيبا ، وإبراهيم ما كان ملكا ، كان هذا المعنى أتم

RAZI-FULL:v7p21/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p21/r1.speaker: أبو بكر الأصم
RAZI-FULL:v7p21/r1.claim: Al-Asamm argues that if Abraham were king, he would have prevented the unbeliever from killing one man and sparing another.
RAZI-FULL:v7p21/r1.anchor: ما ذكره أبو بكر الأصم ، وهو أن إبراهيم صلى الله عليه وسلم لو كان هو الملك

RAZI-FULL:v7p21/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p21/r2.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v7p21/r2.claim: The Qadi calls this proof weak: Abraham may have held spiritual authority while the unbeliever held oppressive political power, or the executed man may have been selected by others or spared for ransom.
RAZI-FULL:v7p21/r2.anchor: قال القاضي هذا الاستدلال ضعيف ، لأنه من المحتمل أن يقال : إن إبراهيم صلى الله عليه وسلم كان ملكا

RAZI-FULL:v7p21/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p21/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p21/r3.claim: The verse reports and promises but does not say in the Quran that the king actually performed the killing-and-sparing act.
RAZI-FULL:v7p21/r3.anchor: وأيضا قوله { ألم تر إلى } خبر ووعد ، ولا دليل في القرآن على أنه فعله

RAZI-FULL:v7p21/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p21/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p21/r4.claim: An omitted prior question is implied: Abraham proclaimed his message, the rejecter asked who his Lord was, and Abraham answered; the story of Moses and Pharaoh supplies a parallel.
RAZI-FULL:v7p21/r4.anchor: الظاهر أن هذا جواب سؤال سابق غير مذكور

RAZI-FULL:v7p21/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p21/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p21/r5.claim: Abraham's proof begins from life and death, which creatures cannot produce; their occurrence by choice requires another agent, who must be powerful and freely acting rather than a necessary cause.
RAZI-FULL:v7p21/r5.anchor: لا سبيل إلى معرفة الله تعالى إلا بواسطة أفعاله التي لا يشاركه فيها أحد من القادرين

RAZI-FULL:v7p21/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p21/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p21/r6.claim: A necessary cause would produce an unchanging effect, contrary to life changing into death and death into life; varied animal forms and properties likewise show a freely acting creator.
RAZI-FULL:v7p21/r6.anchor: لأنه يلزم من دوامه دوام الأثر ، فكان يجب أن لا يتبدل الأحياء بالإماتة

RAZI-FULL:v7p21#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p21#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p21#2/r1.claim: Life is mentioned before death because the aim is a clear proof for God, and the marvels of creation during life are more numerous and more accessible to observation.
RAZI-FULL:v7p21#2/r1.anchor: ولا شك أن عجائب الخلقة حال الحياة أكثر ، واطلاع الإنسان عليها أتم

RAZI-FULL:v7p21#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p21#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p21#2/r2.claim: A familiar interpretation says the king killed one man and spared another, claiming thereby to give life and death.
RAZI-FULL:v7p21#2/r2.anchor: يروى أن إبراهيم عليه السلام لما احتج بتلك الحجة ، دعا ذلك الملك الكافر شخصين

RAZI-FULL:v7p21#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p21#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p21#2/r3.claim: Al-Razi considers that interpretation implausible: Abraham's proof distinguished real creation from killing or releasing, a difference no reasonable audience could miss.
RAZI-FULL:v7p21#2/r3.anchor: امتنع أن يشتبه على العاقل الإماتة والإحياء على ذلك الوجه بالإماتة والإحياء بمعنى القتل وتركه

RAZI-FULL:v7p21#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p21#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p21#2/r4.claim: Al-Razi instead reconstructs the king's objection as asking whether God creates life and death directly or through earthly and heavenly causes; humans also cause them indirectly through sex and poison.
RAZI-FULL:v7p21#2/r4.anchor: تدعى الإحياء والإماتة من الله ابتداء من غير واسطة الأسباب الأرضية والأسباب السماوية

RAZI-FULL:v7p21#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p21#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p21#2/r5.claim: Abraham's answer, in this reconstruction, is that even if celestial configurations mediate life and death, God directs those motions; humans cannot control them, so their agency is different.
RAZI-FULL:v7p21#2/r5.anchor: لا بد لتلك الاتصالات والحركات الفلكية من فاعل مدبر

RAZI-FULL:v7p22/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p22/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p22/r1.claim: The sun's rising is not a second proof but completes the first: celestial motions are God's, whereas humans cannot control them, so human actions do not refute divine life-giving and death-causing.
RAZI-FULL:v7p22/r1.anchor: ليس دليلا آخر ، بل تمام الدليل

RAZI-FULL:v7p22/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p22/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p22/r2.claim: Al-Razi says this reconstruction is his own considered account of the debate, rather than the familiar interpretation.
RAZI-FULL:v7p22/r2.anchor: فهذا هو الذي أعتقده في كيفية جريان هذه المناظرة ، لا ما هو المشهور عند الكل

RAZI-FULL:v7p22/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p22/r3.speaker: جمهور القراء
RAZI-FULL:v7p22/r3.claim: The readers generally drop the extra alif of ana in connected recitation throughout the Quran; a report from Nafi retains it before a hamza, but al-Razi prefers the majority.
RAZI-FULL:v7p22/r3.anchor: أجمع القراء على إسقاط ألف { أنا } في الوصل في جميع القرآن ، إلا ما روي عن نافع

RAZI-FULL:v7p22/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p22/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p22/r4.claim: The pronoun ana is hamza plus nun; the extra alif belongs only to pause and drops in connection, like the pausal h and hamzat al-wasl.
RAZI-FULL:v7p22/r4.anchor: فأمّا الألف فإنما تلحقها في الوقف كما تلحق الهاء في سكوته للوقف

RAZI-FULL:v7p22/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p22/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p22/r5.claim: Most exegetes say Abraham shifted to a clearer proof after the king's objection, showing a debater may move from one proof to another.
RAZI-FULL:v7p22/r5.anchor: طريقة أكثر المفسرين أن إبراهيم عليه السلام لما رأى من نمروذ أنه ألقى تلك الشبهة عدل عن ذلك إلى دليل آخر

RAZI-FULL:v7p23/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p23/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p23/r1.claim: One response to why Nimrod did not ask God to bring the sun from the west is that he had seen Abraham survive the fire and knew God could do it.
RAZI-FULL:v7p23/r1.anchor: أن هذه المحاجة كانت مع إبراهيم بعد إلقائه في النار وخروجه منها سالما

RAZI-FULL:v7p23/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p23/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p23/r2.claim: Another response is that God disabled Nimrod and made him forget this counterchallenge to support His prophet.
RAZI-FULL:v7p23/r2.anchor: أن الله خذله وأنساه إيراد هذه الشبهة نصرة لنبيه

RAZI-FULL:v7p23/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p23/r3.speaker: المحققون
RAZI-FULL:v7p23/r3.claim: The investigators say Abraham did not switch proofs: one argument is that events humans cannot cause require another agent, illustrated first by life and death and then by celestial motions.
RAZI-FULL:v7p23/r3.anchor: إن هذا ما كان انتقالا من دليل إلى دليل آخر بل الدليل واحد في الموضعين

RAZI-FULL:v7p23/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p23/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p23/r4.claim: Al-Razi judges the single-proof interpretation better suited to rigorous reasoning than the popular explanation of switching arguments.
RAZI-FULL:v7p23/r4.anchor: وهذا الوجه أحسن من الأول وأليق بكلام أهل التحقيق منه

RAZI-FULL:v7p23/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p23/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p23/r5.claim: A first objection to both readings is that a sound disputant must answer a damaging doubt immediately rather than leave its confusion uncorrected.
RAZI-FULL:v7p23/r5.anchor: وجب على المحق القادر على الجواب أن يذكر الجواب في الحال إزالة لذلك التلبيس

RAZI-FULL:v7p23/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p23/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p23/r6.claim: A second objection says abandoning the first point could make Abraham appear to admit that his original proof was weak and that the king exposed its flaw.
RAZI-FULL:v7p23/r6.anchor: أوهم أن كلامه الأول كان ضعيفا ساقطا ، وأنه ما كان عالما بضعفه

RAZI-FULL:v7p23#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p23#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p23#2/r1.claim: A third objection says the sun example is less clear: humans cannot create life, but might move bodies, or a mighty being might move the heavens.
RAZI-FULL:v7p23#2/r1.anchor: لأن جنس الإحياء لا قدرة للخلق عليه ، وأما جنس تحريك الأجسام ، فللخلق قدرة عليه

RAZI-FULL:v7p24/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p24/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p24/r1.claim: Al-Razi says rebutting the weak objection about life and death is easier than accepting a demand that the sun rise from the west.
RAZI-FULL:v7p24/r1.anchor: ومن المعلوم أن الاشتغال بإظهار فساد سؤاله في الإحياء والإماتة أسهل بكثير من التزام إطلاع الشمس من المغرب

RAZI-FULL:v7p24/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p24/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p24/r2.claim: A fifth objection says Nimrod could claim to make the sun rise in the east and ask Abraham's God to make it rise in the west; some exegetes say God would then reverse it.
RAZI-FULL:v7p24/r2.anchor: أن نمروذ لما لم يستح من معارضة الإحياء والإماتة الصادرين عن الله تعالى بالقتل والتخلية

RAZI-FULL:v7p24/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p24/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p24/r3.claim: Al-Razi says accepting that counterfactual entails that only a westward sunrise would prove a creator, leaves Abraham's silence unexplained, and makes the popular account implausible.
RAZI-FULL:v7p24/r3.anchor: فظهر بهذا أن هذا التفسير الذي أجمع المفسرون عليه ضعيف

RAZI-FULL:v7p24/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p24/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p24/r4.claim: His reconstruction avoids the objections: Nimrod's sophistry says direct divine action cannot be shown and mediated action resembles human action; Abraham answers that God controls celestial causes and humans do not.
RAZI-FULL:v7p24/r4.anchor: ومتى حملنا الكلام على هذا الوجه لم يكن شيء من المحذورات المذكورة لازما عليه

RAZI-FULL:v7p24#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p24#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p24#2/r1.claim: Bahita means the defeated man was left speechless, unable to make a reply; the word has three forms, and ʿUrwa al-ʿUdhrī uses it for being stunned and silent.
RAZI-FULL:v7p24#2/r1.anchor: فبقي مغلوبا لا يجد مقالا ، ولا للمسألة جوابه

RAZI-FULL:v7p24#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p24#2/r2.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v7p24#2/r2.claim: Al-Qadi suggests God does not guide unbelievers to arguments or truth because they oppose them; al-Razi rejects this since no argument exists for unbelief to guide them toward.
RAZI-FULL:v7p24#2/r2.anchor: قال القاضي : يحتمل وجوها : منها أنه لا يهديهم لظلمهم وكفرهم للحجاج وللحق

RAZI-FULL:v7p24#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p24#2/r3.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v7p24#2/r3.claim: Al-Qadi proposes that injustice bars unbelievers from benefiting from additional divine favors; al-Razi says it is incoherent to say God withholds what is rationally impossible for them to receive.
RAZI-FULL:v7p24#2/r3.anchor: لا يهديهم لزيادات الألطاف من حيث أنهم بالكفر والظلم سدوا

RAZI-FULL:v7p24#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p24#2/r4.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v7p24#2/r4.claim: Al-Qadi reads the denial of guidance as denial of afterlife reward and Paradise; al-Razi rejects this because Paradise is absent from the context of reasoning and recognition.
RAZI-FULL:v7p24#2/r4.anchor: قال القاضي : ومنها أنه تعالى لا يهديهم إلى الثواب في الآخرة ولا يهديهم إلى الجنة

RAZI-FULL:v7p24#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p24#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p24#2/r5.claim: In context, the proof was so clear that the opponent was silenced, yet it did not benefit him because God did not grant him guidance; this resembles the warning in 6:111.
RAZI-FULL:v7p24#2/r5.anchor: اللائق بسياق الآية أن يقال إنه تعالى لما بين أن الدليل كان قد بلغ في الظهور

TABATABAI:2:258-260/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:258-260/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:258-260/r1.claim: He rejects excluding Nimrod’s kingship from God because it was unjust: the Qur’an attributes kingship and wealth even to Pharaoh and Qarun and says all sovereignty belongs to God.
TABATABAI:2:258-260/r1.anchor: فما من ملك إلا وهو منه تعالى

TABATABAI:2:258-260/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:258-260/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:258-260/r2.claim: The passage depicts Nimrod disputing Abraham’s monotheism and faith, not his right to rule; visible political kingship belonged to Nimrod, so there was no royal claim to contest.
TABATABAI:2:258-260/r2.anchor: فإن ظاهرها أن نمرود كان ينازع إبراهيم في توحيده وإيمانه

TABATABAI:2:258-260/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:258-260/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:258-260/r3.claim: Kingship, like everything else, has a relation to God, so attributing it to Him presents no difficulty.
TABATABAI:2:258-260/r3.anchor: أن لكل شيء نسبة إلى الله سبحانه والملك من جملة الأشياء

TABATABAI:2:258-260/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:258-260/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:258-260/r4.claim: Abraham may mean animal life and death specifically, or life and death generally; Nimrod’s claim to grant and take life is explained by reports that he released one prisoner and executed another, not by plant cultivation or animal breeding.
TABATABAI:2:258-260/r4.anchor: أمر بإحضار رجلين ممن كان في سجنه فأطلق أحدهما وقتل الآخر

TABATABAI:2:258-260/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:258-260/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:258-260/r5.claim: Abraham invokes life and death because inert nature cannot produce them, especially conscious, volitional animal life and its opposite, which are nonmaterial.
TABATABAI:2:258-260/r5.anchor: وخاصة التي في الحيوان حيث تستتبع الشعور والإرادة، وهما أمران غير ماديين قطعا

TABATABAI:2:258-260/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:258-260/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:258-260/r6.claim: Nimrod and his audience misunderstood the argument as figurative imprisonment and execution, revealing weak metaphysical understanding; this can coexist with the material achievements of Babylon, Chaldea, and Pharaonic Egypt.
TABATABAI:2:258-260/r6.anchor: فإن المدنية المادية أمر والتقدم في معنويات المعارف أمر آخر

TABATABAI:2:258-260#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:258-260#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:258-260#2/r1.claim: Al-Tabataba'i defines injustice as deviation from justice and proper action; it blocks guidance to the intended end and leads to failure and loss.
TABATABAI:2:258-260#2/r1.anchor: الظلم وهو الانحراف عن صراط العدل والعدول عما ينبغي من العمل إلى غير ما ينبغي موجب لعدم الاهتداء

TABATABAI:2:258-260#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:258-260#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:258-260#2/r2.claim: God guides every created thing toward its existential ends after creation, through its relations and interactions with other things.
TABATABAI:2:258-260#2/r2.anchor: كل شيء بعد تمام خلقه يهتدي بهداية من الله سبحانه إلى مقاصد وجوده وكمالات ذاته

TABATABAI:2:258-260#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:258-260#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:258-260#2/r3.claim: Natural processes do not misidentify their ends: fire does not seek to cool wood, and a growing plant tends toward increased size.
TABATABAI:2:258-260#2/r3.anchor: الأمور التكوينية لا تغلط في آثارها

TABATABAI:2:258-260#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:258-260#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:258-260#2/r4.claim: Because guidance is universal and creation does not err, each effect has its own real causal routes; ends are reached only by their specific causes and conditions.
TABATABAI:2:258-260#2/r4.anchor: أن يكون لكل شيء روابط حقيقية مع غيره

TABATABAI:2:258-260#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:258-260#3/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:258-260#3/r1.claim: Social institutions and actions also follow causal patterns rooted in nature: sound education comes from a sound educator, while a corrupt educator produces corruption despite outward propriety.
TABATABAI:2:258-260#3/r1.anchor: فالتربية الصالحة لا تتحقق إلا من مرب صالح

TABATABAI:2:258-260#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:258-260#3/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:258-260#3/r2.claim: Illegitimate rulers, judges, offices, and false acts may imitate truth temporarily, but their effects expose and destroy them; deception cannot permanently replace truth.
TABATABAI:2:258-260#3/r2.anchor: فكل ذلك سيظهر أثرها ويقطع دابرها وإن اشتبه أمرها أياما

TABATABAI:2:258-260#3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:258-260#3/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:258-260#3/r3.claim: Truth endures while falsehood cannot keep its effects, even when its harm or identity is temporarily obscured.
TABATABAI:2:258-260#3/r3.anchor: فالحق لا يموت ولا يتزلزل أثره

TABATABAI:2:259#2/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:259#2/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:259#2/r7.claim: The three stories show ranked modes of divine guidance: Abraham's debate demonstrates guidance to truth by proof, while his opponent is confounded by his wrongdoing.
TABATABAI:2:259#2/r7.anchor: أولها الهداية إلى الحق بالبرهان والاستدلال كما في قصة الذي حاج إبراهيم في ربه

TABATABAI:2:259-260/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:259-260/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:259-260/r1.claim: The three proofs can be framed as three successive examples, three types of guidance, or a command to recall each story; all fit the context.
TABATABAI:2:259-260/r1.anchor: يصح فيه جميع السياقات الثلاث في إلقاء المراد إلى المخاطب

TABATABAI:2:259-260/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:259-260/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:259-260/r2.claim: God varies the three rhetorical patterns across these verses to stimulate attention and realize all the contextual benefits available.
TABATABAI:2:259-260/r2.anchor: أخذ بالتفنن في البيان وخص كل واحدة من الآيات الثلاث بواحد من السياقات الثلاث تنشيطا لذهن المخاطب

THALABI:v2p239/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p239/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p239/r1.claim: The dispute is an argument from proof; Nimrod ibn Canaan is identified as a tyrant who claimed divinity, and God granting him kingship explains his arrogance.
THALABI:v2p239/r1.anchor: خاصم وجادل وأصلها من الحجة، وهو نمرود بن كنعان

THALABI:v2p239/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p239/r2.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v2p239/r2.claim: Mujahid says two believers ruled the earth—Solomon and Dhul-Qarnayn—and two disbelievers—Nimrod and Nebuchadnezzar.
THALABI:v2p239/r2.anchor: ملك الأرض مؤمنان وكافران، فأما المؤمنان فسليمان بن داود

THALABI:v2p239/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p239/r3.speaker: مقاتل
THALABI:v2p239/r3.claim: Muqatil dates the debate to after Abraham broke the idols, when Nimrod imprisoned him and prepared to burn him.
THALABI:v2p239/r3.anchor: لما كسر إبراهيم الأصنام سجنه نمرود ثم أخرجه ليحرقه

THALABI:v2p239/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p239/r4.speaker: آخرون
THALABI:v2p239/r4.claim: Other interpreters place the debate after Abraham had been thrown into the fire.
THALABI:v2p239/r4.anchor: آخرون: كان هذا بعد إلقائه في النار

THALABI:v2p239/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p239/r5.speaker: زيد بن أسلم عن معمر
THALABI:v2p239/r5.claim: A report says Nimrod controlled food distribution; when Abraham answered that God gives life and death, Nimrod sent him away without food, but God provided a fine meal from a sand dune he carried home.
THALABI:v2p239/r5.anchor: فرده بغير طعام فرجع إبراهيم عليه السلام إلى أهله

THALABI:v2p240/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p240/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p240/r1.claim: The continuation says Nimrod rejected an angel's repeated call to believe, challenged God to battle, and his army was destroyed by mosquitoes; one entered his brain and tormented him for four hundred years, matching his reign.
THALABI:v2p240/r1.anchor: فأوحى الله عز وجل إلى خزنة البعوض أن افتحوا منها

THALABI:v2p240/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p240/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p240/r2.claim: The verse's answer to Nimrod responds to an unstated prior question: who is Abraham's Lord?

THALABI:v2p240/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p240/r3.speaker: الأعمش وحمزة وعيسى
THALABI:v2p240/r3.claim: They read ربي with a quiescent ya; the other readers vocalize it with a fatha before the definite article.
THALABI:v2p240/r3.anchor: ربي الذي بإسكان الياء، وقرأ الباقون بفتحه

THALABI:v2p240/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p240/r4.speaker: أهل المدينة
THALABI:v2p240/r4.claim: Readers of Medina lengthen أنا throughout the Qur'an, treating connected speech like the original form; al-Kisai and another poet's verses attest the usage.
THALABI:v2p240/r4.anchor: أهل المدينة (أنا) بالمد في جميع القرآن

THALABI:v2p241/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p241/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p241/r1.claim: The original أنا has an open n; its written alif represents pause, and many Arabs pronounce it with a final h at pause.
THALABI:v2p241/r1.anchor: والأصل في (أنا) أن تفتح النون وابتغي لها الوقت

THALABI:v2p241/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p241/r2.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
THALABI:v2p241/r2.claim: Most commentators say Nimrod called sparing one man and killing another giving life and death, with the same sense as 5:32's phrase about not killing a person.
THALABI:v2p241/r2.anchor: دعا نمرود برجلين فقتل أحدهما واستحيا الآخر فسمى ترك القتل إحياء

THALABI:v2p241/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p241/r3.speaker: السدي
THALABI:v2p241/r3.claim: Al-Suddi says Nimrod starved four men, fed two near death, and let two die; Abraham then changed to the clearer proof of the sun rather than because he lacked a reply.
THALABI:v2p241/r3.anchor: أخذ أربعة نفر فأدخلهم بيتا فلا يطعمون ولا يسقون

THALABI:v2p241/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p241/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p241/r4.claim: Nimrod was bewildered, stunned, and cut off from argument.
THALABI:v2p241/r4.anchor: فبهت الذي كفر أي تحير ودهش وانقطعت حجته

THALABI:v2p241/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p241/r5.speaker: محمد بن السميقع اليماني
THALABI:v2p241/r5.claim: He reads فبهت with open b and h, meaning Abraham stunned Nimrod, supported by 21:97.
THALABI:v2p241/r5.anchor: محمد بن السميقع اليماني: فبهت بفتح الباء والهاء

THALABI:v2p241/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p241/r6.speaker: بعض نحاة البصرة
THALABI:v2p241/r6.claim: They attach أو كالذي to an implicit question about whether one has seen a case like the disputant or the traveler; some take the comparative kāf as extra.
THALABI:v2p241/r6.anchor: عطف على معنى الآية الأولى تقديره: هل رأيت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p371#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p371#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p371#2/r1.claim: ألم draws the listener's attention to an astonishing matter while taking the form of a question.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p371#2/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: {ألم تر إلى الذي حاج إبراهيم في ربه} الآية {ألم} كلمة يوقف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p371#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p371#2/r2.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p371#2/r2.claim: Arabic inserts إلى in this construction to express astonishment, as in “do you see this?”; it means have you seen someone like this, or seen such a case?

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p371#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p371#2/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p371#2/r3.claim: The إلى marks reaching an endpoint: has your sight reached someone of this sort? It highlights how extraordinary and unfamiliar the case is.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p371#2/r3.anchor: لما كانت نهاية صارت بمنزلة: هل انتهت رؤيتك إلى من هذه صفته

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p371#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p371#2/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p371#2/r4.claim: حاج means disputed or argued; the disputant is Nimrod son of Canaan.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p371#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p371#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس في رواية عطاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p371#2/r5.claim: Abraham entered Nimrod's town to obtain provisions; when Nimrod asked his lord, Abraham said the Lord gives life and death, and Nimrod claimed the same power.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p371#2/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس، في رواية عطاء

ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r1.claim: The episode shows what a believer, aided by God, can do when confronting a tyrant who claims divine power.
ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r1.anchor: Bakınız Allah’ın inâyetiyle bir mü’min bir tâgūta ne yapmış

ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r2.claim: Nemrud may have become arrogant at receiving sovereignty, or repaid its blessing perversely with disbelief.
ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r2.anchor: mağrur olarak -veya hükümdarlığının şükrânını ma‘kus bir surette küfran ile edâya kalkışarak-

ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r3.claim: A report says Nimrod imprisoned Abraham after he broke the idols, then later asked whom Abraham called people to worship.
ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r3.anchor: Rivayet olunduğuna göre Hazret-i İbrâhim putları kırdığı zaman Nemrud onu zindana atmış

ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r4.claim: Abraham's proof is that God creates life and death, meaning that He originates both life and its opposite.
ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r4.anchor: hem hayat halk eder, hem memat demekti

ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r5.claim: Nimrod claimed the same power by executing one man and sparing another, evading Abraham's proof and making a threatened claim to lordship.
ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r5.anchor: iki adam getirtmiş, birini idam edip birini salıvermiş, “İşte gördün mü?” demiş

ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r6.claim: Abraham answers with a fitting rhetorical shift: God brings the sun from the east, so Nimrod should bring it from the west.
ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r6.anchor: İbrâhim “şu muhakkak ki Allah [878] güneşi meşrıktan doğduruyor, sen de mağribden doğdur bakayım!” dedi

ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r7.claim: The disbeliever is left stunned and defeated; had he accepted truth instead of acting unjustly, he would not have fallen into darkness.
ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r7.anchor: kâfir tutuldu kaldı, mebhût ü mağlub oldu

ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r8.claim: Creating life is a greater proof of power than changing the sun's course, but unjust people trivialize it and claim its power for themselves.
ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r8.anchor: Hayat halk etmenin hareket-i şemsi tebdil etmekten daha mühim

ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r9.claim: Arrogant people may be defeated by a forceful sign and still refuse faith; the same pattern applies to communities as well as individuals.
ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r9.anchor: Ferdler böyle olduğu gibi cemaatler de böyledir

ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r10.claim: A taghut includes an unbeliever who claims to rival God by saying that he gives life and death; a believer should plainly correct him.
ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r10.anchor: tâgūtun misâllerinden biri böyle “ben ihyâ ederim ve öldürürüm” diye Allah ile rekabete kalkışan kâfirdir

ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r11.claim: Abraham's composure before Nimrod demonstrates God's favor: those without faith tremble before the tyrant, while Abraham overwhelms him.
ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r11.anchor: Allah’a imanı olmayanlar, bunun yanında korkusundan tiril tiril titrerken bak İbrâhim ona ne yapmış

ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r12.claim: A person can be king and remain unguided; sovereignty is a divine trust to govern by God's command and justice, not personal desire.
ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r12.anchor: kâfir, melik olabilir ve fakat bir kimse melik olmakla hidâyete ermiş olmaz

ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r13.claim: Life and death are manifest truths, yet people who treat them as ordinary may accept life's origin while denying resurrection because they miss recurring examples.
ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r13.anchor: asl-ı hayâtı tasdik ederken ba‘s ü neşri inkâr ederler

ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r14.claim: Those who place themselves above God's law and alter truth are destined to God's blow, dragging themselves and their subjects into ruin.
ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r14.anchor: teba‘alarıyla beraber kendilerini de zulümâta sürükler ve uçurumlardan yuvarlanır

ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r15.claim: Political sovereignty is a great divine blessing, but rulers possess it only as deputies rather than as its true owners.
ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r15.anchor: insanlar kendilerini bunun sâhib-i aslî ve hakīkīsi değil, sâhib-i niyâbî ve mecâzîsi bilmelidirler

ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r16.claim: Nimrod was deprived of guidance because he misunderstood delegated sovereignty, while Abraham prevailed through reliance on God.
ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r16.anchor: Nemrud bunu böyle tanımadığı için hidâyet-i ilâhiyeden mahrum zâlimlerden oldu

ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r17.claim: The concise debate conveys divine support for believers and their proper conduct toward tyrants with clarity and eloquence; the verse is clear proof.
ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r17.anchor: bu âyet, ıtlâkıyla muhkemâttan olan bir âyet-i beyyinedir

ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r18.claim: God's power to give life is not limited to one occurrence: He creates from nothing and can revive the dead in ordinary or extraordinary ways.
ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r18.anchor: Ma‘dûmu îcad edip hayat verdiği gibi meyyiti de tekrar ba‘s ile ihyâ edebilir

ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r19.claim: Life itself is miraculous, and God's bringing believers from darkness into light can exceed the limits of intellect and science without being impossible.
ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r19.anchor: Böyle olmakla beraber [880] bunlar akılların kabul edemeyeceği, reddine mecbur olacakları muhâlâttan değildirler

ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r20.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r20.claim: Some events seem inexplicable to unbelievers but become clear proofs to believers after they occur; God is about to give two such examples.
ELMALILI:2:257-260#3/r20.anchor: Cenâb-ı Allah bunları da iki misâl ile[^12] beyan edecektir

TABATABAI:6:74-83#23/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:74-83#23/r2.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:6:74-83#23/r2.claim: Some say Abraham’s people considered the sun male and assigned it a wife named Anunit; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī replies that this belief cannot change the feminine grammar for sun.
TABATABAI:6:74-83#23/r2.anchor: ومنهم من قال إن قوم إبراهيم عليه السلام كانوا يعدون الشمس من الذكور وقد أثبتوا لها زوجة

TABATABAI:6:74-83#23/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:74-83#23/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:74-83#23/r3.claim: A proposal that Abraham spoke ungendered Syriac is rejected: grammatical forms depend on the language, and other Qur’anic quotations of Abraham preserve feminine agreement for the sun.
TABATABAI:6:74-83#23/r3.anchor: على أنه تعالى حكى عن إبراهيم عليه السلام احتجاجات كثيرة وأدعية وافرة في القرآن وفيها موارد كثيرة اعتبر فيها التأنيث

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p314/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p314/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p314/r4.claim: Abraham shifted his argument with Nimrod from God's giving life and death to the sun's rising and setting, leaving the disbeliever confounded.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p314/r4.anchor: انتقل إلى الاحتجاج به خليل الله ، عن الاحتجاج بالإحياء والإماتة على نمروذ بن كنعان ، فبهت الذي كفر .

SAMIN-DURR:2:258/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:258/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:258/r1.claim: This opening was discussed at the parallel expression in 2:243; ʿAlī is reported to read تر with a still rāʾ, whose analysis was also given there.
SAMIN-DURR:2:258/r1.anchor: تقدم نظيره في قوله: ألم تر إلى الذين خرجوا

SAMIN-DURR:2:258/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:258/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:258/r2.claim: The pronoun in ربه most clearly refers to Abraham; another analysis refers it to the disputant.
SAMIN-DURR:2:258/r2.anchor: والهاء في " ربه " فيهما قولان، أظهرهما: أنها تعود على " إبراهيم "

SAMIN-DURR:2:258/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:258/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:258/r3.claim: حاجه means that he displayed rivalry in argument with Abraham, trying to prevail through his proof.
SAMIN-DURR:2:258/r3.anchor: ومعنى حاجه: أظهر المغالبة في حجته

SAMIN-DURR:2:258/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:258/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:258/r4.claim: The clearest parse makes أن آتاه a causal object with a deleted preposition, because God gave him kingship. It can then be accusative or genitive; the preposition is omitted because this cause clause lacks the same subject, a deletion allowed with لام before أن.
SAMIN-DURR:2:258/r4.anchor: أظهرهما: أنه مفعول من أجله على حذف حرف العلة، أي: لأن آتاه

SAMIN-DURR:2:258/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:258/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:258/r5.claim: One causal interpretation is ironic reversal: the man should have thanked God for kingship but instead made it an occasion for disputation, like the reversal in 56:82 and the example of opposing someone because he treated you well.
SAMIN-DURR:2:258/r5.anchor: أنه من باب العكس في الكلام بمعنى أنه وضع المحاجة موضع الشكر، إذ كان من حقه أن يشكر

SAMIN-DURR:2:258/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:258/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:258/r6.claim: The other causal interpretation is that receiving kingship made him arrogant and insolent, which led to his dispute with Abraham.
SAMIN-DURR:2:258/r6.anchor: والثاني: أن إيتاء الملك حمله على ذلك، لأنه أورثه الكبر والبطر، فتسبب عنهما المحاجة

SAMIN-DURR:2:258/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:258/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:2:258/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī instead lets أن and its clause function as a time expression: he disputed when God gave him kingship. The Shaykh questions this because the dispute was not simultaneous with the grant unless time is loose, and notes grammarians' objection to a clause replacing a temporal noun; he counters that maṣdariyya ما can do so.
SAMIN-DURR:2:258/r7.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " ويجوز أن يكون التقدير: حاج وقت أن آتاه "

SAMIN-DURR:2:258#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:258#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:258#2/r1.claim: The pronoun in آتاه most clearly refers to the disputant; al-Mahdawī allows Abraham as referent, taking the gift as the kingship of prophecy. Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls that interpretation forced.
SAMIN-DURR:2:258#2/r1.anchor: والضمير في " آتاه " فيه وجهان، أحدهما - وهو الأظهر - أن يعود على " الذي "

SAMIN-DURR:2:258#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:258#2/r2.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:2:258#2/r2.claim: The Shaykh identifies the Abraham-as-recipient reading as Muʿtazilite: kingship is a divine covenant that wrongdoers cannot receive (2:124), while 4:54 says Abraham's family received scripture, wisdom, and great kingship.
SAMIN-DURR:2:258#2/r2.anchor: وقال الشيخ: " هذا قول المعتزلة، قالوا: لأن الله تعالى

SAMIN-DURR:2:258#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:258#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:258#2/r3.claim: The clearest governor of إذ قال is حاج: he disputed when Abraham said this.
SAMIN-DURR:2:258#2/r3.anchor: قوله: { إذ قال } فيه أربعة أوجه، أظهرها: أنه معمول لحاج

SAMIN-DURR:2:258#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:258#2/r4.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:2:258#2/r4.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ makes إذ depend on آتاه; the author questions this because granting kingship was not the time Abraham made his statement, except by loose extension of the time phrase.
SAMIN-DURR:2:258#2/r4.anchor: ذكره أبو البقاء. وفيه نظر من حيث إن وقت إيتاء الملك ليس وقت قول إبراهيم

SAMIN-DURR:2:258#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:258#2/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:2:258#2/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī allows إذ as appositive to أن آتاه if that clause means at the time; the author considers this weak because the time expressions differ unless construed loosely. Abū al-Baqāʾ rejects apposition if أن is causal, unless إذ itself means the verbal noun أن, an attested usage.
SAMIN-DURR:2:258#2/r5.anchor: أجازه الزمخشري بناء منه على أن " أن " واقعة موقع الظرف

SAMIN-DURR:2:258#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:258#2/r6.speaker: مكي
SAMIN-DURR:2:258#2/r6.claim: Makkī makes إذ depend on تر, but the author rejects this: seeing, on either interpretation of the parallel expression, did not occur when Abraham said this.
SAMIN-DURR:2:258#2/r6.anchor: ذكره مكي، وهذا ليس بشيء، لأن الرؤية على كلا التفسيرين المذكورين

SAMIN-DURR:2:258#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:258#2/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:258#2/r7.claim: ربي is a subject with a relative-clause predicate, and the whole clause is governed in the accusative by قال; أنا أحيي is likewise a subject-predicate clause governed by قال.
SAMIN-DURR:2:258#2/r7.anchor: مبتدأ وخبر في محل نصب بالقول

SAMIN-DURR:2:258#2/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:258#2/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:258#2/r8.claim: Abraham states God's power through a relative clause, which implies exclusivity; the disputant's finite clause does not. He did not claim unique possession of that lowly power for himself.
SAMIN-DURR:2:258#2/r8.anchor: وأخبر عن " أنا " بالجملة الفعلية، وعن " ربي " بالموصول بها، لأنه في الإخبار بالموصول يفيد الاختصاص

SAMIN-DURR:2:258#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:258#3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:258#3/r1.claim: أنا is a separate nominative pronoun; its underlying form is أن, with added alif to mark the vowel at pause and ordinarily deleted in connected speech. Some retain it throughout, explained either by extending pause pronunciation into liaison or by dialect.
SAMIN-DURR:2:258#3/r1.anchor: و " أنا " ضمير مرفوع منفصل، والاسم منه " أن "

SAMIN-DURR:2:258#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:258#3/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:258#3/r2.claim: The sound account recognizes two dialects: Tamīm retains alif in both pause and liaison, which explains Nāfiʿ's reading before hamza with ḍamma or fatḥa and his differing report before kasra, and Ibn ʿĀmir's form noted later. The other dialect retains alif only at pause; liaison retention is poetic necessity.
SAMIN-DURR:2:258#3/r2.anchor: والصحيح أنه فيه لغتان، إحداهما: لغة تميم، وهي إثبات ألفه وصلا ووقفا

SAMIN-DURR:2:258#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:258#3/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:258#3/r3.claim: Other forms are أنا, أن, and آن; one account explains آن by moving alif before nūn and associates it with time. In أنه, the hāʾ is pause hāʾ rather than a substitute for alif, as cited poetry illustrates.
SAMIN-DURR:2:258#3/r3.anchor: وفيه لغات: أنا وأن - كلفظ أن الناصبة - وآن، وكأنه قدم الألف على النون

SAMIN-DURR:2:258#3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:258#3/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:258#3/r4.claim: Nāfiʿ retains alif before hamza either by combining the two dialects or because hamza is difficult to pronounce and the long vowel eases it.
SAMIN-DURR:2:258#3/r4.anchor: وإنما أثبت نافع ألفه قبل الهمز جمعا بين اللغتين، أو لأن النطق بالهمز عسر

SAMIN-DURR:2:258#4/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:258#4/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:258#4/r1.claim: The fāʾ answers an omitted condition: Abraham effectively says if you claim or pretend that, then God... Without the omitted condition, a quotation after قال would have no fāʾ and would read قال إبراهيم إن الله يأتي.
SAMIN-DURR:2:258#4/r1.anchor: هذه الفاء جواب شرط مقدر تقديره: قال إبراهيم إن زعمت أو موهت بذلك

SAMIN-DURR:2:258#4/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:258#4/r2.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:2:258#4/r2.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ says the fāʾ connects the statement to what preceded: if the opponent claims life and death without understanding, the proof is that God brings the sun.
SAMIN-DURR:2:258#4/r2.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء: " دخلت الفاء إيذانا بتعلق هذا الكلام بما قبله، والمعنى إذا أدعيت

SAMIN-DURR:2:258#4/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:258#4/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:258#4/r3.claim: The bāʾ in بالشمس makes the verb transitive: أتت الشمس means the sun came, while أتى الله بها means He brought it; من المشرق and من المغرب modify their respective verbs.
SAMIN-DURR:2:258#4/r3.anchor: والباء في " بالشمس " للتعدية، تقول: أتت الشمس

SAMIN-DURR:2:258#4/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:258#4/r4.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:2:258#4/r4.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ also allows the directional phrases as circumstances meaning subjugated or compliant, after previously denying that analysis; the author wishes he had maintained his initial rejection.
SAMIN-DURR:2:258#4/r4.anchor: وأجاز أبو البقاء فيهما بعد أن منع ذلك أن يكونا حالين

SAMIN-DURR:2:258#4/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:258#4/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:258#4/r5.claim: The majority read بهت passively: الذي is raised as the passive subject, with Abraham as the understood agent; alternatively, the original agent may be the speech implied by قال.
SAMIN-DURR:2:258#4/r5.anchor: الجمهور: " بهت " مبنيا للمفعول، والموصول مرفوع به

SAMIN-DURR:2:258#4/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:258#4/r6.speaker: ابن السميفع
SAMIN-DURR:2:258#4/r6.claim: Ibn al-Sumayfiʿ reads بهت with fatḥa on both consonants as active: Abraham may be subject and the disbeliever object, meaning Abraham defeated him in argument; alternatively the disbeliever is subject and Abraham an omitted object as the disbeliever resorted to slander when silenced.
SAMIN-DURR:2:258#4/r6.anchor: وقرأ ابن السميفع: " فبهت " بفتح الباء والهاء مبنيا للفاعل

SAMIN-DURR:2:258#4/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:258#4/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:258#4/r7.claim: On Ibn al-Sumayfiʿ's active reading, an intransitive parse takes الذي as subject, matching the passive reading's meaning of bewilderment; it can also mean to produce a falsehood.
SAMIN-DURR:2:258#4/r7.anchor: والثاني: أن يكون لازما والموصول فاعل، والمعنى معنى بهت

SAMIN-DURR:2:258#4/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:258#4/r8.speaker: أبو حيوة
SAMIN-DURR:2:258#4/r8.claim: Abū Ḥaywa reads fatḥa on bāʾ and ḍamma on hāʾ with the relative pronoun as subject; al-Akhfash reports a kasra on hāʾ, also intransitive. The author summarizes three forms: both fatḥa, ḍamma, and kasra; the fatḥa form can be transitive or intransitive.
SAMIN-DURR:2:258#4/r8.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة: " فبهت " بفتح الباء وضم الهاء كظرف

SAMIN-DURR:2:258#4/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:258#4/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:258#4/r9.claim: بهت means bewilderment and astonishment; bāhata or bahtahu can mean confronting someone with a lie. The cited saying calls the Jews people of falsehood because lies bewilder the person lied to.
SAMIN-DURR:2:258#4/r9.anchor: والبهت: التحير والدهش، وباهته وبهته واجهه بالكذب

SAMIN-DURR:2:258#5/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:258#5/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:258#5/r1.claim: A lie confounds the person against whom it is directed, explaining the use of بهت for bewilderment.
SAMIN-DURR:2:258#5/r1.anchor: وذلك أن الكذب يحير المكذوب عليه

ZAJJAJ:v1p340/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p340/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p340/r1.claim: Alam tara is interrogative in form but draws the listener's attention to an astonishing matter, as in ordinary speech about someone's remarkable deed.
ZAJJAJ:v1p340/r1.anchor: هذه كلمة يوقف بها المخاطب على أمر يعجب منه، ولفظها لفظ استفهام، تقول في الكلام: ألم تر إلى فلان صنع كذا وصنع كذا.

ZAJJAJ:v1p340/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p340/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p340/r2.claim: This account is evidence against the People of the Book and Arab polytheists: Muhammad could know it only through scripture, a teacher, or revelation.
ZAJJAJ:v1p340/r2.anchor: وهذا مما أعلمه النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - حجة على أهل الكتاب ومشركي العرب لأنه نبأ لا يجوز أن يعلمه إلا من وقف عليه بقراءة كتاب أو تعليم معلم، أو بوحي من الله عز وجل.

ZAJJAJ:v1p340/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p340/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p340/r3.claim: The Arabs knew Muhammad was unlettered and had not learned the Torah, Gospel, or earlier prophets' accounts, leaving revelation as the only source.
ZAJJAJ:v1p340/r3.anchor: فقد علمت العرب الذين نشأ بينهم رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - أنه أمي، وأنه لم يعلم التوراة والإنجيل وأخبار من مضى من الأنبياء، فلم يبق وجه تعلم منه هذه الأحاديث إلا الوحي.

ZAJJAJ:v1p340#2/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p340#2/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p340#2/r1.claim: The king who disputed with Abraham was the disbeliever whom God gave kingship; this is the exegetes' established view and best fits the passage.
ZAJJAJ:v1p340#2/r1.anchor: أي آتى الكافر الملك، وهذا هو الذي عليه أهل التفسير وعليه يصح المعنى

ZAJJAJ:v1p340#2/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p340#2/r2.speaker: قوم
ZAJJAJ:v1p340#2/r2.claim: Some instead say God gave kingship to Abraham, arguing that God does not grant kingship to disbelievers.
ZAJJAJ:v1p340#2/r2.anchor: وقال قوم إن الذي آتاه - الله الملك إبراهيم عليه السلام وقالوا: الله عز وجل لا يملك الكفار.

ZAJJAJ:v1p340#2/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p340#2/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p340#2/r3.claim: That a disbeliever received kingship accords with God's statement that He grants and removes kingship, honors and humbles whom He wills.
ZAJJAJ:v1p340#2/r3.anchor: والله قال: (تؤتي الملك من تشاء وتنزع الملك ممن تشاء وتعز من تشاء وتذل من تشاء).

ZAJJAJ:v1p340#2/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p340#2/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p340#2/r4.claim: Giving a disbeliever kingship is one of God's tests of His creatures; God knows its wisdom.
ZAJJAJ:v1p340#2/r4.anchor: فتأويل إيتاء الله الكافر الملك ضرب من امتحانه الذي يمتحن الله به خلقه، وهو أعلم بوجه الحكمة فيه.

ZAJJAJ:v1p340#2/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p340#2/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p340#2/r5.claim: The opponent was king: he claimed to give life and death and demonstrated power by summoning two men, killing one and releasing another, while Abraham was a prophet rather than a king.
ZAJJAJ:v1p340#2/r5.anchor: والدليل على أن الكافر هو الذي كان ملك إنه قال: (أنا أحيي وأميت) وأنه دعا برجلين فقتل أحدهما وأطلق الآخر

ZAJJAJ:v1p340#2/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p340#2/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p340#2/r6.claim: Abraham's silence about the life-and-death claim is a concise way to defeat his opponent: the sunrise challenge would expose the man's inability and silence him.
ZAJJAJ:v1p340#2/r6.anchor: فمن أبلغ ما يقطع به الخصوم ترك الإطالة والاحتجاج بالحجة المسكتة لأن إبراهيم لما قال له: (فإن الله يأتي بالشمس من المشرق فأت بها من المغرب)

ZAJJAJ:v1p340#2/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p340#2/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p340#2/r7.claim: Bahita means he was struck dumb and perplexed; bahatta-hu can also mean to confront someone with a lie.
ZAJJAJ:v1p340#2/r7.anchor: وتأويله انقطع وسكت متحيرا، يقال: بهت الرجل يبهت بهتا إذا انقطع وتحير، ويقال بهذا المعنى " بهت الرجل ييهت "، ويقال بهت الرجل أبهته بهتانا إذا قابلته بكذب.

ASAD-NOTES:2:258#n251/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:258#n251/r1.speaker: Muhammad 'Abduh
ASAD-NOTES:2:258#n251/r1.claim: Muhammad Abduh explains the wrong as deliberately turning away from the light of God’s guidance.
ASAD-NOTES:2:258#n251/r1.anchor: According to Muhammad 'Abduh, the wrong (zulm) referred to here consists in "one's deliberately turning away

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p358/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p358/r3.speaker: نافع، ورش، أبو بكر بن أبي أويس، قالون
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p358/r3.claim: All drop the alif in connected speech except these Nāfiʿ transmissions, which retain it before hamza; they drop it at 26:15 and generally before non-hamza.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p358/r3.anchor: غير نافع، فإن ورشا وأبا بكر بن أبي أويس وقالون رووا: إثباتها في الوصل إذا لقيتها همزة

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p358/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p358/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p358/r4.claim: Anā’s alif is a pause marker, like a pause hāʾ or hamzat al-waṣl, and drops in connected speech because the following word enables pronunciation.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p358/r4.anchor: القول في أنا أنه ضمير المتكلم، والاسم: الهمزة والنون

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p134/r1.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p134/r1.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p134/r1.claim: The fragment relates حانية to حانية on the فاعلة pattern, while حانة is shortened from it, like بالة from بالية; al-Kisāʾī similarly derives آية from آيية.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p134/r1.anchor: فأما الحانة فمحذوفة من الحانية، ومثالها فاعة، ومثلها البالة من قولهم: ما باليت

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p134/r2.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p134/r2.speaker: ابن السميفع ونعيم بن ميسرة وأبو حيوة
