IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p134/r2.claim: Ibn al-Sumayfa and Nuʿaym read فَبَهَتَ with fatḥa throughout; Abū Ḥaywa has fatḥa on bāʾ, ḍamma on hāʾ, and the mainstream form is فَبُهِتَ. Al-Akhfash adds an unattributed fourth form on faʿila.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p134/r2.anchor: ومن ذلك قراءة ابن السميفع2: "فبهت الذي كفر"3 بفتح الباء والهاء والتاء،

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p134/r3.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p134/r3.speaker: الأخفش
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p134/r3.claim: Al-Akhfash also reports an unattributed reading فَبَهِتَ on the pattern of عَلِمَ, bringing the total to four readings.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p134/r3.anchor: زاد أبو الحسن الأخفش قراءة أخرى لا يحضرني الآن ذكر قارئها،

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p134/r4.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p134/r4.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p134/r4.claim: The faʿula reading is stronger: this form can intensify a quality, as in قضو الرجل and فقه, and means reaching an extreme of bewilderment and confusion.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p134/r4.anchor: وذلك أن فعل تأتي للمبالغة كقولهم: قضو الرجل إذا جاد قضاؤه، وفقه إذا قوي في فقهه،

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p134/r5.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p134/r5.speaker: أحمد بن يحيى
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p134/r5.claim: A report from Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā says Arabs use ضربت اليد when the hand strikes forcefully, illustrating the intensive reading.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p134/r5.anchor: وروينا عن أبي بكر محمد بن الحسن عن أحمد بن يحيى: أن العرب تقول:

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p134/r6.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p134/r6.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p134/r6.claim: The reading may be intransitive like ذهل and نكل, or transitive with an omitted object, meaning the disbeliever confounded Abraham; in the latter account he tried but failed, and Abraham prevailed.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p134/r6.anchor: وقد يمكن أن يكون متعديا ويكون مفعوله محذوفا؛ أي: فبهت الذي كفر إبراهيم عليه السلام.

NASHR:v2p192/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p192/r1.speaker: قنبل
NASHR:v2p192/r1.claim: For the yāʾ reading under discussion, Qunbul has two soundly transmitted and performed forms at pause; the author recited and adopts both.
NASHR:v2p192/r1.anchor: (قلت) : وكلا الوجهين صحيح عن قنبل نصا وأداء حالة الوقف بهما قرأت

NASHR:v2p192/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p192/r4.speaker: القراء
NASHR:v2p192/r4.claim: The codices consistently write yāʾ in fifteen listed places, and the readers likewise agree to retain it; the list includes فإن الله يأتي بالشمس in al-Baqara.
NASHR:v2p192/r4.anchor: أجمعت المصاحف على إثبات الياء رسما في خمسة عشر موضعا مما وقع نظيره محذوفا مختلفا فيه

NASHR:v1p35/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p35/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p35/r1.claim: The author notes an unnamed scholar's Jamiʿ al-bayan on the seven readings contains over 500 transmissions and routes; the excerpt gives his death year as 444 AH.
NASHR:v1p35/r1.anchor: وغير ذلك توفي سنة أربع وأربعين وأربعمائة، وهذا كتاب جامع البيان له في قراءات السبعة فيه عنهم أكثر من خمسمائة رواية وطريق

NASHR:v1p35/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p35/r2.speaker: أبو القاسم يوسف بن علي بن جبارة الهذلي
NASHR:v1p35/r2.claim: Al-Hudhali traveled widely, collected fifty readings and 1,459 transmissions/routes in al-Kamil, met 365 teachers from the Maghrib to Farghana, and died in 465 AH.
NASHR:v1p35/r2.anchor: وألف كتابه الكامل جمع فيه خمسين قراءة عن الأئمة وألفا وأربعمائة وتسعة وخمسين رواية وطريقا

NASHR:v1p35/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p35/r3.speaker: أبو معشر عبد الكريم بن عبد الصمد الطبري
NASHR:v1p35/r3.claim: Al-Tabari of Mecca authored al-Talkhis on eight readings and Suq al-Arus with 1,550 transmissions/routes; he died in 478 AH.
NASHR:v1p35/r3.anchor: مؤلف كتاب التلخيص في القراءات الثمان وسوق العروس فيه ألف وخمسمائة وخمسون رواية وطريقا

NASHR:v1p35/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p35/r4.speaker: أبو القاسم عيسى بن عبد العزيز الإسكندري
NASHR:v1p35/r4.claim: The author knows no later compiler exceeding al-Hudhali and al-Tabari except al-Iskandari, whose al-Jamiʿ al-Akbar wa al-Bahr al-Azkhar contains 7,000 routes; he died in 629 AH.
NASHR:v1p35/r4.anchor: لا نعلم أحدا بعدهما جمع أكثر منهما إلا أبا القاسم عيسى بن عبد العزيز الإسكندري، فإنه ألف كتابا سماه الجامع الأكبر والبحر الأزخر

NASHR:v1p35/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p35/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p35/r5.claim: Qiraat authors preserve rare and sound readings as transmitted; this follows the predecessors' principle that recitation is a transmitted Sunnah, with each generation receiving it from the one before.
NASHR:v1p35/r5.anchor: ولا ينكر أحد عليهم، بل هم في ذلك متبعون سبيل السلف حيث قالوا: القراءة سنة متبعة يأخذها الآخر عن الأول

NASHR:v1p35/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p35/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p35/r6.claim: The only criticized exceptions were Ibn Shunbudh for departing from the Uthmani codex and Ibn Miqsam for permitting any reading matching the codex without transmitted authority.
NASHR:v1p35/r6.anchor: إلا ما قدمنا عن ابن شنبوذ، لكنه خرج عن المصحف العثماني، وللناس في ذلك خلاف كما قدمناه

QIRAAT-ER:2:258:6#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:2:258:6#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:2:258:6#1/r1.claim: The long ā variant in Ibrāhām replaces ī in the penultimate syllable, reflecting dialectal variation in Arabizing the Hebrew name; both readings are canonical.
QIRAAT-ER:2:258:6#1/r1.anchor: Long-vowel variant — ā instead of ī in penultimate syllable. Reflects dialectal variation

QIRAAT-ER:2:258:15#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:2:258:15#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:2:258:15#1/r1.claim: This instance likewise has the long ā variant instead of ī, consistently reflecting the same dialectal reading.
QIRAAT-ER:2:258:15#1/r1.anchor: Long-vowel variant ā replacing ī — identical to word 6 variant

QIRAAT-ER:2:258:16#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:2:258:16#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:2:258:16#1/r1.claim: A quiescent yāʾ gives rabbī, while open yāʾ gives rabbiya; the fatḥa form makes the declaration more emphatic.
QIRAAT-ER:2:258:16#1/r1.anchor: Quiescent yāʾ vs. open yāʾ — rabbī (possessive with sukūn) vs. rabbiya

QIRAAT-ER:2:258:22#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:2:258:22#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:2:258:22#1/r1.claim: A lengthened final alif in anā is a dialectal pronunciation variant of the pronoun, without a stated semantic difference.
QIRAAT-ER:2:258:22#1/r1.anchor: Extended vowel (madd) on final alif — lengthened pronunciation

QIRAAT-ER:2:258:27#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:2:258:27#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:2:258:27#1/r1.claim: The third Ibrāhīm instance receives the same long-vowel variant as the earlier two occurrences.
QIRAAT-ER:2:258:27#1/r1.anchor: Long-vowel variant — consistent with words 6 and 15. All three Ibrahim instances receive the same variant

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p103/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p103/r1.speaker: الكلبي وقتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p103/r1.claim: Al-Kalbi and Qatada identify the disputant as Nimrod, a tyrant whom they call the first to become tyrannical on earth.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p103/r1.anchor: عن الكلبي وقتادة في قوله ﴿ ألم تر إلى الذي حاج إبراهيم في ربه ﴾ قالا هو جبار اسمه نمرود وهو أول من تجبر في الأرض

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p103/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p103/r2.speaker: الجبار
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p103/r2.claim: The tyrant Nimrod explains his claim to give life and death as the claim that he can kill whomever he chooses or spare whomever he chooses.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p103/r2.anchor: فقال ذلك الجبار فأنا أحيي وأميت يقول أنا أقتل من شئت وأحيي من شئت

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p103/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p103/r3.speaker: وهب بن منبه
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p103/r3.claim: Wahb reports that David killed Goliath with a sling; after Saul reneged on a promised marriage, he demanded 300 enemy foreskins as a bride-price, which David delivered and then married Saul’s daughter.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p103/r3.anchor: قال نا بكار بن عبد الله قال سمعت وهب بن منبه يحدث قال لما خرج أو قال برز طالوت لجالوت

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p103/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p103/r4.speaker: وهب بن منبه
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p103/r4.claim: Wahb says Saul later pursued David, who could have killed him but instead took his drinking vessel, beard hairs, and clothing fringe to prove he had spared him; Saul let him go, though later plotting against him again.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p103/r4.anchor: قال نا بكار بن عبد الله قال سمعت وهب بن منبه يحدث قال لما خرج أو قال برز طالوت لجالوت

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p103/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p103/r5.speaker: وهب بن منبه
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p103/r5.claim: Wahb says Saul received no revelation and was not a prophet; a prophet named Samuel received revelation and appointed him king.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p103/r5.anchor: قال بكار وسئل وهب وأنا أسمع أنبيا كان طالوت يوحى إليه فقال لا لم يأته وحي ولكن كان معه نبي يوحى إليه

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p105/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p105/r1.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p105/r1.claim: Zayd b. Aslam reports that Nimrod, the first tyrant, denied Abraham food; God provided for Abraham, then destroyed Nimrod’s army with gnats and tormented him with one for 400 years. Nimrod’s sky-reaching tower was destroyed at its foundations.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p105/r1.anchor: عن زيد بن أسلم أن أول جبار كان في الأرض نمرود قال وكان الناس يخرجون يمتارون من عنده الطعام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p623/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p623/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p623/r12.claim: The debate follows the statement that God is protector of believers while the disbelievers’ protectors are false gods: Abraham defeats the opponent as God’s ally, while the opponent is confounded as a false-god ally; the story exemplifies the believers and disbelievers just described.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p623/r12.anchor: لما أخبر أنه ولي الذين آمنوا، وأخبر: أن الكفار أولياؤهم الطاغوت، ذكر هذه القصة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p623/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p623/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p623/r13.claim: The account illustrates that God’s party prevails and prospers, echoing the Qurʾānic declarations about the party of God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p623/r13.anchor: ألا فإن حزب الله هم الغالبون ألا إن حزب الله هم المفلحون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p623/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p623/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p623/r14.claim: He does not repeat the earlier discussion of the wording alam tara ilā alladhīna, since it has already been covered.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p623/r14.anchor: وتقدم الكلام على قوله: ألم تر إلى الذين فأغنى عن إعادته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p627/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p627/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p627/r1.claim: In rabbī alladhī yuḥyī wa-yumīt, rabbī is the subject and the relative clause is its predicate.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p627/r1.anchor: وربي الذي يحيي ويميت، مبتدأ وخبر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p627/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p627/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p627/r2.claim: God created the disbeliever and controls his life and death, powers neither he nor his peers can exercise; the wording also points to creation and resurrection.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p627/r2.anchor: هو الذي أوجد الكافر ويحييه ويميته، كأنه قال: ربي الذي يحيي ويميت هو متصرف فيك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p627/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p627/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p627/r3.claim: The relative predicate implies exclusivity: saying God is the one who does this marks Him as uniquely possessing the act.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p627/r3.anchor: وفي قوله: الذي يحيي ويميت دليل على الاختصاص لأنهم قد ذكروا أن الخبر، إذا كان بمثل هذا، دل على الاختصاص

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p627/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p627/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p627/r4.claim: The disbeliever counters Abraham’s claim of exclusive life-giving and death-dealing by asserting that he shares in those acts; he avoids saying ana alladhī because that would falsely assert exclusivity and contradict observable human lives and deaths.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p627/r4.anchor: ولم يقل: أنا الذي يحيي ويميت، لأنه كان يدل على الاختصاص، وكان الحس يكذبه إذ قد حيي ناس قبل وجوده

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p627/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p627/r5.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p627/r5.claim: One explanation says the ruler brought two men, killed one, and released the other, calling this killing and sparing life his power to kill and revive.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p627/r5.anchor: قيل: أحضر رجلين، قتل أحدهما وأرسل الآخر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p627/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p627/r6.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p627/r6.claim: A second explanation says he kept four people hungry, fed two so they lived, and left two until they died.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p627/r6.anchor: وقيل: أدخل أربعة نفر بيتا حتى جاعوا، فأطعم اثنين فحييا، وترك اثنين فماتا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p627/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p627/r7.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p627/r7.claim: A third explanation takes his alleged life-giving as intercourse and the depositing of sperm, and his death-dealing as killing.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p627/r7.anchor: وقيل: أحيا بالمباشرة وإلقاء النطفة، وأمات بالقتل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p627/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p627/r8.speaker: نافع
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p627/r8.claim: Nāfiʿ retains the alif of ana before an open or implicit hamza; Abū Nasīṭ reports it retained before a kasra hamza. The other readers omit it, while all retain it at pause.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p627/r8.anchor: وقرأ نافع بإثبات ألف: أنا إذا كان بعدها همزة مفتوحة أو مضمرة. وروى أبو نسيط إثباتها مع الهمزة المكسورة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p627/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p627/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p627/r9.claim: The connected alif in Nāfiʿ’s reading is best understood as the language of Banū Tamīm, who retain it both in connection and at pause.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p627/r9.anchor: والأحسن أن تجعل قراءة نافع على لغة بني تميم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p627/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p627/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p627/r10.claim: He rejects the explanation as pause pronunciation carried into connected speech, calling it very weak and unsuitable for Qurʾānic recitation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p627/r10.anchor: وليس هذا مما يحسن الأخذ به في القرآن. انتهى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p627/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p627/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p627/r11.claim: Outside Banū Tamīm, retaining the alif in connected speech occurs only by poetic necessity, as in the cited line.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p627/r11.anchor: ولا تثبت عند غير بني تميم وصلا إلا في ضرورة الشعر نحو قوله: فكيف أنا وانتحالي القوافي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p627/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p627/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p627/r12.claim: Seeing the opponent’s weak understanding or sophistry in matching Abraham’s words rather than their meaning, Abraham gives an unanswerable challenge about the sun’s direction.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p627/r12.anchor: لما خيل الكافر أنه مشارك لرب إبراهيم في الوصف الذي ذكره إبراهيم، ورأى إبراهيم من معارضته ما يدل على ضعف فهمه أو مغالطته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p627/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p627/r13.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p627/r13.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī reads the sun challenge as a move from one proof to another after the foolish reply, choosing a proof the opponent cannot answer; he says this shows that changing arguments is permitted.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p627/r13.anchor: وإلى القول الأول ذهب الزمخشري. قال: وكان الاعتراض عتيدا، ولكن إبراهيم لما سمع جوابه الأحمق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p627/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p627/r14.speaker: المفسرون
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p627/r14.claim: Exegetes differ over whether Abraham changes from one proof to another, or keeps one proof but replaces its example with a clearer one; no preference is stated here.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p627/r14.anchor: واختلف المفسرون هل ذلك انتقال من دليل إلى دليل؟ أو هو دليل واحد والانتقال فيه من مثال إلى مثال أوضح منه

ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r1.claim: The verse illustrates God’s guidance and support for believers and His abandonment of others; Al-Ālūsī says it is therefore not coordinated with the preceding statement.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r1.anchor: بيان لتسديد المؤمنين إذ كان وليهم وخذلان غيرهم ولذا لم يعطف

ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r2.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r2.claim: An alternative takes the story as evidence for the preceding claim that unbelievers’ allies are the Taghut, while the following passage supports God’s guardianship of believers.

ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r3.claim: The story comes first to pair it with its referent, to foreground its striking independent interest, and to avoid dispersing the later, more detailed sequence.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r3.anchor: وبدأ به لرعاية الاقتران بينه وبين مدلوله ولإستقلاله بأمر عجيب

ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r4.claim: Abraham’s call to truth and defeat of the unbeliever’s argument also show God guiding believers through His guardianship.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r4.anchor: فإن ما يحكى عنه من الدعوة إلى الحق وإدحاض حجة الكافرين من آثار ولايته

ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r5.claim: The interrogative hamza denies the apparent negation and affirms the denied proposition; the audience is asked to marvel at a story whose fame makes it virtually undeniable.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r5.anchor: وهمزة الإستفهام لإنكار النفي وتقرير المنفي والجمهور على أن في الكلام معنى التعجب

ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r6.claim: The address means, “Have you seen or heard of this unbeliever?” His extraordinary challenge should reassure the Prophet: God aided Abraham and defeated the chief of the tyrants.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r6.anchor: فلتكن في الغاية القصوى من تحقق ما ذكرته لك من ولايتي للمؤمنين وعدمها للكافرين ولتطب نفسك

ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r7.claim: The person who disputed with Abraham was Nimrod son of Canaan son of Senjarib, described as the first tyrant to claim divinity.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r7.anchor: والمراد بالموصول نمروذ بن كنعان بن سنجاريب وهو أول من تجبر وإدعى الربوبية

ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r8.claim: The text calls the encounter a disputation even though Nimrod argued falsely, because his false argument was presented as if it were a real proof.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r8.anchor: وإنما أطلق على ما وقع لفظ المحاجة وإن كانت مجادلة بالباطل لإيرادها موردها

ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r9.speaker: مقاتل
ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r9.claim: One report places the dispute after Abraham broke the idols and before Nimrod cast him into the fire.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r9.anchor: قبل إلقائه في النار وهو المروي عن مقاتل

ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r10.speaker: جعفر الصادق
ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r10.claim: A report from Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq places the dispute after Abraham was cast into the fire and it became cool and safe for him.

ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r11.claim: Calling God Abraham’s Lord honors Abraham and signals from the outset that God, as his guardian, will support him in the dispute.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r11.anchor: وفي التعرض لعنوان الربوبية مع الإضافة إلى ضميره عليه الصلاة والسلام تشريف له وإيذان من أول الأمر بتأييد وليه

ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r12.claim: The clause means “because God granted him kingship,” with an omitted causal lām; it is not an object of purpose because the agents differ.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r12.anchor: أي لأن آتاه الله تعالى ذلك فالكلام على حذف اللام وهو مطرد في أن وإن وليس هناك مفعول لأجله

ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r13.claim: On one causal reading, God’s grant of kingship caused Nimrod’s arrogance and insolence, which led him to dispute.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r13.anchor: إما أن إيتاء الملك حمله على ذلك لأنه أورثه الكبر والبطر فنشأت المحاجة عنهما

ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r14.claim: A second causal reading is ironic: Nimrod disputed despite having reason to thank God for the kingship He had granted.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r14.anchor: وإما أنه من باب العكس في الكلام بمعنى أنه وضع المحاجة وضع الشكر إذ كان من حقه أن يشكر على ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r15.claim: Another parsing treats “gave him” as temporal, with or without an implied noun: Nimrod disputed when God granted him kingship.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r15.anchor: واقعا موقع الظرف بدون تقدير أو بتقدير مضاف

ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r16.claim: Critics object that the grant preceded the dispute and that a temporal adverb normally requires an explicit verbal noun; defenders invoke an extended period and the temporal use of مصدرية ما.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r16.anchor: وأورد عليه أن المحاجة لم تقع وقت إيتاء الملك بل الإيتاء سابق عليها وبأن النحاة نصوا

ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r17.claim: Al-Ālūsī prefers the causal construction because it is agreed and avoids the strained temporal analyses and disputed grammatical exceptions.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r17.anchor: والحق أن التعليل لما أمكن وهو متفق عليه خال عما يقال لا ينبغي أن يعدل عنه

ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r18.claim: The verse supports that God can grant kingship to an unbeliever; restricting the grant to wealth, servants, and followers, or calling it a test, does not remove the theological problem.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r18.anchor: والآية حجة على من منع إيتاء الله الملك لكافر وحملها على إيتاء الله تعالى ما غلب به وتسلط

ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r19.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r19.claim: Some avoid attributing kingship to Nimrod by making the pronoun in “gave him” refer to Abraham instead.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p15#2/r19.anchor: بعضهم جعل ضمير ( آتاه ) لإبراهيم عليه السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v3p16/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p16/r1.speaker: أبو قاسم البلخي
ALUSI-FULL:v3p16/r1.claim: Abū al-Qāsim al-Balkhī takes the recipient of the kingship as Abraham, connecting the claim to the covenant’s exclusion of wrongdoers and to Abraham’s descendants receiving immense kingship.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p16/r1.anchor: وهو المحكي عن أبي قاسم البلخي

ALUSI-FULL:v3p16/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p16/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p16/r2.claim: Al-Ālūsī rejects the Abraham reading as contrary to the apparent sense and early transmitted exegesis; Abraham then had no rule, authority, or command.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p16/r2.anchor: ولا يخفى أنه خلاف المنساق إلى الذهن وخلاف التفسير المأثور عن السلف الصالح

ALUSI-FULL:v3p16/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p16/r3.speaker: بعض الإمامية
ALUSI-FULL:v3p16/r3.claim: Some Imāmīs distinguish prohibited kingship, which invests someone with command and obligatory obedience, from Nimrod’s coercive power, wealth, and influence.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p16/r3.anchor: وذهب بعض الإمامية إلى أن الملك الذي لا يؤتيه الله للكافر هو ما كان بتمليك الأمر والنهي

ALUSI-FULL:v3p16/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p16/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p16/r4.claim: Al-Ālūsī says the Imāmī argument comes close to the truth in assigning true kingship to Abraham, though he detects doctrinal misdirection and an insinuation against the Companions.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p16/r4.anchor: بل الذي أوتي ذلك في الحقيقة إبراهيم عليه الصلاة والسلام

ALUSI-FULL:v3p16/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p16/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p16/r5.claim: The wording shifts from a pronoun to God’s explicit name, a noteworthy choice in this context.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p16/r5.anchor: وفي العدول عن الإضمار إلى الإظهار في هذا المقام

ALUSI-FULL:v3p16/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p16/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p16/r6.claim: The temporal “when Abraham said” can attach to “disputed”; it has also been proposed as a substitute for “gave him,” though that assumes the Abraham reading.

ALUSI-FULL:v3p16/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p16/r7.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v3p16/r7.claim: Abū Ḥayyān objects to making this a substitute for the grant because the two time expressions refer to different times.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p16/r7.anchor: واعترضه أبو حيان بأن الظرفين مختلفان إذ وقت إيتائه الملك ليس وقت إبراهيم عليه السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v3p16/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p16/r8.speaker: ما روي
ALUSI-FULL:v3p16/r8.claim: A report says Abraham spoke these words while imprisoned for breaking the idols, after Nimrod asked who was Lord of the one calling people to the truth.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p16/r8.anchor: فانه على ما روى قاله أن سجن لكسره الأصنام وإثر قول نمروذ له وقد كان أوتي قبل الملك

ALUSI-FULL:v3p17/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p17/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p17/r1.claim: One common approach sees Abraham switch to a clearer proof after Nimrod’s objection; a second says he switches only the example, from life and death to sunrise.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p17/r1.anchor: وفيه دليل على جواز انتقال المجادل من حجة إلى أخرى أوضح منها وهي مسألة متنازع فيها

ALUSI-FULL:v3p17/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p17/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p17/r2.claim: On the second approach, Abraham’s first claim concerned creating and annihilating possible things; life and death were examples, replaced by the clearer sun example.

ALUSI-FULL:v3p17/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p17/r3.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v3p17/r3.claim: Al-Imām argues that an apparent objection heard by an audience must be answered immediately, or confusion remains and an infallible messenger seems to leave a challenge unanswered.

ALUSI-FULL:v3p17/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p17/r4.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v3p17/r4.claim: Al-Imām says silence after the opponent’s challenge diminishes the messenger’s standing and makes him appear insignificant.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p17/r4.anchor: والثان أنه لما أورد المبطل ذلك السؤال كان ترك المحق الكلام عليه والتنبيه على ضعفه مما يوجب سقوط وقع الرسول

ALUSI-FULL:v3p17/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p17/r5.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v3p17/r5.claim: Al-Imām says the sun proof is weaker: humans cannot create life, but they can move bodies, so a powerful celestial being might move the heavens.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p17/r5.anchor: والثالث أنه وإن كان الانتقال من دليل إلى آخر أو من مثال إلى غيره لكنه يجب أن يكون المنتقل إليه

ALUSI-FULL:v3p17/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p17/r6.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v3p17/r6.claim: Al-Imām objects that Nimrod could claim to cause sunrise and challenge Abraham’s God to make it rise from the west; answering that challenge could force a miracle and displace the proof.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p17/r6.anchor: والرابع أن المارد لما لم يستح من معارضة الإحياء

ALUSI-FULL:v3p17/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p17/r7.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v3p17/r7.claim: Al-Imām adds that even if the sun rose from the west, that new event would become the proof, leaving the original sun argument wasted.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p17/r7.anchor: وأيضا فبتقدير أن يحصل طلوع الشمس من المغرب يكون الدليل على وجود الصانع هو هذا الطلوع لا الطلوع الأول

ALUSI-FULL:v3p17/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p17/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p17/r8.claim: The first-person yāʾ in “my Lord” is read with fatḥ or omitted.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p17/r8.anchor: بفتح الياء وقرئ بحذفها وأراد عليه السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v3p17/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p17/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p17/r9.claim: Abraham meant that God creates life and death in bodies.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p17/r9.anchor: وأراد عليه السلام يحي ويميت يخلق الحياة والموت

ALUSI-FULL:v3p17/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p17/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p17/r10.claim: Nimrod meant something else: according to a report, he brought two men, killed one, spared the other, and claimed that he gave life and death.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p17/r10.anchor: فقد روي عنه أنه أتى برجلين فقتل أحدهما

ALUSI-FULL:v3p17#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p17#2/r1.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v3p17#2/r1.claim: Al-Imām’s preferred account treats both statements as one proof: if life and death are direct, Nimrod cannot establish that claim; if mediated by celestial motions, humans lack power over those motions.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p17#2/r1.anchor: فالحق أن هذا ليس دليلا آخر ولا مثالا بل هو من تتمة الدليل الأول

ALUSI-FULL:v3p17#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p17#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p17#2/r2.claim: Al-Ālūsī says Nimrod’s claim was so plainly false that Abraham could leave it unanswered without confusing the audience or diminishing his authority.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p17#2/r2.anchor: أما أولا فلأن الشبهة إذا كانت في غاية السقوط ونهاية البطلان بحيث لا يكاد يخفى حالها

ALUSI-FULL:v3p17#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p17#2/r3.speaker: رُوي
ALUSI-FULL:v3p17#2/r3.claim: One report says Abraham did answer Nimrod, pointing out that Nimrod made the living dead but did not make the dead alive.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p17#2/r3.anchor: روى أنه ما انتقل حتى بين للمارد فساد قوله

ALUSI-FULL:v3p17#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p17#2/r4.speaker: الصادق
ALUSI-FULL:v3p17#2/r4.claim: Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq reports Abraham challenging Nimrod to revive the man he had killed if his claim were true.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p17#2/r4.anchor: وعن الصادق رضي الله تعالى عنه أنه قال له

ALUSI-FULL:v3p17#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p17#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p17#2/r5.claim: The Qur’an omits that refutation because Nimrod’s claim is manifestly false.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p17#2/r5.anchor: لكن لم يقص الله تعالى ذلك الإلزام علينا في الكتاب اكتفاءا بظهور الفساد جدا

ALUSI-FULL:v3p17#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p17#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p17#2/r6.claim: Al-Ālūsī rejects al-Imām’s claim that the sun proof is less clear, calling the opposite nearly undeniable.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p17#2/r6.anchor: وأما ثانيا فلأنه من الواضح أن المتنقل اليه أوضح في المقصود من المتنقل عنه

ALUSI-FULL:v3p17#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p17#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p17#2/r7.claim: The possible westward-sun objection also applies to al-Imām’s account of celestial motion; proposed explanations that the fire miracle silenced Nimrod or God made him forget are offered, but the latter is weak.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p17#2/r7.anchor: وقد أجابوا عن عدم قول اللعين ذلك بأن المحاجة كانت بعد خلاصه من النار

ALUSI-FULL:v3p17#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p17#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p17#2/r8.claim: Abraham’s proof rests on the self-evident need for a mover: Nimrod cannot be the mover, so if he claims to cause this motion, let him make the sun rise from the west.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p17#2/r8.anchor: بل الجواب أنه عليه السلام أستدل بأنه لابد للحركة المخصوصة والمتحرك بها من محرك لان حاجة المتحرك في الحركة إلى المحرك بديهية

ALUSI-FULL:v3p17#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p17#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p17#2/r9.claim: Al-Ālūsī says al-Imām’s celestial-motion reconstruction is not indicated by the verse or Nimrod’s stated claim, so it should not be imposed on the text.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p17#2/r9.anchor: وأما رابعا فلأن ما اختاره لا تدل عليه الآية الكريمة بوجه وليس في كلام الكافر سوى دعواه الإحياء والإماتة

ALUSI-FULL:v3p18/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p18/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p18/r1.claim: Al-Ālūsī relays the possibility that Nimrod did not claim to be the world’s sole god; he may have believed in delegated gods, as some Sabians attributed creation and governance to planets, and imagined such power could be delegated to an earthly being.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p18/r1.anchor: من أن المارد لما كان مجوزا لتعدد الآلهة

ALUSI-FULL:v3p18/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p18/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p18/r2.claim: Abraham exposes Nimrod’s inability to hold delegated creative power by invoking his necessary knowledge that he was born after not existing and therefore depends on a creator.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p18/r2.anchor: أراد إبراهيم عليه السلام أن ينبه على قصوره عن هذه الرتبة وفساد رأيه من جهة علمه الضرورى بأنه مولود أحدث بعد أن لم يكن

ALUSI-FULL:v3p18/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p18/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p18/r3.claim: Abraham does not state the whole doctrine of divine uniqueness; he hints that life and death are kinds of creation and annihilation, and a creator of every possibility must be wholly outside possibility, since multiplicity entails dependence.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p18/r3.anchor: على أنه لوح اليه من حيث أنه لا فرق بين الايجاد والاعدام نوعين هما الاحياء والاماتة والقادر على إيجاد كل ممكن وإعدامه يلزمه أن يكون خارجا عن الممكنات

ALUSI-FULL:v3p18/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p18/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p18/r4.claim: Nimrod’s reply suggests that an agent may depend on a creator for initial existence yet act independently thereafter, a position Al-Ālūsī attributes to deficient theologians.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p18/r4.anchor: كما عند بعض القاصرين من المتكلمين مفوضا إليه بعد إيجاده

ALUSI-FULL:v3p18/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p18/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p18/r5.claim: Nimrod contradicts himself: if he independently governs and creates, he is not delegated power by the Creator and cannot be free of dependence even briefly; sparing someone is not creating life.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p18/r5.anchor: وهذا قد خفى على الأذكياء فضلا عن الاغبياء

ALUSI-FULL:v3p18/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p18/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p18/r6.claim: Abraham makes the same point through the sun: the one responsible for its continued motion must also be responsible for its origination; Nimrod cannot assign the two to different agents.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p18/r6.anchor: فألزمه الخليل عليه السلام بأن القادر لا يفترق بالنسبة اليه الدوام والابتداء فان الله تعالى يأتى بالشمس من المشرق

ALUSI-FULL:v3p18/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p18/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p18/r7.claim: The challenge exposes Nimrod’s mistaken division of origination and continuation before the audience; the exchange is one integrated proof, not a switch to another argument or a clearer example.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p18/r7.anchor: مظهرا لدى السامعين ما كان عسى أن يغبى على البعض فهذا كلام وارد على الخطابة والبرهان

ALUSI-FULL:v3p19/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p19/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p19/r1.claim: The second statement names God directly rather than saying “my Lord,” countering Nimrod’s “I” and asserting God’s lordship over Abraham and Nimrod.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p19/r1.anchor: وإنما أتى في الجملة الثانية بالاسم الكريم ولم يؤت بعنوان الربوبية

ALUSI-FULL:v3p19/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p19/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p19/r2.claim: The wording rises from the earthly dispute to the heavens; “indeed” strengthens the assertion, and the imperative is a challenge that demonstrates incapacity.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p19/r2.anchor: ففيه ترق عما في تلك الجملة مالترقى من الأرض إلى السماء وهو في هذا المقام حسن التأكيد بأن والامر للتعجيز

ALUSI-FULL:v3p19/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p19/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p19/r3.claim: The first fa signals that the sun argument follows from the preceding claim; the sense is that if Nimrod misunderstood or argued sophistically, this removes the confusion.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p19/r3.anchor: والفاء الاولى للايذان بتعلق ما بعدها بما قبلها والمعنى إذا ادعيت الإحياء والإماتة لله تعالى وأخطأت أنت في الفهم أو غالطت

ALUSI-FULL:v3p19/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p19/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p19/r4.claim: The bāʾ is transitive, and both occurrences of min mark the starting point of motion.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p19/r4.anchor: في الموضعين لابتداء الغاية متعلقة بما تقدمها من الفعل

ALUSI-FULL:v3p19/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p19/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p19/r5.claim: Alternatively, each min phrase can be attached to an omitted circumstantial description meaning “subjugated” or “obedient.”
ALUSI-FULL:v3p19/r5.anchor: وقيل : متعلقة بمحذوف وقع حالا أي مسخرة أو منقادة

ALUSI-FULL:v3p19/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p19/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p19/r6.claim: “Buhita” means he was overcome, left speechless, and bewildered when the proof prevailed.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p19/r6.anchor: أي غلب وصار مبهوتا منقطعا عن الكلام متحيرا لاستيلاء الحجة عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v3p19/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p19/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p19/r7.claim: The reading buhita, with bāʾ open and hāʾ rounded, and bahita, with hāʾ kasra, are intransitive forms.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p19/r7.anchor: وقرئ بهت بفتح الباء وضم الهاء وبهت بفتح الأولى وكسر الثانية وهما لغتان

ALUSI-FULL:v3p19/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p19/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p19/r8.claim: With both first syllables open, the verb may be intransitive with “the one who disbelieved” as subject, or transitive with Abraham as subject and the unbeliever as object.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p19/r8.anchor: بفتحهما فيجوز أن يكون لازما أيضا

ALUSI-FULL:v3p19/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p19/r9.speaker: الكيا
ALUSI-FULL:v3p19/r9.claim: Al-Kiyā takes the verse to show that disputing in religion is permitted, even though Nimrod’s particular disputation was disbelief.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p19/r9.anchor: قال الكيا : وفى الآية دليل على جواز المحاجة في الدين

ALUSI-FULL:v3p19/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p19/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p19/r10.claim: God does not guide wrongdoers to paths of truth as He guided His allies; another reported interpretation is that He does not guide them to Paradise on Judgment Day.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p19/r10.anchor: إلى مناهج الحق كما هدى أولياءه وقيل : لا يهديهم إلى طريق الجنة يوم القيامة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p315#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p315#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p315#2/r1.claim: The opening asks whether the Prophet has heard the account of the man who disputed Abraham about his Lord.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p315#2/r1.anchor: معناه هل انتهى إليك يا محمد خبر الذي حاج إبراهيم أي خاصم وجادل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p315#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p315#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p315#2/r2.claim: حاج means that he quarreled and argued with Abraham.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p315#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p315#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p315#2/r3.claim: The disputant was Nimrod, the first to wear a crown, who tyrannized on earth and claimed divinity.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p315#2/r3.anchor: وهو نمرود وهو أول من وضع التاج على رأسه، وتجبر في الأرض وادعى الربوبية؟

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p315#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p315#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p315#2/r4.claim: The kingship God gave him caused his dispute: he became insolent and transgressed through the pride of rule.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p315#2/r4.anchor: أي لأن آتاه الله الملك فطغى أي كانت تلك المحاجة من بطر الملك وطغيانه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p315#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p315#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p315#2/r5.claim: Mujāhid says four ruled the earth: the believers Solomon and Dhū al-Qarnayn, and the unbelievers Nimrod and Bukhtanassar.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p315#2/r5.anchor: قال مجاهد: ملك الأرض أربعة، مؤمنان وكافران فأما المؤمنان فسليمان وذو القرنين

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p315#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p315#2/r6.speaker: مقاتل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p315#2/r6.claim: Muqātil dates the debate to after Abraham broke the idols: Nimrod jailed him, then released him before the attempted burning and asked about his Lord.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p315#2/r6.anchor: قال مقاتل: لما كسر إبراهيم الأصنام سجنه نمرود ثم أخرجه ليحرقه بالنار فقال له

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p315#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p315#2/r7.speaker: آخرون
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p315#2/r7.claim: Others place the debate after the fire: during famine Nimrod withheld food unless people named him lord; Abraham refused, received sand by divine provision, and his wife prepared it as food.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p315#2/r7.anchor: وقال آخرون: كان هذا بعد إلقائه في النار، وذلك أن الناس قحطوا على عهد نمرود

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p315#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p315#2/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p315#2/r8.claim: The verse omits the question that prompted Abraham's reply: Nimrod had asked him, Who is your Lord?
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p315#2/r8.anchor: وهذا جواب سؤال غير مذكور تقديره قال له: من ربك؟ فقال إبراهيم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p315#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p315#2/r9.speaker: حمزة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p315#2/r9.claim: Ḥamza reads the yāʾ of ربي with sukūn; Ibn ʿĀmir and al-Kisāʾī share this treatment in لعبادي الذين آمنوا, and Ibn ʿĀmir also in آياتي الذين.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p315#2/r9.anchor: قرأ حمزة {ربي الذي يحيي ويميت} بإسكان الياء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p316/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p316/r1.speaker: أهل المدينة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p316/r1.claim: Medinan readers retain and lengthen the alif of أنا in connected reading before a following fatḥa or ḍamma; other readers omit it, while all pause with it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p316/r1.anchor: قرأ أهل المدينة {أنا} بإثبات الألف والمد في الوصل إذا تلتها ألف مفتوحة أو مضمومة والباقون بحذف الألف

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p316/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p316/r2.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p316/r2.claim: Most commentators say Nimrod called sparing one man life and killing another death; Abraham's proof concerned resurrection, so he shifted to the clearer sun argument, not from inability.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p316/r2.anchor: قال أكثر المفسرين: دعا نمرود برجلين فقتل أحدهما واستحيا الآخر فجعل ترك القتل إحياء له

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p316/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p316/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p316/r3.claim: Nimrod was confounded, astonished, and left without an argument.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p316/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p316/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p316/r4.claim: The verb فبهت describes being bewildered and stunned, with the argument cut off.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p316/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p316/r5.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p316/r5.claim: An explanation for Nimrod's silence is that he feared Abraham would pray for the sun to rise from the west, worsening his disgrace and defeat.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p316/r5.anchor: قيل: إنما لم يقله لأنه خاف أن لو سأل ذلك دعا إبراهيم ربه فكان زيادة في فضيحته

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p316/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p316/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p316/r6.claim: Baghawī calls it correct that God diverted Nimrod from that reply, either to display the proof against him or as a miracle for Abraham.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p316/r6.anchor: والصحيح أن الله صرفه عن تلك المعارضة إظهارا للحجة عليه أو معجزة لإبراهيم عليه السلام

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:258/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:258/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:258/r1.claim: The disputant is Nimrod; his argument and foolishness are presented as astonishing.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:258/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:258/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:258/r2.claim: One reading takes the phrase causally: God’s granting kingship made Nimrod insolent and led him to argue.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:258/r2.anchor: لأن آتاه أي أبطره إيتاء الملك وحمله على المحاجة،

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:258/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:258/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:258/r3.claim: A second parsing says he argued out of gratitude for the kingship, an ironic reversal like repaying kindness with hostility.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:258/r3.anchor: أو حاج لأجله شكرا له على طريقة العكس كقولك عاديتني

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:258/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:258/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:258/r4.claim: A third parsing makes the phrase temporal: the dispute occurred when God granted Nimrod kingship.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:258/r4.anchor: أو وقت أن آتاه الله الملك

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:258/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:258/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:258/r5.claim: The temporal reading proves against Muʿtazilites who deny that God grants kingship to a disbeliever.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:258/r5.anchor: وهو حجة على من منع إيتاء الله الملك الكافر من المعتزلة.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:258/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:258/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:258/r6.claim: The time clause may depend on ḥājja, or replace the “because He granted him kingship” phrase on the second parsing.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:258/r6.anchor: ظرف ل { حاج } ، أو بدل من { أن آته الله الملك }

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:258/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:258/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:258/r7.claim: God gives life and death by creating life and death in bodies.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:258/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:258/r8.speaker: حمزة
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:258/r8.claim: Ḥamza reads rabb, omitting the yāʾ.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:258/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:258/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:258/r9.claim: Nimrod claimed to give life and death by pardoning a person sentenced to death and killing another.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:258/r9.anchor: قال أنا أحيي وأميت } بالعفو عن القتل وبالقتل.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:258/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:258/r10.speaker: نافع
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:258/r10.claim: Nāfiʿ reads anā without the alif.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:258/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:258/r11.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:258/r11.claim: Abraham avoids debating Nimrod’s false equivocation and offers a clear, unanswerable example of God’s power to prevent obstruction; this changes the example, not the proof.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:258/r11.anchor: أعرض إبراهيم عليه الصلاة والسلام عن الاعتراض على معارضته الفاسدة

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:258/r12.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:258/r12.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:258/r12.claim: Nimrod may have claimed power over every kind of action God performs, which Abraham refuted with the sun’s course.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:258/r12.anchor: ولعل نمروذ زعم أنه يقدر أن يفعل كل جنس يفعله الله فنقضه

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:258/r13.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:258/r13.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:258/r13.claim: Another account says Nimrod imprisoned Abraham for days after he broke the idols, then released him to be burned and questioned him about his Lord.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:258/r13.anchor: وقيل لما كسر إبراهيم عليه الصلاة والسلام الأصنام سجنه أياما

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:258/r15.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:258/r15.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:258/r15.claim: A variant reading means that Abraham overcame the disbeliever.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:258/r15.anchor: وقرىء { فبهت } أي فغلب إبراهيم الكافر.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:258/r16.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:258/r16.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:258/r16.claim: The unjust are those who refuse guidance; alternatively, God does not guide them to argument, salvation, or the path to Paradise on Judgment Day.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:258/r16.anchor: الذين ظلموا أنفسهم بالامتناع عن قبول الهداية. وقيل لا يهديهم محجة الاحتجاج

BURSEVI:v1p335#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p335#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p335#2/r1.claim: The question means: has knowledge reached you with certainty comparable to direct sight? More literally, it commands the listener to know from God's report, which gives certainty.
BURSEVI:v1p335#2/r1.anchor: ألم ينته علمك الذي يضاهي العيان في الإيقان

BURSEVI:v1p335#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p335#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p335#2/r2.claim: The phrase refers to the story of the king who argued with Abraham about his Lord.

BURSEVI:v1p335#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p335#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p335#2/r3.claim: Ḥājja means he debated, disputed, and answered an opponent with argument.

BURSEVI:v1p335#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p335#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p335#2/r4.claim: The reference to God's lordship, attached to Abraham, honors Abraham and signals that God supported him in the debate.
BURSEVI:v1p335#2/r4.anchor: عنوان الربوبية مع أن الإضافة إلى ضميره عليه الصلاة والسلام تشريف له

BURSEVI:v1p335#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p335#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p335#2/r5.claim: The king was Nimrod son of Canaan son of Shem son of Noah, the first to wear a crown, act tyrannically, and claim divinity.
BURSEVI:v1p335#2/r5.anchor: هو نمرود بن كنعان بن سام بن نوح

BURSEVI:v1p335#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p335#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p335#2/r6.claim: The clause is causal: God gave him sovereignty, and that is why he argued.

BURSEVI:v1p335#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p335#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p335#2/r7.claim: One explanation is that he reversed the proper response: instead of thanking God for sovereignty, he argued with Abraham.
BURSEVI:v1p335#2/r7.anchor: من باب العكس في الكلام بمعنى أنه وضع المحاجة موضع الشكر

BURSEVI:v1p335#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p335#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p335#2/r8.claim: Alternatively, God's granting him great wealth, ample means, and complete rule made him proud and insolent, which led him to dispute.
BURSEVI:v1p335#2/r8.anchor: والثاني أن إيتاء الملك حمله على ذلك لأنه أورثه الكبر والبطر

BURSEVI:v1p335#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p335#2/r9.speaker: مجاهد
BURSEVI:v1p335#2/r9.claim: Mujāhid says only four people ruled the whole world: the Muslims Solomon and Dhū al-Qarnayn, and the unbelievers Nimrod and Bukht Naṣr, identified in the source with Shaddād son of ʿĀd, builder of Iram.
BURSEVI:v1p335#2/r9.anchor: قال مجاهد لم يملك الدنيا بأسرها إلا أربعة مسلمان وكافران

BURSEVI:v1p335#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p335#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p335#2/r10.claim: God's granting sovereignty to an unbeliever challenges the Muʿtazilite claim that God must do what is best for each person; empowering an unbeliever over believers may not seem best for believers, but the author says it is a trial for ruler and subjects.
BURSEVI:v1p335#2/r10.anchor: ثم هو حجة على من منع إيتاء الله الملك للكافر وهم المعتزلة

BURSEVI:v1p335#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p335#2/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p335#2/r11.claim: The phrase idh qāla is a temporal adverb attached to ḥājja.

BURSEVI:v1p335#2/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p335#2/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p335#2/r12.claim: After Abraham broke the idols, Nimrod imprisoned him and brought him out to burn him, then asked who was the Lord to whom Abraham called people.
BURSEVI:v1p335#2/r12.anchor: روى أنه عليه السلام لما كسر الأصنام سجنه ثم أخرجه ليحرقه

BURSEVI:v1p335#2/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p335#2/r13.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p335#2/r13.claim: Abraham means that his Lord creates life and death in bodies; this is a sound proof because God is known through attributes and acts no other powerful being shares.
BURSEVI:v1p335#2/r13.anchor: يخلق الحياة والممات في الأجساد وجواب إبراهيم في غاية الصحة

BURSEVI:v1p335#2/r14.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p335#2/r14.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p335#2/r14.claim: Nimrod summoned two prisoners, killed one and released the other, then misleadingly described sparing a life as giving life.
BURSEVI:v1p335#2/r14.anchor: دعا برجلين قد حبسهما فقتل أحدهما وأطلق الآخر

BURSEVI:v1p335#2/r15.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p335#2/r15.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p335#2/r15.claim: Abraham answers with a decisive sign: God moves the sun from east to west by compulsion according to His will, whereas Nimrod would have to make it travel naturally the opposite way if he possessed comparable power.
BURSEVI:v1p335#2/r15.anchor: تحريكا قسريا حسبما تقتضيه مشيئته والباء للتعدية

BURSEVI:v1p335#2/r16.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p335#2/r16.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p335#2/r16.claim: Abraham does not bother to refute Nimrod's sham claim to give life and death, signaling that its falsity is so obvious it needs no response.
BURSEVI:v1p335#2/r16.anchor: ولم يلتفت عليه السلام إلى إبطاله مقالة اللعين إيذانا بأن بطلانها من الجلاء والظهور

BIQAI-FULL:v1p502/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p502/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p502/r7.claim: After God's majesty, the believers' allegiance, and the disbelievers' rejection, the Abraham and ruined-town narratives demonstrate divine power and recall the people revived after death in 2:243; al-Ḥarālī says this elevated point is addressed specifically to the Prophet.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p502/r7.anchor: أخذ يدل على ذلك بقصة المحاج للخليل والمار على القرية مذكرا بقصة الذين قال لهم موتوا ثم أحياهم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p502/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p502/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p502/r8.claim: The question means know as though witnessing directly, owing to the Prophet's complete insight and the illuminating meanings God placed within him.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p502/r8.anchor: أي تعلم بما نخبرك به علما هو عندك كالمشاهدة لما لك من كمال البصيرة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p502/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p502/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p502/r9.claim: The opponent is Nimrod; Abraham is the Arabs' forefather, whom they especially ought to follow. The pronoun in his Lord can refer to Abraham or his disputant, and the dispute concerns the creator and benefactor despite clear proofs and innate guidance.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p502/r9.anchor: الضمير يصح أن يعود على كل منهما أي فيما يختص به خالقه المربي له المحسن إليه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p502/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p502/r10.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p502/r10.claim: Al-Ḥarālī says worldly kingship is a trial for its recipient; Nimrod's sovereignty fed pride instead of gratitude and led him to imagine he deserved the kingship of the Lord of all dominion.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p502/r10.anchor: قال الحرالي : وفي إشعاره أن الملك فتنة وبلاء على من أوتيه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p503/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p503/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p503/r1.claim: The story of those told to die and then revived in 2:243 proves resurrection on a Day without sale, friendship, or intercession and prepares for Abraham's argument.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p503/r1.anchor: دلالة على البعث ليوم لا بيع فيه ولا خلة ولا شفاعة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p503/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p503/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p503/r2.claim: Abraham says his Lord alone gives life and death; the wording implies an earlier exchange and someone claiming to share this divine attribute.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p503/r2.anchor: وهذه العبارة تدل على تقدم كلام في هذا وادعاء أحد لمشاركة في هذه الصفة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p503/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p503/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p503/r3.claim: Nimrod boasts that he gives life and death by pardoning someone liable to execution and killing someone who did not deserve death; this is a bold, unreflective misuse of his power over others.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p503/r3.anchor: بأن أمن على من استحق القتل وأقتل من لا يستحق القتل

BIQAI-FULL:v1p503/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p503/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p503/r4.claim: Seeing that the life-and-death claim might become obscure or prolonged, Abraham shifts to an unmistakable challenge that will silence Nimrod and expose his weakness.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p503/r4.anchor: فلما رأى إبراهيم عليه الصلاة والسلام أنه قد اجترأ على عظيم وأن محاجته في نفس الإحياء ربما خفيت أو طالت

BIQAI-FULL:v1p503/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p503/r5.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p503/r5.claim: Al-Ḥarālī says sound disputation avoids wrangling over a confusing proof and shifts to an outwardly clear argument, citing 18:53 as printed in the source.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p503/r5.anchor: وقال الحرالي : ولما كان من حسن الاحتجاج ترك المراء بمتابعة الحجة الملبسة كما قال تعالى

BIQAI-FULL:v1p503/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p503/r6.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p503/r6.claim: Al-Ḥarālī describes a shift from proof within the self to proof in the cosmos, using the sun, and links the two kinds of signs to 41:53.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p503/r6.anchor: نقل المحاج من الحجة الواقعة في الأنفس إلى الحجة الواقعة في الآفاق بأعظم كواكبها الشمس

BIQAI-FULL:v1p504/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p504/r1.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p504/r1.claim: Al-Ḥarālī says the apparent move from human life to the sun still completes the first proof: the soul is the body's sun, and giving life is like bringing that sun up from where it set.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p504/r1.anchor: ففي ظاهر الاحتجاج انتقال وفي طيه تقرير الأول لأن الروح شمس البدن

BIQAI-FULL:v1p504/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p504/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p504/r2.claim: God created the sun and brings it from the east each day, ages before Nimrod existed; Abraham challenges him to bring it from the west even once.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p504/r2.anchor: أي تسبب عن دعواك هذه أو أقول لك : إن { الله } بما له من العظمة والجلال

BIQAI-FULL:v1p504/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p504/r3.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p504/r3.claim: Al-Ḥarālī says the challenge shows that one Lord governs both human life and death and the sun's rising and setting; the sun's eventual rising in the west anticipates the Hour and the return of souls from bodies.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p504/r3.anchor: وفي لحنه إشعار بأن الله سبحانه وتعالى لا بد وأن يأتي بالشمس من المغرب ليكون في ذلك إظهار تصريفه لها

BIQAI-FULL:v1p504/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p504/r4.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p504/r4.claim: Al-Ḥarālī derives bahita from bewilderment that leaves someone frozen in the same state and form under the impact of something overwhelming.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p504/r4.anchor: قال الحرالي : من البهت وهو بقاء الشيء على حاله وصورته لا يتغير عنها لأمر يبهره وقعه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p504/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p504/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p504/r5.claim: Nimrod is confounded because the challenge proves he cannot change even a form God made, much less create from nothing or breathe life into it; Abraham exposes his denial of God's exclusive power.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p504/r5.anchor: فكيف له بأن يوجد صورة من العدم فكيف ثم كيف بإفاضة الروح عليها

BIQAI-FULL:v1p504/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p504/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p504/r6.claim: Nimrod wronged by claiming divine power and by executing the innocent while sparing the guilty; God's refusal to guide the unjust generalizes to those who put things out of place and whose hearts become dark.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p504/r6.anchor: لأنه ظلم في ادعائه ذلك وفي الوجه الذي ادعى ذلك بسبه من قتل البريء وترك المجترئ

BIQAI-FULL:v1p504/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p504/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p504/r7.claim: The shortened negative statement about guidance conveys generality; al-Imām says the concise wording yields greater meaning, a Qur'anic subtlety.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p504/r7.anchor: وقصر فعل الهداية لإفادة العموم , قال الإمام : فاختصر اللفظ إفادة لزيادة المعنى وهو من اللطائف القرآنية

BURSEVI:v1p336/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p336/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p336/r1.claim: Ibrahim changes examples to block Nimrod’s equivocation and clarify his point, rather than changing proofs, which would be poor debate practice.
BURSEVI:v1p336/r1.anchor: وأتى بمثال لا يجد اللعين فيه مجالا للتمويه والتلبيس فهو عدول عن مثال إلى مثال آخر لإيضاح كلامه وليس انتقالا من دليل إلى دليل آخر لأن ذلك غير محمود في باب المناظرة

BURSEVI:v1p336/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p336/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p336/r2.claim: The disbeliever became dumbfounded, confused, and astonished.

BURSEVI:v1p336/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p336/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p336/r3.claim: Calling him a disbeliever in the relative clause signals that disbelief caused the judgment and identifies the disputation itself as disbelief.
BURSEVI:v1p336/r3.anchor: وإيراد الكفر في حيز الصلة للإشعار بعلة الحكم والتنصيص على كون المحاجة كفرا

BURSEVI:v1p336/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p336/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p336/r4.claim: A wisdom of the sun rising in the west near the Hour is to demonstrate God’s power to deniers, including astrologers, and that the sun belongs to His kingdom.
BURSEVI:v1p336/r4.anchor: قال في "أسئلة الحكم" الحكمة في طلوع شمس قرب القيامة من مغربها إن إبراهيم عليه الصلاة والسلام قال لنمرود

BURSEVI:v1p336/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p336/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p336/r5.claim: Wrongdoers who expose themselves to lasting punishment by rejecting clear, decisive proofs are not guided while they choose disbelief and error.
BURSEVI:v1p336/r5.anchor: الذين ظلموا أنفسهم بتعريضها للعذاب المخلد بسبب إعراضهم عن قبول الهداية إلى مناهج الاستدلال

BURSEVI:v1p336/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p336/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p336/r6.claim: Alternatively, the verse means that God will not guide to Paradise in the afterlife those who disbelieved in this world.
BURSEVI:v1p336/r6.anchor: ويحتمل أنه لا يهدي طريق الجنة في الآخرة من كفر بالله في الدنيا

BURSEVI:v1p336/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p336/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p336/r7.claim: After Abraham’s debate and being cast into the fire, Nimrod’s people were devastated by mosquitoes; one entered Nimrod’s nostril and tormented him with blows to his head for four hundred years.
BURSEVI:v1p336/r7.anchor: روي أن النمرود لما عتا عتوا كبيرا وألقى إبراهيم في النار بعد هذه المحاجة سلط الله على قومه البعوض

BURSEVI:v1p336/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p336/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p336/r8.claim: Nimrod built a tower toward heaven in Babylon, but God brought its structure down from its foundations.
BURSEVI:v1p336/r8.anchor: وهو الذي بنى صرحا إلى السماء ببابل فأتى الله بنياهم من القواعد فخر عليهم السقف من فوقهم

DURR-FULL:v2p24/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p24/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v2p24/r1.claim: After Abraham's opponent sends him away without food, Abraham gathers sand for his household; his wife finds it has become excellent food, and he recognizes it as God's provision and gives thanks.
DURR-FULL:v2p24/r1.anchor: فأخذ منه فأتى أهله فوضع متاعه ثم نام فقامت امرأته إلى متاعه ففتحته فإذا هو بأجود طعام رآه أحد

DURR-FULL:v2p24/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p24/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p24/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the disputant as Nimrod son of Canaan, said to be earth's first king; Nimrod claimed to give life by sparing one man and cause death by killing another.
DURR-FULL:v2p24/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {ألم تر إلى الذي حاج إبراهيم} قال: نمرود بن كنعان يزعمون أنه أول من ملك في الأرض

DURR-FULL:v2p24/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p24/r3.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v2p24/r3.claim: Qatada reports that Nimrod son of Canaan was the first king to become tyrannical, built Babylon's tower, and staged his claim by killing one man and sparing another.
DURR-FULL:v2p24/r3.anchor: عن قتادة قال: كنا نحدث أنه ملك يقال له نمرود بن كنعان وهو أول ملك تجبر في الأرض

IBNABIHATIM:v2p498#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p498#2/r1.speaker: علي
IBNABIHATIM:v2p498#2/r1.claim: Ali identifies the man who disputed with Abraham as Nimrod son of Canaan.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p498#2/r1.anchor: سمعت عليا يقول : الذي حاج إبراهيم في ربه : نمرود بن كنعان

IBNABIHATIM:v2p498#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p498#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v2p498#2/r2.claim: Qatada says God gave Nimrod kingship; Nimrod son of Canaan was a tyrant and the first person to tyrannize on earth. Mujahid, Ikrima, Hasan, and Qatada likewise identify him as Nimrod.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p498#2/r2.anchor: عن قتادة ، في قوله : الم تر إلى الذي حاج إبراهيم في ربه

IBNABIHATIM:v2p498#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p498#2/r3.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v2p498#2/r3.claim: Al-Suddi recounts that Nimrod claimed to give life and death by starving four captives, then feeding two so they lived and leaving two to die; Abraham recognized this was power exercised within Nimrod’s kingdom.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p498#2/r3.anchor: عن السدى ، قال : واخرجوا إبراهيم - يعني من النار - فادخلوه على الملك

IBNABIHATIM:v2p498#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p498#2/r4.speaker: عكرمة
IBNABIHATIM:v2p498#2/r4.claim: Ikrima explains Nimrod’s claim to give life and death as meaning that he kills whomever he wishes and spares whomever he wishes.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p498#2/r4.anchor: عن عكرمة في قوله : انا احيي واميت يقول : انا اقتل من شئت

IBNABIHATIM:v2p498#2/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p498#2/r5.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v2p498#2/r5.claim: Al-Suddi says Abraham answered Nimrod’s claim by challenging him to reverse the sun’s course; Nimrod was confounded and called Abraham mad, then expelled him to hide his own shame among his people.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p498#2/r5.anchor: قال له إبراهيم فان الله ياتي بالشمس من المشرق فات بها من المغرب فبهت الذي كفر وقال :

IBNABIHATIM:v2p498#2/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p498#2/r6.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v2p498#2/r6.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam relates that people sought food from Nimrod and acknowledged him as their lord; after Abraham defeated him with the sun challenge, Nimrod sent Abraham away without food.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p498#2/r6.anchor: عن زيد بن اسلم ان اول جبار كان في الأرض نمروذ ، وكان الناس يخرجون

IBNABIHATIM:v2p499/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p499/r1.speaker: سفيان
IBNABIHATIM:v2p499/r1.claim: Sufyan explains that the disbeliever was confounded by saying nothing in reply.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p499/r1.anchor: قال : سفيان ، قوله : فبهت الذي كفر قال : فسكت ، فلم يجبه بشيء

IBNABIHATIM:v2p499/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p499/r2.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v2p499/r2.claim: Ibn Ishaq says the proof was established against Nimrod.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p499/r2.anchor: عن ابن اسحاق ، يقول الله تبارك وتعالى : فبهت الذي كفر يقول : وقعت عليه الحجة

IBNABIHATIM:v2p499/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p499/r3.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v2p499/r3.claim: Ibn Ishaq explains that God does not guide the wrongdoers in argument, because they persist in misguidance.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p499/r3.anchor: وبه في قوله : والله لا يهدي القوم الظالمين اي : لا يهديهم في الحجة عند الخصومة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p345/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p345/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p345/r1.claim: “Have you not seen?” is an admonition using the vision of the heart, not physical sight.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p345/r1.anchor: ألم تر تنبيه، وهي رؤية القلب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p345/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p345/r2.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p345/r2.claim: ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib read the final rāʾ of “alam tara” with sukūn.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p345/r2.anchor: وقرأ علي بن أبي طالب «ألم تر» بجزم الراء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p345/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p345/r3.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة والربيع والسدي وابن إسحاق وزيد بن أسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p345/r3.claim: The disputant was Nimrod son of Canaan, son of Cush, son of Shem, son of Noah, the contemporary king associated with the fire and the mosquito.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p345/r3.anchor: هذا قول مجاهد وقتادة والربيع والسدي وابن إسحاق وزيد بن أسلم وغيرهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p345/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p345/r4.speaker: ابن جريج
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p345/r4.claim: Ibn Jurayj identifies Nimrod as the first king on earth; Ibn ʿAṭiyya says this is rejected.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p345/r4.anchor: وقال ابن جريج: هو أول ملك في الأرض وهذا مردود

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p345/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p345/r5.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p345/r5.claim: Qatāda calls Nimrod the first tyrant and the builder or owner of the tower at Babylon.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p345/r5.anchor: وقال قتادة: هو أول من تجبر وهو صاحب الصرح ببابل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p345/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p345/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p345/r6.claim: Other accounts give Nimrod a different lineage, as son of Falikh, son of ʿĀmir, son of Shalikh, son of Arfakhshadh, son of Shem, son of Noah.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p345/r6.anchor: وقيل: إن الذي حاج إبراهيم نمرود بن فالخ بن عامر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p345/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p345/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p345/r7.claim: Some say Nimrod ruled the whole world; he was one of two great disbelievers, the other being Nebuchadnezzar.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p345/r7.anchor: وقيل: إنه ملك الدنيا بأجمعها ونفذت فيها طينته وهو أحد الكافرين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p345/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p345/r8.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p345/r8.claim: In Zayd b. Aslam’s account, Nimrod controlled food distributions and demanded that visitors name their lord; when Abraham answered, Nimrod claimed to give life and death, then denied him provisions after the sun challenge.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p345/r8.anchor: ذكر زيد بن أسلم أن النمرود هذا قعد يأمر للناس بالميرة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346/r1.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346/r1.claim: After leaving without provisions, Abraham wished to bring home sand so his children could play; his wife found fine flour in one sack, and Abraham recognized this as God’s provision.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346/r1.anchor: فعلم إبراهيم أن الله تعالى يسر لهم ذلك،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346/r2.speaker: الربيع وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346/r2.claim: Al-Rabīʿ and others say Nimrod summoned two men, killed one and released the other, claiming he had caused one death and one life; Abraham answered with the sunrise challenge, leaving him stunned.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346/r2.anchor: وقال الربيع وغيره في هذه القصص:

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346/r3.speaker: السدي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346/r3.claim: Al-Suddī says that after Abraham emerged from the fire, Nimrod asked his lord; Nimrod claimed life and death by starving four men, feeding two and leaving two to die, before Abraham challenged him about the sun.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346/r3.anchor: ذكر السدي: أنه لما خرج إبراهيم من النار أدخلوه على الملك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346/r4.speaker: الأصوليون
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346/r4.claim: The legal theorists say Abraham meant life and death literally as divine attributes, while Nimrod exploited a figurative sense to mislead his people; Abraham yielded for argument’s sake, then used a sun example admitting no figurative evasion.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346/r4.anchor: وذكر الأصوليون في هذه الآية: أن إبراهيم عليه السلام وصف ربه تعالى بما هو صفة له

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346/r5.speaker: الأصوليون
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346/r5.claim: The theorists add that Nimrod could not claim to bring the sun from the east because the people would call him a liar.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346/r5.anchor: ولم يمكنه أن يقول: أنا الآتي بها من المشرق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346/r6.claim: The verb ḥājja is on the fāʿala pattern from ḥujja, meaning that the disputant contended with Abraham over the proof.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346/r6.anchor: وقوله حاج وزنه «فاعل» من الحجة أي جاذبه إياها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346/r7.claim: The pronoun in “his Lord” may refer either to Abraham or to the disputant.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346/r7.anchor: والضمير في ربه يحتمل أن يعود على إبراهيم عليه السلام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346/r8.claim: An ā-tāhu is causal (“because He gave him”); most commentators take the pronoun in ā-tāhu to mean Nimrod.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346/r8.anchor: وأن مفعول من أجله والضمير في آتاه للنمرود

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346/r9.speaker: المهدوي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346/r9.claim: Al-Mahdawī suggests the pronoun refers to Abraham, who was given the kingship of prophethood; Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls this an overstrained interpretation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346/r9.anchor: وقال المهدوي: يحتمل أن يعود الضمير على إبراهيم أن آتاه ملك النبوءة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346/r10.speaker: جمهور القراء ونافع
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346/r10.claim: Most readers drop the alif of anā in connected recitation; Nāfiʿ’s transmitters Warsh, Ibn Abī Uways, and Qālūn retain it before a following hamza, except in 7:188 and 26:115.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346/r10.anchor: وقرأ جمهور القراء أن أحيي بطرح الألف التي بعد النون من أنا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346/r11.speaker: أبو علي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346/r11.claim: Abū ʿAlī explains that anā consists of hamza and nūn with an alif added in pause; in liaison the following word takes the alif’s place, as with the pause hāʾ and the form ḥayyahlā.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346/r11.anchor: قال أبو علي: ضمير المتكلم الاسم فيه الهمزة والنون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the alif resembles one added in poetic rhyme; Abū ʿAlī says it drops when the word is joined, though the following word fills its role.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346#2/r1.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: وهذا مثال الألف التي تلحق في القوافي، فتأمل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346#2/r2.claim: A poetic line preserves the alif in connected anā, illustrating the exceptional retention discussed by the grammarians.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346#2/r2.anchor: أنا شيخ العشيرة فاعرفوني ... حميدا قد تذريت السناما

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346#2/r3.speaker: جمهور القراء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346#2/r3.claim: Most readers pronounce buhita with ḍamma on bāʾ and kasra on hāʾ, meaning the opponent was silenced and overcome by proof.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346#2/r3.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: «فبهت» الذي بضم الباء وكسر الهاء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346#2/r4.speaker: ابن سيده
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346#2/r4.claim: Ibn Sīda reports two other forms for being stunned: bahti with both opening and kasra on hāʾ, and buhita with opened bāʾ and ḍamma on hāʾ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346#2/r4.anchor: قال ابن سيده: ويقال في هذا المعنى: «بهت» بفتح الباء وكسر الهاء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346#2/r5.speaker: الطبري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346#2/r5.claim: Al-Ṭabarī reports that some Arabs used bahta with both bāʾ and hāʾ opened for this meaning.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346#2/r5.anchor: قال الطبري: وحكي عن بعض العرب في هذا المعنى، «بهت» بفتح الباء والهاء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346#2/r6.speaker: أبو حيوة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346#2/r6.claim: Abū Ḥaywa reads with opened bāʾ and ḍamma on hāʾ, a dialectal form of the reading with kasra on hāʾ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346#2/r6.anchor: قرأ أبو حيوة: «فبهت» بفتح الباء وضم الهاء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346#2/r7.speaker: ابن السميفع
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346#2/r7.claim: Ibn al-Sumayfiʿ reads both consonants opened, construing the phrase as Abraham stunning the disbeliever, with “the one who disbelieved” as the object; it may also be a dialect variant.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346#2/r7.anchor: وقرأ ابن السميفع: «فبهت» بفتح الباء والهاء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346#2/r8.speaker: الأخفش وابن جني
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346#2/r8.claim: Al-Akhfash reports a kasra-on-hāʾ reading like khariqa and dahisha; Ibn Jinnī says the more common ḍamma intensifies the meaning.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346#2/r8.anchor: وحكى أبو الحسن الأخفش قراءة «فبهت» بكسر الهاء كخرق ودهش

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346#2/r9.claim: Some interpreted the both-open reading as Nimrod abusing or cursing Abraham after being silenced and left without an answer.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346#2/r9.anchor: وقد تأول قوم في قراءة من قرأ فبهت بفتحهما أنه بمعنى سب وقذف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346#2/r10.claim: The closing statement addresses Muḥammad and his community: God does not guide people in arguments while they persist in wrongdoing, since wrongdoing has no guidance.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346#2/r10.anchor: إخبار لمحمد عليه السلام وأمته. والمعنى: لا يرشدهم في حججهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346#2/r11.claim: Although phrased generally, the warning is particular: God may guide wrongdoers who repent and return to faith; alternatively, it concerns those who meet God still unjust.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p346#2/r11.anchor: فظاهره العموم، ومعناه الخصوص، كما ذكرنا، لأن الله قد يهدي الظالمين بالتوبة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p307#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p307#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p307#2/r1.claim: Ḥājja means to dispute or argue; the opponent is Nimrod according to the collective exegetes.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p307#2/r1.anchor: قد سبق معنى ألم تر وحاج بمعنى خاصم وهو نمروذ في قول الجماعة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p307#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p307#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p307#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says four kings ruled east and west: the believers Solomon and Dhū al-Qarnayn, and the unbelievers Nimrod and Nebuchadnezzar.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p307#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس ملك الأرض شرقها وغربها مؤمنان وكافران فالمؤمنان سليمان بن داود وذو القرنين والكافران نمروذ وبختنصر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p307#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p307#2/r3.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p307#2/r3.claim: Ibn Qutayba explains that Nimrod disputed Abraham because God had given him kingship, making him impressed with himself and his rule.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p307#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة معنى الآية حاج إبراهيم لأن الله آتاه الملك فأعجب بنفسه وملكه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p307#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p307#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p307#2/r4.claim: Some exegetes supply an unstated prior question: Nimrod asked who Abraham's Lord was, and Abraham answered that his Lord gives life and death.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p307#2/r4.anchor: قال بعضهم هذا جواب سؤال سابق غير مذكور تقديره أنه قال له من ربك فقال ربي الذي يحيي ويميت

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p307#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p307#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p307#2/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses Nimrod's claim as “I pardon whom I wish and kill whom I wish.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p307#2/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس يقول أترك من شئت و أقتل من شئت

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p307#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p307#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p307#2/r6.claim: Abraham changed arguments to end the dispute after Nimrod's faulty reply exposed his poor understanding; matching the wording concealed that the two acts differ, and the shift was not an inability to defend the first proof.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p307#2/r6.anchor: فانتقل إلى حجة أخرى قصدا لقطع المحاج لا عجزا عن نصرة الأولى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p308/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p308/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p308/r1.claim: The unbeliever was silenced, his argument ended, and he became bewildered.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p308/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p308/r2.speaker: أبو رزين العقيلي، ابن السميفع
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p308/r2.claim: Abū Razīn al-ʿUqaylī and Ibn al-Sumayfa read the verb with fatḥa on both bāʾ and hāʾ.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p308/r2.anchor: وقرأ أبو رزين العقيلي وابن السميفع فبهت بفتح الباء والهاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p308/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p308/r3.speaker: أبو الجوزاء، يحيى بن يعمر، أبو حيوة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p308/r3.claim: Abū al-Jawzāʾ, Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar, and Abū Ḥaywa read with fatḥa on bāʾ and ḍamma on hāʾ.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p308/r3.anchor: وقرأ أبو الجوزاء ويحيى بن يعمر و أبو حيوة فبهت بفتح الباء وضم الهاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p308/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p308/r4.speaker: الكسائي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p308/r4.claim: Al-Kisāʾī notes that some Arabs pronounce the hāʾ with either kasra or ḍamma.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p308/r4.anchor: قال الكسائي ومن العرب من يقول بهت وبهت بكسر الهاء وضمها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p308/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p308/r6.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p308/r6.claim: Muqātil says God does not guide them to the argument; the verse refers to Nimrod.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p308/r6.anchor: قال مقاتل لا يهديهم إلى الحجة وعنى بذكل نمروذ

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p686/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p686/r1.speaker: author
