IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p686/r1.claim: The disputant is Nimrod, king of Babylon, whom Ibn Kathir identifies as Nimrod son of Canaan, son of Cush, son of Shem, son of Noah.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p686/r1.anchor: هذا الذي حاج إبراهيم في ربه وهو ملك بابل: نمروذ بن كنعان بن كوش بن سام بن نوح.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p686/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p686/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p686/r2.claim: The source also gives an alternate lineage for Nimrod: son of Falikh, son of Eber, son of Shalikh, son of Arpakhshad, son of Shem, son of Noah.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p686/r2.anchor: ويقال: نمرود بن فالخ بن عابر بن شالخ بن أرفخشذ بن سام بن نوح والأول قول مجاهد وغيره.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p686/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p686/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p686/r3.claim: Mujahid says the four who ruled the world were the believers Solomon and Dhul-Qarnayn and the unbelievers Nimrod and Nebuchadnezzar; Ibn Kathir adds that God knows best.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p686/r3.anchor: قال مجاهد: وملك الدنيا مشارقها ومغاربها أربعة: مؤمنان وكافران فالمؤمنان: سليمان بن داود وذو القرنين.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p686/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p686/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p686/r4.claim: The address means to see with the heart, addressed to Muhammad.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p686/r4.anchor: ومعنى قوله: {ألم تر} أي: بقلبك يا محمد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p686/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p686/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p686/r5.claim: Nimrod disputed with Abraham about whether his Lord exists and denied that any deity existed besides himself, as Pharaoh later did.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p686/r5.anchor: وذلك أنه أنكر أن يكون ثم إله غيره كما قال بعده فرعون

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p686/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p686/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p686/r6.claim: Nimrod's tyranny and grave defiance arose from arrogance and his long reign; he is said to have ruled for four hundred years.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p686/r6.anchor: وما حمله على هذا الطغيان والكفر الغليظ والمعاندة الشديدة إلا تجبره، وطول مدته في الملك؛ وذلك أنه يقال: إنه مكث أربعمائة سنة في ملكه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p686/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p686/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p686/r7.claim: Abraham argues for God from the observed origination of things after nonexistence and their passing away after existence: they cannot arise by themselves and require a free-acting creator.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p686/r7.anchor: أي: الدليل على وجوده حدوث هذه الأشياء المشاهدة بعد عدمها، وعدمها بعد وجودها. وهذا دليل على وجود الفاعل المختار ضرورة؛ لأنها لم تحدث بنفسها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p686/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p686/r8.speaker: قتادة، محمد بن إسحاق، السدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p686/r8.claim: Qatada, Muhammad ibn Ishaq, al-Suddi, and others say Nimrod claimed to give life and death by executing one condemned man and pardoning another.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p686/r8.anchor: قال قتادة ومحمد بن إسحاق والسدي وغير واحد: وذلك أني (4) أوتى بالرجلين قد استحقا القتل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p686/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p686/r9.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p686/r9.claim: Ibn Kathir rejects the execution-and-pardon reading as a real answer: it does not meet Abraham's argument, and Nimrod instead arrogantly pretended to possess divine power.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p686/r9.anchor: والظاهر -والله أعلم-أنه ما أراد هذا؛ لأنه ليس جوابا لما قال إبراهيم ولا في معناه؛ لأنه غير مانع لوجود الصانع.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p686/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p686/r10.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p686/r10.claim: Abraham's challenge shows that the true giver of life and death controls creation and the heavenly bodies; if Nimrod were divine, he should bring the sun from the west.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p686/r10.anchor: فالذي يحيي ويميت هو الذي يتصرف في الوجود في خلق ذواته وتسخير كواكبه وحركاته فهذه الشمس تبدو كل يوم من المشرق

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p686/r11.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p686/r11.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p686/r11.claim: Nimrod was struck dumb and unable to speak when his incapacity became clear, and Abraham's proof stood established.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p686/r11.anchor: فلما علم عجزه وانقطاعه، وأنه لا يقدر على المكابرة في هذا المقام بهت أي: أخرس فلا يتكلم، وقامت عليه الحجة.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p686/r12.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p686/r12.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p686/r12.claim: God does not inspire unjust people with proof; their arguments are invalid, and they face divine anger and severe punishment.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p686/r12.anchor: أي: لا يلهمهم حجة ولا برهانا بل حجتهم داحضة عند ربهم، وعليهم غضب ولهم عذاب شديد.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p686#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p686#2/r1.speaker: كثير من المنطقيين
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p686#2/r1.claim: Many logicians say Abraham abandoned the first proof for a clearer second one; Ibn Kathir rejects this account of the argument.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p686#2/r1.anchor: وهذا التنزيل على هذا المعنى أحسن مما ذكره كثير من المنطقيين: أن عدول إبراهيم عن المقام الأول إلى المقام الثاني انتقال من دليل إلى أوضح منه،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p686#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p686#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p686#2/r2.claim: The first proof serves as a premise for the sun challenge: together they expose Nimrod's false claim at both stages.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p686#2/r2.anchor: وليس كما قالوه بل المقام الأول يكون كالمقدمة للثاني ويبين بطلان ما ادعاه نمروذ في الأول والثاني

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p686#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p686#2/r3.speaker: السدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p686#2/r3.claim: Al-Suddi says the debate took place after Abraham came out of the fire, when he met the king for the first time that day.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p686#2/r3.anchor: وقد ذكر السدي أن هذه المناظرة كانت بين إبراهيم ونمروذ بعد خروج إبراهيم من النار ولم يكن اجتمع بالملك إلا في ذلك اليوم فجرت بينهما هذه المناظرة.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p686#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p686#2/r4.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p686#2/r4.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam reports that Nimrod withheld provisions from Abraham, who carried home saddlebags of dirt to distract his family; Sarah found them filled with fine food, which Abraham recognized as God's provision.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p686#2/r4.anchor: عن زيد بن أسلم: أن النمروذ كان عنده (1) طعام وكان الناس يغدون (2) إليه للميرة فوفد إبراهيم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p686#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p686#2/r5.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p686#2/r5.claim: In Zayd ibn Aslam's report, the king refused an angel's three calls to believe and challenged God to assemble forces; a swarm of gnats destroyed his army, one tormented him in the nose for four hundred years, and it killed him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p686#2/r5.anchor: وبعث الله إلى ذلك الملك الجبار ملكا يأمره بالإيمان بالله فأبى عليه ثم دعاه الثانية فأبى ثم الثالثة فأبى

JISHUMI:v2p1007/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1007/r4.speaker: الأعمش وحمزة
JISHUMI:v2p1007/r4.claim: The common reading has rabiya with a fatḥa on the yāʾ because of the following alif; al-Aʿmash and Hamza read the yāʾ quiescent, following the original form.
JISHUMI:v2p1007/r4.anchor: وعن الأعمش وحمزة ربي بسكون الياء على الأصل

JISHUMI:v2p1007/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1007/r5.speaker: القراء
JISHUMI:v2p1007/r5.claim: The readers generally pronounce buhita with ḍamma on bāʾ and kasra on hāʾ, in the passive; some read both vowels fatḥa, making Abraham the stunned subject.
JISHUMI:v2p1007/r5.anchor: والقراء على بهت بضم الباء، وكسر الهاء

JISHUMI:v2p1007/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1007/r6.speaker: أبو جعفر ونافع
JISHUMI:v2p1007/r6.claim: Abu Jaʿfar and Nafiʿ lengthen the alif in ana before a following alif in phrases such as ana uḥyī; other readers omit it in connected speech and retain it at pause.
JISHUMI:v2p1007/r6.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر ونافع أنا أحيي بمد أنا

JISHUMI:v2p1007/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1007/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1007/r7.claim: Muḥājja is a reciprocal verbal form derived from proof: each disputant acts or speaks in response to the other's action or statement.
JISHUMI:v2p1007/r7.anchor: مفاعلة من الحجة، ووزنه فاعل كقاتل وخاصم

JISHUMI:v2p1007/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1007/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1007/r8.claim: Shams is feminine and its plural is shumus.

JISHUMI:v2p1007/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1007/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1007/r9.claim: Baht can mean confronting someone with a lie; it also means bewilderment when proof prevails, and has three reported vocalizations.
JISHUMI:v2p1007/r9.anchor: مواجهة الرجل بالكذب عاتبه، بهته بهتا، ومنه الحديث

JISHUMI:v2p1007/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1007/r10.speaker: النبي
JISHUMI:v2p1007/r10.claim: A Prophetic report describes the Jews as a people of falsehood or bewildering speech, illustrating the word baht.
JISHUMI:v2p1007/r10.anchor: ومنه الحديث: اليهود قوم بهت والبهت

JISHUMI:v2p1007/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1007/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1007/r11.claim: The phrase al-ladhī kafara occupies nominative position because the verb is annexed to it.
JISHUMI:v2p1007/r11.anchor: الذي كفر موضعه رفع لإضافة الفعل إليه

JISHUMI:v2p1007/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1007/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1007/r12.claim: The preposition ilā in ilā alladhī ḥāj is an expression of wonder, as in asking whether one has seen such conduct.
JISHUMI:v2p1007/r12.anchor: دخلت في قوله إلى الذي حاج للتعجيب كما يقال

JISHUMI:v2p1008/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1008/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1008/r1.claim: After establishing God as believers' protector and saying unbelievers have no protector, God consoles the Prophet with Abraham's story as further proof.
JISHUMI:v2p1008/r1.anchor: لما بين تعالى أنه ولي المؤمنين وناصرهم، وأن الكافر لا ولي له

JISHUMI:v2p1008/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1008/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1008/r2.claim: The address to Muhammad expresses wonder: have you seen the conduct of someone who disputed and argued?
JISHUMI:v2p1008/r2.anchor: ألم تر يا محمد تعجيب منه لنبيه، أي أرأيت كصنع من حاج

JISHUMI:v2p1008/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1008/r3.speaker: مجاهد
JISHUMI:v2p1008/r3.claim: Mujahid, Qatada, and al-Rabiʿ identify Abraham's disputant as Nimrod son of Canaan, the first to claim divinity.
JISHUMI:v2p1008/r3.anchor: النمرود بن كنعان، وهو أول من تجرأ وادعى الربوبية، عن مجاهد وقتادة والربيع

JISHUMI:v2p1008/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1008/r4.speaker: مقاتل
JISHUMI:v2p1008/r4.claim: Muqatil places the dispute after Abraham broke the idols but before he was thrown into the fire.
JISHUMI:v2p1008/r4.anchor: عند كسر الأصنام قبل الإلقاء في النار، عن مقاتل

JISHUMI:v2p1008/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1008/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1008/r5.claim: Another account places the dispute after Abraham had been thrown into the fire.

JISHUMI:v2p1008/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1008/r6.speaker: الحسن وأبو علي وأبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v2p1008/r6.claim: Hasan, Abu ʿAli, and Abu Muslim take the pronoun as Nimrod: God gave him worldly wealth and dominion, which even an unbeliever may receive, unlike spiritual authority.
JISHUMI:v2p1008/r6.anchor: آتاه قيل: تعود إلى المحاج أعطاه الله الملك وهو نعيم الدنيا

JISHUMI:v2p1008/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1008/r7.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v2p1008/r7.claim: Abu Muslim also says the ruler was given dominion while a believer and later became an unbeliever.
JISHUMI:v2p1008/r7.anchor: وقيل: آتاه الملك وكان مؤمنا فكفر، عن أبي مسلم

JISHUMI:v2p1008/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1008/r8.speaker: أبو حذيفة وأبو القاسم
JISHUMI:v2p1008/r8.claim: Abu Hudhayfa and Abu al-Qasim take the pronoun in atāhu to refer to Abraham.
JISHUMI:v2p1008/r8.anchor: وقيل: تعود الكناية على إبراهيم، عن أبي حذيفة وأبي القاسم

JISHUMI:v2p1008/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1008/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1008/r9.claim: An omitted question is understood before Abraham's answer: someone asks who his Lord is, and he replies that his Lord gives life and death.
JISHUMI:v2p1008/r9.anchor: كأنه قيل: من ربك؟ فقال: ربي الذي يحيي ويميت

JISHUMI:v2p1008/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1008/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1008/r10.claim: Nimrod claims to give life by releasing a condemned prisoner and to cause death by killing whomever he chooses.
JISHUMI:v2p1008/r10.anchor: أنا أحيي بالتخلية من الحبس من وجب عليه القتل، وأميت بالقتل

JISHUMI:v2p1008/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1008/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1008/r11.claim: Nimrod's answer is profound ignorance: he equivocates on the wording and avoids the proof, since only God originates life and death.
JISHUMI:v2p1008/r11.anchor: وهذا جهل عظيم منه؛ لأنه اعتمد في المعارضة الاشتراك

JISHUMI:v2p1008/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1008/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1008/r12.claim: Abraham asks Nimrod to bring the sun from the west after God brings it from its place of rising to its setting.
JISHUMI:v2p1008/r12.anchor: يعني من موضع الطلوع فأت بها من المغرب موضع الغروب

JISHUMI:v2p1008/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1008/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1008/r13.claim: Abraham's shift to the sun argument was not a concession: Nimrod had no response to the first proof, and the new proof reinforced it.
JISHUMI:v2p1008/r13.anchor: إلى حجة أخرى لا عجزا، ولكن ظهرت حجته من غير اعتراض

JISHUMI:v2p1008/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1008/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1008/r14.claim: Another explanation says Abraham moved from one example to another because the core proof is that God can do what no one else can, such as life, death, or celestial motion.
JISHUMI:v2p1008/r14.anchor: وقيل: انتقل من مثال إلى مثال؛ لأن أصل الحجة أنه يقدر على ما لا يقدر عليه أحد

JISHUMI:v2p1009/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1009/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1009/r1.claim: Nimrod did not challenge Abraham to ask God to bring the sun from the west because he knew from the signs that God would do it, making his defeat worse.
JISHUMI:v2p1009/r1.anchor: لأنه علم بما رأى من الآيات أنه لو سأله لفعله، فيزداد فضيحة

JISHUMI:v2p1009/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1009/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1009/r2.claim: Alternatively, God abandoned Nimrod and gave Abraham subtle aid, preventing the opponent from confusing the issue or offering a specious doubt.
JISHUMI:v2p1009/r2.anchor: خذله ولطف لإبراهيم حتى لم يلبس، ولم يأت بشبهة

JISHUMI:v2p1009/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1009/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1009/r3.claim: The unbeliever was bewildered and silenced when the proof appeared.

JISHUMI:v2p1009/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1009/r4.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v2p1009/r4.claim: Abu Muslim says the disputant remained defeated, unable to say anything.
JISHUMI:v2p1009/r4.anchor: بقي مغلوبا لا يجد مقالا، عن أبي مسلم

JISHUMI:v2p1009/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1009/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1009/r5.claim: One reading is that God does not assist wrongdoers in achieving corrupt aims.
JISHUMI:v2p1009/r5.anchor: بالمعونة على بلوغ البغية من الفساد

JISHUMI:v2p1009/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1009/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1009/r6.claim: Another reading is that God does not guide them in argument as He guides His prophets.
JISHUMI:v2p1009/r6.anchor: لا يهديهم إلى المحاجة كما يهدي أنبياءه

JISHUMI:v2p1009/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1009/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1009/r7.claim: A further view says God withholds subtle aid and support from people known to be ineligible for it.
JISHUMI:v2p1009/r7.anchor: إذ علم أنه لا لطف لهم

JISHUMI:v2p1009/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1009/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1009/r8.claim: Other explanations say God does not judge them to be guided or lead them to Paradise.
JISHUMI:v2p1009/r8.anchor: لا يحكم بهدايتهم، وقيل: لا يهديهم إلى الجنة

JISHUMI:v2p1009/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1009/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1009/r9.claim: The validity of disputation shows that knowledge of God is acquired rather than necessary, since debating necessary truths would be improper.
JISHUMI:v2p1009/r9.anchor: تدل الآية على أن المعارف مكتسبة غير ضرورية؛ لذلك صحت المحاجة

JISHUMI:v2p1009/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1009/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1009/r10.claim: The verse refutes blind imitation as a route to knowledge: if imitation produced knowledge, disputation would be unnecessary.
JISHUMI:v2p1009/r10.anchor: وتدل على بطلان التقليد؛ إذ لو كان طريقا للعلم لما احتيج إلى المحاجة

JISHUMI:v2p1009/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1009/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1009/r11.claim: The argument validates analogy and rational inference because they make disputation possible.
JISHUMI:v2p1009/r11.anchor: وتدل على صحة القياس والاستدلال؛ لأن المحاجة بها تتم

JISHUMI:v2p1009/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1009/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1009/r12.claim: Nimrod's claim to give life and death indicates that he claimed divinity for himself.
JISHUMI:v2p1009/r12.anchor: هذا الذي حاج كان يدعي الربوبية لنفسه؛ لذلك قال: أنا أحيي وأميت

JISHUMI:v2p1009/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1009/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1009/r13.claim: The route to knowing God is to infer from acts no one else can perform; the verse uses life and death as especially clear examples.
JISHUMI:v2p1009/r13.anchor: الطريق إلى معرفته سبحانه - هو فعل ما لا يقدر عليه غيره

JISHUMI:v2p1009/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1009/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1009/r14.claim: Nimrod's reply was an obviously false equivocation: Abraham argued from origination, while Nimrod answered with a verbal resemblance, so he went silent.
JISHUMI:v2p1009/r14.anchor: احتج بالاختراع، فعارضه بالعبارة، فلذلك سكت عن الجواب

JISHUMI:v2p1009/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1009/r15.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1009/r15.claim: Giving a second proof after the first succeeds is sound reinforcement; Abraham changes examples, not the underlying proof that only God can create such acts.
JISHUMI:v2p1009/r15.anchor: حسن إيراد حجة بعد حجة تأكيدا إذا ظهرت الأولى

JISHUMI:v2p1009/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1009/r16.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1009/r16.claim: Abraham chose life-giving because it indicates God and is the first and foundational blessing, reminding Nimrod and others of divine unity and favor.
JISHUMI:v2p1009/r16.anchor: وإنما اختار إبراهيم (عليه السلام) الإحياء؛ لأنه - مع دلالته

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p329/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p329/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p329/r1.claim: The person who argued with Abraham is Nimrod son of Canaan, described as the first tyrant on earth and claimant to divinity.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p329/r1.anchor: هو النمرود بن كنعان , وهو أول من تجبر في الأرض

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p329/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p329/r2.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p329/r2.claim: Hasan says the pronoun refers to Nimrod: God gave him kingship, and he then disputed about God.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p329/r2.anchor: أحدهما : هو النمرود لما أوتي الملك حاج في الله تعالى

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p329/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p329/r3.speaker: أبو حذيفة
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p329/r3.claim: Abu Hudhayfa says the pronoun refers to Abraham: God gave Abraham kingship, and Nimrod argued against him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p329/r3.anchor: والثاني : هو إبراهيم لما آتاه الله الملك حاجه النمرود

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p329/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p329/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p329/r4.claim: Muḥājja can mean answering an argument with a counterargument or objecting to an argument in a way that invalidates it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p329/r4.anchor: وفي المحاجة وجهان محتملان : أحدهما : أنه معارضة الحجة بمثلها

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p329/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p329/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p329/r5.claim: Nimrod claimed to give life by releasing and sparing someone liable to execution, and death by killing without a legally sufficient cause, matching the words while evading the different causes.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p329/r5.anchor: يريد أنه يحيي من وجب عليه القتل بالتخلية والاستبقاء , ويميت بأن يقتل

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p329/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p329/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p329/r6.claim: One answer is that Nimrod's defective reply was already evident, so the sun argument reinforced the case; the other is that Abraham chose an unconfounded proof to defeat Nimrod's sophistry.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p329/r6.anchor: ففيه جوابان : أحدهما : أنه قد ظهر من فساد معارضته ما لم يحتج معه إلى نصرة حجته

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p329/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p329/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p329/r7.claim: The second answer is that Abraham chose a proof free of confusion after Nimrod muddied the earlier argument with a specious objection.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p329/r7.anchor: والجواب الثاني : أنه لما كان في تلك الحجة إشغاب منه بما عارضها به من الشبهة

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p329/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p329/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p329/r8.claim: Māwardī gives two answers to why Nimrod did not demand that Abraham's Lord bring the sun from the west: God deprived him of that reply, or Nimrod feared disgrace after seeing the signs.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p329/r8.anchor: ففيه جوابان : أحدهما : أن الله خذله بالصرف عن هذه الشبهة

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p329/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p329/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p329/r9.claim: The second possibility is that Nimrod saw Abraham's God could do it and feared further disgrace.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p329/r9.anchor: والجواب الثاني : أنه علم بما رأى معه من الآيات أنه يفعل

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p329/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p329/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p329/r10.claim: Bahita has two explanations: he was perplexed, or he was silenced and had no answer.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p329/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p329/r11.speaker: أبو عبيدة
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p329/r11.claim: Abu Ubayda explains bahita as being cut off or silenced.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p329/r11.anchor: والثاني : معناه انقطع , وهو قول أبي عبيدة

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p329/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p329/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p329/r12.claim: A reading with fatḥa on both bāʾ and hāʾ makes the king the subject: he confounded Abraham with his sophistry.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p329/r12.anchor: وقرئ : فبهت الذي كفر بفتح الباء والهاء بمعنى أن الملك

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p329/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p329/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p329/r13.claim: Not guiding wrongdoers may mean that God does not help them uphold wrongdoing, or does not save them from its punishment.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p329/r13.anchor: يحتمل وجهين : أحدهما : لا يعينهم على نصرة الظلم

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p329/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p329/r14.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p329/r14.claim: Wrongdoing here may refer specifically to unbelief, or generally to turning from truth toward falsehood.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p329/r14.anchor: ويحتمل الظلم هنا وجهين : أحدهما : أنه الكفر خاصة

MUJAHID:v1p115#3/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p115#3/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p115#3/r1.claim: The ruler who argued with Abraham about his Lord was Nimrod son of Canaan.
MUJAHID:v1p115#3/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد ] ﴿ ألم تر إلى الذي حاج إبراهيم في ربه ﴾ قال هو نمروذ بن كنعان

MUQATIL:2:258/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:258/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:258/r1.claim: The disputant was Nimrod son of Kanaan, described as the first ruler of the whole earth and builder of the tower at Babel.
MUQATIL:2:258/r1.anchor: وهو نمروذ بن كنعان بن ريب بن نمروذ ابن كوشى بن نوح، وهو أول من ملك الأرض كلها،

MUQATIL:2:258/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:258/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:258/r2.claim: After Abraham smashed the idols, Nimrod imprisoned him, brought him out to burn him, and asked who his Lord was.
MUQATIL:2:258/r2.anchor: وذلك أن إبراهيم صلى الله عليه وسلم: حين كسر الأصنام سجنه نمروذ، ثم أخرجه ليحرقه بالنار،

MUQATIL:2:258/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:258/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:258/r3.claim: Abraham says his Lord gives life and death, and that He is the one Abraham worships and asks for good.
MUQATIL:2:258/r3.anchor: وإياه أعبد ومنه أسأل الخير، { قال } نمروذ { أنا أحيي وأميت } ،

MUQATIL:2:258/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:258/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:258/r4.claim: Nimrod claimed to give life and death by killing one of two men and sparing the other, calling this killing and reviving.
MUQATIL:2:258/r4.anchor: قال له إبراهيم: أرنى بيان الذى تقول، فجاء برجلين فقتل أحدهما، واستحيا الآخر، وقال: كان هذا حيا فأمته

MUQATIL:2:258/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:258/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:258/r5.claim: When Abraham challenged Nimrod to bring the sun from the west, Nimrod was stunned and had no answer.
MUQATIL:2:258/r5.anchor: فأت بها من المغرب فبهت } الجبار { الذي كفر } بتوحيد الله عز وجل، يقول: بهت نمروذ الجبار،

MUQATIL:2:258/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:258/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:258/r6.claim: After God saved Abraham from the fire, He sent a gnat that entered Nimrod's nose and brain; it tortured him for forty days. He struck his head with a hammer, quieting it briefly, and died from it.
MUQATIL:2:258/r6.anchor: ثم إن الله عز وجل سلط على نمروذ بعوضة، بعدما أنجا الله عز وجل إبراهيم من النار، فعضت شفته، فأهوى إليها فطارت فى منخره،

MUQATIL:2:258/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:258/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:258/r7.claim: God vows that before the Hour He will bring the sun from the west, so those who see it know He is God, able to do whatever He wills.
MUQATIL:2:258/r7.anchor: فقال الله سبحانه: وعزتى وجلالى لا تقوم الساعة حتى آتى بها، يعنى الشمس من قبل المغرب،

MUQATIL:2:258/r8.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:258/r8.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:258/r8.claim: God does not guide wrongdoers to the proof; here this refers to Nimrod, as in the parallel wording in 9:19.
MUQATIL:2:258/r8.anchor: ثم قال سبحانه: { والله لا يهدي القوم الظالمين } [آية: 258] إلى الحجة، يعنى نمروذ،

NASAFI-FULL:v1p125#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p125#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p125#4/r1.claim: God consoles the Prophet by recalling Abraham’s dispute with Nimrod, who claimed lordship.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p125#4/r1.anchor: ثم عجب نبيه عليه السلام وسلاه بمجادلة إبراهيم عليه السلام نمرود

NASAFI-FULL:v1p125#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p125#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p125#4/r2.claim: The pronoun in Abraham’s Lord may refer to Abraham or to the arguer; either way the two share one Lord.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p125#4/r2.anchor: والهاء فى ربه يرجع إلى إبراهيم أو الذى حاج فهو ربهما

NASAFI-FULL:v1p125#4/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p125#4/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p125#4/r3.claim: The clause may mean kingship made Nimrod arrogant and caused the dispute, used against the Muʿtazila on aṣlaḥ; alternatively the dispute occurred when kingship was given.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p125#4/r3.anchor: لأن آتاه الله يعنى أن إيتاء الملك أبطره وأورثه الكبر

NASAFI-FULL:v1p125#4/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p125#4/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p125#4/r4.claim: إذ is an adverb governed by يحاج or a substitute for أن آتاه when that phrase means at the time.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p125#4/r4.anchor: نصب يحاج أو بدل من أن آتاه إذا جعل بمعنى الوقت

NASAFI-FULL:v1p125#4/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p125#4/r5.speaker: حمزة
NASAFI-FULL:v1p125#4/r5.claim: The segment attributes a reading of إبراهيم ربي to Hamza.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p125#4/r5.anchor: ﴿ إبراهيم ربي ﴾ حمزة ﴿ الذي يحيى ويميت ﴾ كأنه قال له من ربك

NASAFI-FULL:v1p125#4/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p125#4/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p125#4/r6.claim: Abraham answers the question about his Lord by saying He is the one who gives life and death.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p125#4/r6.anchor: كأنه قال له من ربك قال ربى الذي يحيى ويميت

NASAFI-FULL:v1p125#4/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p125#4/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p125#4/r7.claim: Nimrod claimed to give life and death by pardoning one condemned to die and killing another.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p125#4/r7.anchor: يريد أعفى عن القتل وأقتل فانقطع اللعين بهذا

NASAFI-FULL:v1p125#4/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p125#4/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p125#4/r8.claim: Abraham did not abandon a valid first proof; because Nimrod distorted it out of obstinacy, Abraham gave an argument that could not mislead the weak-minded.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p125#4/r8.anchor: وهذا ليس بانتقال من حجة إلى حجة كما زعم البعض

NASAFI-FULL:v1p125#4/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p125#4/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p125#4/r9.claim: These astrologers knew the sun’s motion; God forces it against its apparent direction, so a claimant to divinity should be able to reverse it.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p125#4/r9.anchor: وكانوا أهل تنجيم وحركة الكواكب من المغرب إلى المشرق معلومة لهم

NASAFI-FULL:v1p125#4/r10.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p125#4/r10.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p125#4/r10.claim: Forced movement is likened to water carrying an ant on a millstone opposite its own direction.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p125#4/r10.anchor: كتحريك الماء النمل على الرحى إلى غير جهة حركة النمل

NASAFI-FULL:v1p125#4/r11.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p125#4/r11.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p125#4/r11.claim: The disbeliever was bewildered and stunned.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p125#4/r12.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p125#4/r12.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p125#4/r12.claim: God does not guide wrongdoers means that He does not grant them success.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p125#4/r13.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p125#4/r13.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p125#4/r13.claim: Some say God diverted Nimrod from asking Abraham to bring the sun from the west; another says Nimrod claimed divinity and acknowledged no other lord.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p125#4/r13.anchor: وقيل إنه كان يدعى الربوبية لنفسه وما كان يعترف بالربوبية لغيره

NASAFI-FULL:v1p125#4/r14.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p125#4/r14.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p125#4/r14.claim: Nimrod meant that he alone was the one to whom giving life and death could be attributed.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p125#4/r14.anchor: ومعنى قوله انا أحيي وأميت أن الذى ينسب إليه

NASAFI-FULL:v1p125#4/r15.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p125#4/r15.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p125#4/r15.claim: The verse permits theological argument: Abraham debated, prophets do not commit forbidden acts, and inviting disbelievers requires answering their demand for proof.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p125#4/r15.anchor: ولأنا أمرنا بدعاء الكفرة إلى الإيمان بالله وتوحيده

QURTUBI-FULL:2:258/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258/r1.claim: Alam tara is an interrogative of confirmation carrying amazement: the audience is told to marvel at the man who argued with Abraham.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258/r1.anchor: هذه ألف التوقيف، وفي الكلام معنى التعجب، أي اعجبوا له

QURTUBI-FULL:2:258/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258/r2.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ explains alam tara as have you seen, applying it both to the man who argued with Abraham and the one who passed a town.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258/r2.anchor: وقال الفراء: «ألم تر» بمعنى هل رأيت، أي هل رأيت الذي حاج إبراهيم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:258/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258/r3.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة والربيع والسدي وابن إسحاق وزيد بن أسلم وغيرهم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, Qatāda, al-Rabīʿ, al-Suddī, Ibn Isḥāq, Zayd ibn Aslam, and others identify the opponent as Nimrod son of Kush son of Canaan son of Sam, Abraham's contemporary king associated with the fire and the gnat.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258/r3.anchor: وهو النمروذ بن كوش بن كنعان بن سام بن نوح ملك زمانه وصاحب النار والبعوضة! هذا قول ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:258/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258/r4.claim: The account says gnats covered the sun, consumed Nimrod's army, and one entered his brain and ate it; he endured forty days while a servant beat his head with a hammer.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258/r4.anchor: بأن فتح الله تعالى عليه بابا من البعوض فستروا عين الشمس وأكلوا عسكره ولم يتركوا إلا العظام

QURTUBI-FULL:2:258/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258/r5.speaker: ابن جريج
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258/r5.claim: Ibn Jurayj says Nimrod was the first king on earth, but Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejects this claim.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258/r5.anchor: قال ابن جريج: هو أول ملك في الأرض. قال ابن عطية: وهذا مردود

QURTUBI-FULL:2:258/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258/r6.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258/r6.claim: Qatāda calls Nimrod the first tyrant and identifies him as the builder of the tower at Babel.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258/r6.anchor: وقال قتادة: هو أول من تجبر وهو صاحب الصرح ببابل

QURTUBI-FULL:2:258/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258/r7.speaker: قوم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258/r7.claim: Some say Nimrod ruled the whole world and was one of two infidel world rulers, the other being Nebuchadnezzar.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258/r7.anchor: وقيل: إنه ملك الدنيا بأجمعها وهو أحد الكافرين والآخر بختنصر

QURTUBI-FULL:2:258/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258/r8.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya gives another genealogy: Nimrod son of Faligh, son of Shalikh, son of Arfakhshad, son of Sam.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258/r8.anchor: وقيل: إن الذي حاج إبراهيم نمروذ بن فالخ بن شالخ بن أرفخشد بن سام حكى جميعه ابن عطية

QURTUBI-FULL:2:258/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258/r9.speaker: السهيلي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258/r9.claim: Al-Suhaylī instead traces Nimrod through Kush and Canaan son of Ham and says he ruled al-Sawād; he also recounts the separate king al-Ḍaḥḥāk, called al-Azhadaq, named Bīwarāsb son of Andarāst, who ruled all regions.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258/r9.anchor: وحكى السهيلي أنه النمروذ بن كوش بن كنعان بن حام بن نوح وكان ملكا على السواد

QURTUBI-FULL:2:258/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258/r10.speaker: حبيب
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258/r10.claim: The account says al-Ḍaḥḥāk was killed by Afrīdūn son of Athfiyān, was a tyrant who ruled a thousand years, and first crucified and amputated people; Ḥabīb compares a later tyrant's violence to his.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258/r10.anchor: وكان الضحاك طاغيا جبارا ودام ملكه ألف عام فيما ذكروا. وهو أول من صلب وأول من قطع الأيدي والأرجل

QURTUBI-FULL:2:258/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258/r11.claim: Nimrod the elder is said to have reigned four hundred years; his son Kush fathered Nimrod the younger, who ruled for one year.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258/r11.anchor: وللنمروذ ابن لصلبه يسمى «كوشا» أو نحو هذا الاسم، وله ابن يسمى نمروذ الأصغر

QURTUBI-FULL:2:258/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258/r12.claim: One account says Abraham broke the idols while people attended a festival; when they returned, he rejected worship of carved things and named the Lord who gives life and death.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258/r12.anchor: إحداهما أنهم خرجوا إلى عيد لهم فدخل إبراهيم على أصنامهم فكسرها فلما رجعوا قال لهم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:258/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258/r13.claim: Another account says Nimrod hoarded food and made people prostrate to receive supplies; Abraham refused to bow, so Nimrod denied him provisions and he returned empty-handed.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258/r13.anchor: إن نمروذ كان يحتكر الطعام فكانوا إذا احتاجوا إلى الطعام يشترونه منه، فإذا دخلوا عليه سجدوا له

QURTUBI-FULL:2:258/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258/r14.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258/r14.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says Nimrod asked each person who their lord was before rationing food; Abraham said his Lord gives life and death, Nimrod claimed the same power, then refused him supplies.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258/r14.anchor: وذكر زيد بن أسلم أن النمروذ هذا قعد يأمر الناس بالميرة، فكلما جاء قوم يقول: من ربكم وإلهكم؟

QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#2/r1.claim: In the food-hoarding account, Abraham's wife opened the bags he had filled with sand and found fine flour; the passage treats it as God's provision.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#2/r1.anchor: فعلم إبراهيم أن الله تعالى يسر لهم ذلك

QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#2/r2.speaker: أبو صالح
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#2/r2.claim: Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shayba transmits from Abū Ṣāliḥ that Abraham returned from seeking food with red earth that proved to be red wheat; crops from it grew dense grain from stalk base to tip.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#2/r2.anchor: ذكر أبو بكر بن أبي شيبة عن أبي صالح قال: انطلق إبراهيم النبي عليه السلام يمتار فلم يقدر على الطعام

QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#2/r3.speaker: الربيع وغيره
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#2/r3.claim: Al-Rabīʿ and others say Nimrod claimed to give life and death by killing one of two men and releasing the other; Abraham then challenged him with the sun's course.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#2/r3.anchor: وقال الربيع وغيره في هذا القصص: إن النمروذ لما قال أنا أحيي وأميت أحضر رجلين

QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#2/r4.speaker: الله تعالى
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#2/r4.claim: A report quotes God swearing that the Hour will not come until He brings the sun from the west, so people know He alone has power to do so.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#2/r4.anchor: وروي في الخبر: أن الله تعالى قال: وعزتي وجلالي لا تقوم الساعة حتى آتي بالشمس من المغرب

QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#2/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#2/r5.claim: Nimrod ordered Abraham thrown into the fire; the author says tyrants resort to punishment when defeated in argument and that God saved Abraham, as will be discussed later.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#2/r5.anchor: ثم أمر نمروذ بإبراهيم فألقي في النار، وهكذا عادة الجبابرة فإنهم إذا عورضوا بشيء وعجزوا عن الحجة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#2/r6.speaker: السدي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#2/r6.claim: Al-Suddī says that after Abraham left the fire, Nimrod claimed to give life and death by keeping four men without food or water, feeding two and leaving two to die; Abraham answered with the sun challenge.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#2/r6.anchor: وقال السدي: إنه لما خرج إبراهيم من النار أدخلوه على الملك ولم يكن قبل ذلك دخل عليه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#2/r7.speaker: الأصوليون
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#2/r7.claim: The theologians say Abraham intended God's literal power to create life and death, while Nimrod shifted to a figurative meaning and misled his people; Abraham granted this for argument, then moved to the sun, where no metaphor was possible.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#2/r7.anchor: ذكر الأصوليون في هذه الآية أن إبراهيم عليه السلام لما وصف ربه تعالى بما هو صفة له من الإحياء والإماتة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#2/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#2/r8.claim: The disbeliever was confounded because his argument was broken; he could not claim to bring the sun from the west, since intelligent people would know he was lying.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#2/r8.anchor: أي انقطعت حجته ولم يمكنه أن يقول أنا الآتي بها من المشرق لأن ذوي الألباب يكذبونه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#2/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#2/r9.claim: The verse permits calling a disbeliever king when God has granted him worldly sovereignty, status, and prominence; it also establishes debate and proof.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#2/r9.anchor: هذه الآية تدل على جواز تسمية الكافر ملكا إذا آتاه الله الملك والعز والرفعة في الدنيا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#2/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#2/r10.claim: The verse supports debate and adducing proof, a Qur'anic practice used to distinguish truth from falsehood.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#2/r10.anchor: وتدل على إثبات المناظرة والمجادلة وإقامة الحجة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#3/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#3/r1.claim: The Qur'an and Sunna teach debate and proof, including the demand for proof in 2:111, denial of proof in 10:68, Abraham's dispute over idols, Noah's debate, and Moses' debate with Pharaoh.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#3/r1.anchor: قل هاتوا برهانكم إن كنتم صادقين

QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#3/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#3/r2.claim: The Prophet debated the People of the Book and challenged them to mutual imprecation after proof; Adam and Moses disputed and Adam prevailed, and the Companions deliberated at the Saqīfa and over fighting apostates until truth was established.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#3/r2.anchor: وجادل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أهل الكتاب وباهلهم بعد الحجة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#3/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#3/r3.claim: The verse 3:66, asking why they dispute what they do not know, shows that argument grounded in knowledge is permitted.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#3/r3.anchor: فلم تحآجون فيما ليس لكم به علم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#3/r4.speaker: المزني
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#3/r4.claim: Al-Muzanī says debate must seek God's approval and participants must accept whatever truth becomes clear.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#3/r4.anchor: قال المزني صاحب الشافعي: ومن حق المناظرة أن يراد بها الله عز وجل وأن يقبل منها ما تبين

QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#3/r5.speaker: قوم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#3/r5.claim: Some say useful debate requires participants to be close or equal in religion, reason, understanding, and fairness; otherwise it becomes disputatious obstinacy.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#3/r5.anchor: وقالوا: لا تصح المناظرة ويظهر الحق بين المتناظرين حتى يكونوا متقاربين أو مستويين في مرتبة واحدة من الدين والعقل

QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#3/r6.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#3/r6.claim: ʿAlī reads alam tara with the final rāʾ in the jussive, with the yāʾ deleted; the majority reads it with a vowel.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#3/r6.anchor: قرأ علي بن أبي طالب «ألم تر» بجزم الراء، والجمهور بتحريكها، وحذفت الياء للجزم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#3/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#3/r7.claim: The phrase an ātāhu Allāhu al-mulk is accusative with an understood lām, meaning because God granted him kingship.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#3/r7.anchor: «أن آتاه الله الملك» في موضع نصب، أي لأن آتاه الله

QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#3/r8.speaker: نافع وابن أبي أويس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#3/r8.claim: Most reciters drop the alif in anā when followed in connected recitation by aḥyī; Nāfiʿ and Ibn Abī Uways retain it except at 7:188, where they drop it because the construction is rare.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#3/r8.anchor: وقرأ جمهور القراء «أن أحيي» بطرح الألف التي بعد النون من «أنا» في الوصل، وأثبتها نافع وابن أبي أويس

QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#3/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#3/r9.speaker: النحويون
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#3/r9.claim: Grammarians say the first-person pronoun is hamza plus nūn; the alif in anā and hāʾ in annahu clarify vowels at pause and fall away in connected speech, though poets sometimes retain the alif.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#3/r9.anchor: قال النحويون: ضمير المتكلم الاسم فيه الهمزة والنون، فإذا قلت: أنا أو أنه فالألف والهاء لبيان الحركة في الوقف

QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#4/r1.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#4/r1.claim: Al-Naḥḥās says Nāfiʿ retains the alif in أنا أحيي وأميت but considers this reading baseless.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#4/r1.anchor: قال النحاس: على أن نافعا قد أثبت الألف

QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#4/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#4/r2.speaker: مكي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#4/r2.claim: Makki reports the Basran analysis: the pronoun is hamza and nūn, while an extra alif reinforces it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#4/r2.anchor: قال مكي: والألف زائدة عند البصريين

QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#4/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#4/r3.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#4/r3.claim: Another explanation says the alif was added at pause to make the nūn's vowel clear.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#4/r3.anchor: وقيل: زيدت للوقف لتظهر حركة النون

QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#4/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#4/r4.speaker: الكوفيون
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#4/r4.claim: The Kufans treat أنا as the full pronoun and Nāfiʿ's alif as original; others delete it for lightness because the fatḥa indicates it.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#4/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#4/r5.speaker: الجوهري
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#4/r5.claim: Al-Jawharī calls أنا a first-person singular pronoun, built on fatḥ to distinguish it from أن, a particle governing the verb; the final alif marks the vowel at pause and normally drops medially, except in a poor dialect, as the poem shows.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#4/r5.anchor: قال الجوهري: وأما قولهم «أنا» فهو اسم مكنى

QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#4/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#4/r6.speaker: النحاس وغيره
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#4/r6.claim: Forms بهت, بهت, and بهت mean that someone was confounded, fell silent, and became perplexed.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#4/r6.anchor: وبهت الرجل وبهت وبهت إذا انقطع وسكت متحيرا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#4/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#4/r7.speaker: الطبري
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#4/r7.claim: Al-Ṭabarī reports that some Arabs used بهت with fatḥa on both letters for this meaning.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#4/r7.anchor: وقال الطبري: وحكي عن بعض العرب في هذا المعنى «بهت»

QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#4/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#4/r8.speaker: أبو حيوة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#4/r8.claim: Abū Ḥaywa reads فبهت with fatḥa on bāʾ and ḍamma on hāʾ, a dialect variant of the form with kasra on hāʾ.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#4/r8.anchor: قال ابن جني قرأ أبو حيوة:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#4/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#4/r9.speaker: ابن السميقع
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#4/r9.claim: Ibn al-Sumayqiʿ reads both letters with fatḥa, meaning Abraham confounded the unbeliever and making الذي accusative; it may also be a dialect form.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#4/r9.anchor: قال: وقرأ ابن السميقع «فبهت» بفتح الباء والهاء

QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#4/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#4/r10.speaker: الأخفش
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#4/r10.claim: Al-Akhfash reports a kasra on hāʾ, like غرق and دهش; most readers use ḍamma there.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#4/r10.anchor: قال: وحكى أبو الحسن الأخفش قراءة «فبهت» بكسر الهاء

QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#4/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#4/r11.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#4/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says some understood the fatḥa reading as abuse and slander: Nimrod cursed after being silenced and left helpless.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:258#4/r11.anchor: قال ابن عطية: وقد تأول قوم في قراءة من قرأ «فبهت» بفتحها

RAZI-FULL:v1p36#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p36#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p36#2/r1.claim: Al-Rāzī says denying that the recited Qur'an is God's speech denies a teaching known by mass transmission from Muhammad's religion and entails unbelief.
RAZI-FULL:v1p36#2/r1.anchor: فمنكره منكر لما عرف بالتواتر من دين محمد عليه الصلاة والسلام فيلزمه الكفر

RAZI-FULL:v1p36#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p36#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p36#2/r2.claim: He answers one argument by saying its reasoning is not peculiar to any one essence and would therefore entail that all things are eternal.
RAZI-FULL:v1p36#2/r2.anchor: ما ذكرتم غير مختص بماهية دون ماهي فيلزمكم قدم الكل

RAZI-FULL:v1p36#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p36#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p36#2/r3.claim: He answers another argument by calling its inference too obscure to outweigh self-evident truths.
RAZI-FULL:v1p36#2/r3.anchor: ما ذكرتم من الاستدلال خفي في مقابلة البديهيات فيكون باطلا

RAZI-FULL:v1p36#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p36#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p36#2/r4.claim: Calling successive letters and sounds God's speech means, metaphorically, that the expressions signify the eternal attribute subsisting in God's essence.
RAZI-FULL:v1p36#2/r4.anchor: كان المراد أنها ألفاظ دالة على الصفة القائمة بذات الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v1p36#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p36#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p36#2/r5.claim: In customary oaths, the expression “God's speech” is understood according to common usage.
RAZI-FULL:v1p36#2/r5.anchor: وأما حديث الحنث والبر فذلك لأن مبنى الإيمان على العرف

RAZI-FULL:v1p36#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p36#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p36#2/r6.claim: Saying God's speech is eternal refers to the eternal attribute signified by the letters and expressions.
RAZI-FULL:v1p36#2/r6.anchor: وإذا قلنا : كلام الله قديم لم نعن به إلا تلك الصفة القديمة التي هي مدلول هذه الألفاظ

RAZI-FULL:v1p36#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p36#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p36#2/r7.claim: Calling the Qur'an a miracle for Muhammad refers to created letters and sounds, since the eternal attribute existed before Muhammad.
RAZI-FULL:v1p36#2/r7.anchor: وإذا قلنا : كلام الله معجزة لمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم عنينا به هذه الحروف وهذه الأصوات

RAZI-FULL:v1p36#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p36#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p36#2/r8.claim: References to Qur'anic sūras and verses mean its letters; calling it eloquent or interpreting it refers to its expressions.
RAZI-FULL:v1p36#2/r8.anchor: وإذا قلنا : كلام الله سور وآيات عنينا به هذه الحروف وإذا قلنا : كلام الله فصيح

RAZI-FULL:v1p36#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p36#2/r9.speaker: الحشوية
RAZI-FULL:v1p36#2/r9.claim: The Ḥashwiyya claim that the sounds heard from a human are themselves God's speech.
RAZI-FULL:v1p36#2/r9.anchor: زعمت الحشوية أن هذه الأصوات التي نسمعها من هذا الإنسان عين كلام الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v1p36#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p36#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p36#2/r10.claim: Al-Rāzī rejects this because the sounds belong to the human tongue and voice; making them God's very attribute would place one attribute in both God and a human body.
RAZI-FULL:v1p36#2/r10.anchor: هذه الحروف والأصوات التي نسمعها من هذا الإنسان صفة قائمة بلسانه وأصواته

RAZI-FULL:v1p36#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p36#2/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p36#2/r11.claim: He compares the Ḥashwiyya claim to the Christian doctrine that the divine Word dwelt in Jesus, noting that the Ḥashwiyya extend the claim to every person.
RAZI-FULL:v1p36#2/r11.anchor: ولا فرق بين القولين إلا أن النصارى قالوا بهذا القول في حق عيسى وحده

STUDYQURAN:2:258/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:258/r1.speaker: Commentators
STUDYQURAN:2:258/r1.claim: Commentators sometimes identify Abraham’s antagonist as Nimrod, but the identification rests on folklore; no hadith names him, and the biblical account is ambiguous.
STUDYQURAN:2:258/r1.anchor: Commentators sometimes understand the antagonist here to be Nimrod, though this is based on folkloric material

STUDYQURAN:2:258/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:258/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:258/r2.claim: A reported account says the ruler killed one of two people and spared the other to claim that he gives life and causes death.
STUDYQURAN:2:258/r2.anchor: It is said that this man who disputed with Abraham brought out two people, killing one and leaving the other alive

STUDYQURAN:2:258/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:258/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:258/r3.claim: The exchange resembles Pharaoh’s claim in 79:24, and the Quran uses the life-and-death expression elsewhere, including 2:28.
STUDYQURAN:2:258/r3.anchor: A similar dynamic can be seen in the conversation between Moses and Pharaoh

STUDYQURAN:2:258/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:258/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:258/r4.claim: Grammatically, the person given sovereignty could be Abraham or his antagonist.
STUDYQURAN:2:258/r4.anchor: Grammatically, the recipient of sovereignty could be either Abraham or his antagonist

STUDYQURAN:2:258/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:258/r5.speaker: Most commentators
STUDYQURAN:2:258/r5.claim: Most commentators take the sovereignty to mean the antagonist’s worldly power, though Abraham’s descendants are also described as receiving mighty sovereignty.
STUDYQURAN:2:258/r5.anchor: but most commentators believe that it refers to the worldly power of the other person

STUDYQURAN:2:258/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:258/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:258/r6.claim: Abraham exposes the ruler’s pretense to God’s power over life and death; his appeal to nature also reflects the Quranic theme that creation displays signs of God.
STUDYQURAN:2:258/r6.anchor: Abraham’s triumph in the encounter both exposes the pretense of the ruler who sought to mimic God’s Power over life and death

STUDYQURAN:2:258/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:258/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:258/r7.claim: Abraham encounters the rising sun in a different context in 6:78.
STUDYQURAN:2:258/r7.anchor: Abraham encounters the rising sun in a different context in 6:78

TAB-FULL:v4p567/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p567/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p567/r1.claim: The address asks Muhammad whether he has seen in his heart the person who disputed with Abraham, God’s prophet, about his Lord.
TAB-FULL:v4p567/r1.anchor: ألم تر يا محمد بقلبك الذي حاج إبراهيم؟ يعني الذي خاصم إبراهيم، يعني إبراهيم نبي الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في ربه

TAB-FULL:v4p567/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p567/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p567/r2.claim: The disputant argued with Abraham because God had granted him dominion; the episode is presented to Muhammad as astonishing.
TAB-FULL:v4p567/r2.anchor: يعني بذلك: حاجه فخاصمه في ربه، لأن الله آتاه الملك، وهذا تعجيب من الله تعالى ذكره نبيه محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم

TAB-FULL:v4p567/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p567/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p567/r3.claim: The preposition ilā is used in an expression of astonishment; Arabs ask “what do you see in this?” meaning “have you seen anything like it?”
TAB-FULL:v4p567/r3.anchor: ولذلك أدخلت «إلى» في قوله: {ألم تر إلى الذي حاج} [البقرة: 258] وكذلك تفعل العرب إذا أرادت التعجيب

TAB-FULL:v4p567/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p567/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p567/r4.claim: The disputant is said to be a tyrant at Babylon called Nimrod, with two reported genealogies: son of Canaan son of Cush, or son of Falikh son of ʿĀbir.
TAB-FULL:v4p567/r4.anchor: وقيل: إن الذي حاج إبراهيم في ربه جبار كان ببابل يقال له نمرود بن كنعان بن كوش بن سام بن نوح، وقيل: إنه نمرود بن فالخ بن عابر بن شالخ

TAB-FULL:v4p567/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p567/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v4p567/r5.claim: Mujāhid identifies Abraham’s disputant as Nimrod son of Canaan.
TAB-FULL:v4p567/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قول الله: {ألم تر إلى الذي حاج} [البقرة: 258] إبراهيم في ربه أن آتاه الله الملك قال: «هو نمرود بن كنعان»

TAB-FULL:v4p567/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p567/r6.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v4p567/r6.claim: Qatāda reports that the king called Nimrod was the first ruler to tyrannize on earth and owned the tower at Babylon.
TAB-FULL:v4p567/r6.anchor: عن قتادة: {ألم تر إلى الذي حاج} [البقرة: 258] إبراهيم في ربه قال: «كنا نتحدث أنه ملك يقال له نمرود، وهو أول ملك تجبر في الأرض، وهو صاحب الصرح ببابل»

TAB-FULL:v4p567/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p567/r7.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v4p567/r7.claim: Qatāda also calls him Nimrod, the first king to tyrannize and dispute with Abraham.
TAB-FULL:v4p567/r7.anchor: عن قتادة، قال: هو اسمه نمروذ، وهو أول ملك تجبر في الأرض حاج إبراهيم في ربه

TAB-FULL:v4p567/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p567/r8.speaker: الربيع
TAB-FULL:v4p567/r8.claim: Al-Rabīʿ reports that the disputant was King Nimrod, the first tyrant on earth and owner of the tower at Babylon.
TAB-FULL:v4p567/r8.anchor: عن الربيع، في قوله: {ألم تر إلى الذي حاج إبراهيم في ربه أن آتاه الله الملك} [البقرة: 258] قال: «ذكر لنا

TAB-FULL:v4p570/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p570/r1.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v4p570/r1.claim: Al-Suddī identifies the king who disputed with Abraham as Nimrod son of Canaan.
TAB-FULL:v4p570/r1.anchor: عن السدي، قال: «هو نمروذ بن كنعان»

TAB-FULL:v4p570/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p570/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v4p570/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd identifies the disputant as Nimrod.

TAB-FULL:v4p570/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p570/r3.speaker: ابن إسحاق
TAB-FULL:v4p570/r3.claim: Ibn Isḥāq likewise identifies the disputant as Nimrod.
TAB-FULL:v4p570/r3.anchor: ثنا سلمة، عن ابن إسحاق، مثله

TAB-FULL:v4p570/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p570/r4.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
TAB-FULL:v4p570/r4.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam likewise identifies the disputant as Nimrod.

TAB-FULL:v4p570/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p570/r6.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v4p570/r6.claim: Ibn Jurayj identifies him as Nimrod and says he was the first king on earth.
TAB-FULL:v4p570/r6.anchor: قال ابن جريج: " هو نمروذ، ويقال: إنه أول ملك في الأرض "

TAB-FULL:v4p570#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p570#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p570#2/r1.claim: Abraham means that his Lord controls life and death, giving life to whom He wills and causing death after life to whom He wills.
TAB-FULL:v4p570#2/r1.anchor: ربي الذي بيده الحياة والموت يحيي من يشاء ويميت من أراد بعد الإحياء

TAB-FULL:v4p570#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p570#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p570#2/r2.claim: The king’s claim means he spares someone he intended to kill, which is called giving life, and kills another, which is called causing death.
TAB-FULL:v4p570#2/r2.anchor: فأحيي وأميت، استحيي من أردت قتله، فلا أقتله، فيكون ذلك مني إحياء له.

TAB-FULL:v4p570#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p570#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p570#2/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarī supports the Arabic use of “giving life” for saving someone by citing the Qur’anic comparison in 5:32.
TAB-FULL:v4p570#2/r3.anchor: وذلك عند العرب يسمى إحياء، كما قال تعالى ذكره: {ومن أحياها فكأنما أحيا الناس جميعا} [المائدة: 32]

TAB-FULL:v4p570#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p570#2/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p570#2/r4.claim: Abraham challenges the king, if he truly is a god, to bring the sun from the west as God brings it from the east.
TAB-FULL:v4p570#2/r4.anchor: قال إبراهيم صلى الله عليه وسلم: فإن الله الذي هو ربي يأتي بالشمس من مشرقها، فأت بها إن كنت صادقا أنك إله من مغربها

TAB-FULL:v4p570#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p570#2/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p570#2/r5.claim: The disbeliever was confounded, cut off, and left without an argument.
TAB-FULL:v4p570#2/r5.anchor: فبهت الذي كفر} [البقرة: 258] يعني انقطع وبطلت حجته

TAB-FULL:v4p570#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p570#2/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p570#2/r6.claim: Al-Ṭabarī explains bahita-yabhatu as being confounded, notes a variant Arab form bahata with that sense, and distinguishes the use for falsely accusing someone.
TAB-FULL:v4p570#2/r6.anchor: يقال منه: بهت يبهت بهتا، وقد حكي عن بعض العرب أنها تقول بهذا المعنى: بهت، ويقال: بهت الرجل إذا افتريت عليه كذبا

TAB-FULL:v4p570#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p570#2/r7.speaker: بعض القراء
TAB-FULL:v4p570#2/r7.claim: Some reciters are reported to read fa-bahata, making the meaning that the disbeliever confounded Abraham.
TAB-FULL:v4p570#2/r7.anchor: وقد روي عن بعض القراء أنه قرأ: «فبهت الذي كفر» بمعنى: فبهت إبراهيم الذي كفر

TAB-FULL:v4p570#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p570#2/r8.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v4p570#2/r8.claim: Qatāda reports that the king brought two men, killed one, spared the other, and claimed these acts were giving death and life before Abraham posed the sun challenge.
TAB-FULL:v4p570#2/r8.anchor: عن قتادة، في قوله: {إذ قال إبراهيم ربي الذي يحيي ويميت قال أنا أحيي وأميت} [البقرة: 258] " وذكر لنا أنه دعا برجلين، فقتل أحدهما، واستحيا الآخر

TAB-FULL:v4p570#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p570#2/r9.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v4p570#2/r9.claim: Mujāhid explains the king’s claim as killing whomever he chose and sparing whomever he chose.
TAB-FULL:v4p570#2/r9.anchor: عن مجاهد، قال: " أنا أحيي، وأميت: أقتل من شئت وأستحيي من شئت، أدعه حيا فلا أقتله "

TAB-FULL:v4p570#2/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p570#2/r10.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v4p570#2/r10.claim: Mujāhid says four people alone ruled the whole earth: believers Solomon and Dhū al-Qarnayn, and unbelievers Nebuchadnezzar and Nimrod son of Canaan.
TAB-FULL:v4p570#2/r10.anchor: وقال: " ملك الأرض مشرقها ومغربها أربعة نفر مؤمنان وكافران، فالمؤمنان: سليمان بن داود، وذو القرنين، والكافران: بختنصر ونمرود بن كنعان

TAB-FULL:v4p573/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p573/r1.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
TAB-FULL:v4p573/r1.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam recounts that Nimrod denied God after Abraham’s challenge, assembled his forces, and was destroyed by a vast swarm of mosquitoes; one entered his nose and tormented him for 400 years, matching his reign. The story also says he built a tower toward heaven, whose foundations God struck down.
TAB-FULL:v4p573/r1.anchor: عن زيد بن أسلم: " أول جبار كان في الأرض نمروذ، فكان الناس يخرجون فيمتارون من عنده الطعام، فخرج إبراهيم يمتار مع من يمتار

TAB-FULL:v4p573/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p573/r2.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
TAB-FULL:v4p573/r2.claim: In Ibn Zayd’s account, Nimrod ruled at Mosul and had visitors affirm he was their lord to receive food; Abraham instead named the Lord who gives life and death, then challenged Nimrod with the sun, so Nimrod sent him away without provisions.
TAB-FULL:v4p573/r2.anchor: أخبرني عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم، في قول الله: {ألم تر إلى الذي حاج إبراهيم

TAB-FULL:v4p575/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p575/r1.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
TAB-FULL:v4p575/r1.claim: The continuation of Ibn Zayd’s account says Abraham filled sacks with sand so his children would be comforted; Sarah found them full of fine grain, and Abraham recognized it as God’s provision.
TAB-FULL:v4p575/r1.anchor: حتى إذا نظر إلى سواد جبال أهله، قال: ليحزنني صبياي إسماعيل وإسحاق، لو أني ملأت هذين الجوالقين من هذه البطحاء

TAB-FULL:v4p575/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p575/r2.speaker: الربيع
TAB-FULL:v4p575/r2.claim: Al-Rabīʿ says Nimrod demonstrated his claimed power by sparing one of two men and killing the other, then Abraham challenged him to bring the sun from the west.
TAB-FULL:v4p575/r2.anchor: عن الربيع، قال: " لما قال له إبراهيم: {ربي الذي يحيي ويميت} [البقرة: 258] ، قال هو يعني نمروذ: فأنا أحيي وأميت

TAB-FULL:v4p575/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p575/r3.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v4p575/r3.claim: Al-Suddī says that after Abraham left the fire, Nimrod claimed control over life by withholding food and water from four people, then reviving two and letting two die; Abraham shifted to the sun challenge, confounding him. Nimrod called Abraham mad and feared public disgrace.
TAB-FULL:v4p575/r3.anchor: عن السدي، قال: " لما خرج إبراهيم من النار، أدخلوه على الملك، ولم يكن قبل ذلك دخل عليه فكلمه، وقال له: من ربك؟

TAB-FULL:v4p575/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p575/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p575/r4.claim: Al-Ṭabarī connects Abraham’s argument against Nimrod with God’s statement that this was an argument given to Abraham against his people in 6:83.
TAB-FULL:v4p575/r4.anchor: وهو قول الله تعالى ذكره: {وتلك حجتنا آتيناها إبراهيم على قومه} [الأنعام: 83]

TAB-FULL:v4p576/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p576/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p576/r1.claim: Al-Tabari reads the opening as addressing Muhammad: have you not seen the one who disputed with Abraham about his Lord?
TAB-FULL:v4p576/r1.anchor: قال له إبراهيم: ربي الذي يحيي ويميت قال نمروذ: فأنا أحيي وأميت

TAB-FULL:v4p576/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p576/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v4p576/r2.claim: Mujahid says the ruler claimed to give life by sparing one condemned man and death by killing another; Ibn Jurayj explains this was his boast of reviving and killing.
TAB-FULL:v4p576/r2.anchor: عن ابن جريج، قال: أخبرني عبد الله بن كثير، أنه سمع مجاهدا، يقول:

TAB-FULL:v4p576/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p576/r3.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
TAB-FULL:v4p576/r3.claim: With the qualification “God knows best,” Ibn Ishaq reports Nimrod's claim that sparing one condemned man and killing another equaled life and death; Abraham challenged him to reverse the sun's course, leaving him speechless.
TAB-FULL:v4p576/r3.anchor: ثني محمد بن إسحاق، قال: " ذكر لنا والله أعلم أن نمروذ قال لإبراهيم

TAB-FULL:v4p576/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p576/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p576/r4.claim: Al-Tabari identifies the disbeliever as Nimrod and explains that the proof overcame and confounded him.
TAB-FULL:v4p576/r4.anchor: يقول تعالى ذكره: {فبهت الذي كفر} [البقرة: 258] يعني وقعت عليه الحجة، يعني نمروذ

TAB-FULL:v4p577/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p577/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p577/r1.claim: God does not guide disbelievers to an argument that defeats the people of truth: falsehood's arguments fail, and the disbeliever wrongs himself by putting denial where it does not belong.
TAB-FULL:v4p577/r1.anchor: لأن أهل الباطل حججهم داحضة، وقد بينا أن معنى الظلم: وضع الشيء في غير موضعه

TAB-FULL:v4p577/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p577/r2.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
TAB-FULL:v4p577/r2.claim: Ibn Ishaq likewise says God does not guide them in argument during disputation because they are astray.
TAB-FULL:v4p577/r2.anchor: حدثنا ابن حميد، قال: ثنا سلمة، قال: ثني محمد بن إسحاق: {والله لا يهدي القوم الظالمين} [البقرة: 258] «أي لا يهديهم في الحجة عند الخصومة لما هم عليه من الضلالة»

TABATABAI:2:258/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:258/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:258/r1.claim: The passage presents divine unity and therefore relates to what precedes; it may have been revealed together with the preceding verses.
TABATABAI:2:258/r1.anchor: الآيات مشتملة على معنى التوحيد ولذلك كانت غير خالية عن الارتباط بما قبلها من الآيات

TABATABAI:2:258/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:258/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:258/r2.claim: Al-muhajjah is setting proof against proof to establish a claim or refute its opposite; the root sense of hujja is intention, later conventionally a proof for a claim.
TABATABAI:2:258/r2.anchor: المحاجة إلقاء الحجة قبال الحجة لإثبات المدعي أو لإبطال ما يقابله، وأصل الحجة هو القصد

TABATABAI:2:258/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:258/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:258/r3.claim: The phrase fi rabbihi is governed by hajjah, and its pronoun refers to Abraham, as the later words about Abraham's Lord show.
TABATABAI:2:258/r3.anchor: وقوله في ربه متعلق بحاج، والضمير لإبراهيم كما يشعر به قوله تعالى فيما بعد

TABATABAI:2:258/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:258/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:258/r4.claim: The disputant is Nimrod, a Babylonian king contemporary with Abraham, as history and reports state.
TABATABAI:2:258/r4.anchor: وهذا الذي حاج إبراهيم عليه السلام في ربه هو الملك الذي كان يعاصره وهو نمرود من ملوك بابل

TABATABAI:2:258/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:258/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:258/r5.claim: Human beings are innately subject to powers superior to them and effective in their lives, a pattern apparent across past nations and present communities.
TABATABAI:2:258/r5.anchor: إن الإنسان لا يزال خاضعا بحسب الفطرة للقوى المستعلية عليه، المؤثرة فيه

TABATABAI:2:258/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:258/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:258/r6.claim: By innate disposition people affirm a maker who affects the world's creation and governance, whether they are monotheists, polytheists, or deniers; fitra is never falsified, though people may neglect it.
TABATABAI:2:258/r6.anchor: وهو بفطرته يثبت للعالم صانعا مؤثرا فيه بحسب التكوين والتدبير

TABATABAI:2:258/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:258/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:258/r7.claim: Early people analogized from themselves, assigned different events to distinct causes, and consequently posited gods of species and planets, using idols as intermediaries; differing cultures formed differing images and cults.
TABATABAI:2:258/r7.anchor: لما كان يقيس الأشياء إلى نفسه، وكان يرى من نفسه أن أفعاله المختلفة تستند إلى قواه وأعضائه المختلفة

TABATABAI:2:258#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:258#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:258#2/r1.claim: People gradually clung to sensory idols and forgot the beings represented, even the supreme God; powerful rulers exploited popular belief to claim divinity, while their visible power made them seem superior to other gods.
TABATABAI:2:258#2/r1.anchor: وربما انجر الأمر تدريجا إلى التشبث بالأصنام ونسيان أربابها حتى رب الأرباب

TABATABAI:2:258#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:258#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:258#2/r2.claim: Pharaoh's claim to be the highest lord shows that he asserted supremacy while still recognizing other gods.
TABATABAI:2:258#2/r2.anchor: كما يحكيه الله تعالى من قول فرعون لقومه

TABATABAI:2:258#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:258#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:258#2/r3.claim: Nimrod too claimed divinity and superiority over other gods; the author infers this from his claim to give life and death, while Pharaoh's reference to his gods shows the rulers could retain a pantheon.
TABATABAI:2:258#2/r3.anchor: وكذلك كان يدعي نمرود على ما يستفاد من قوله

TABATABAI:2:258#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:258#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:258#2/r4.claim: Nimrod's actual dispute was over exclusive lordship: Abraham said only God was his Lord, while Nimrod claimed to be lord of Abraham and others and worthy of their worship.
TABATABAI:2:258#2/r4.anchor: ومن هنا يستنتج أن المحاجة التي وقعت بينه وبين إبراهيم عليه السلام هي، أن إبراهيم عليه السلام كان يدعي

TABATABAI:2:258#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:258#2/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:258#2/r5.claim: Nimrod's reply means that he himself was the Lord Abraham described; he said أنا أحيي وأميت without a coordinating 'and' because he sought exclusive superiority, not partnership in God's lordship.
TABATABAI:2:258#2/r5.anchor: ولم يقل وأنا أحيي وأميت، لأن لازم العطف أن يشارك الله في ربوبيته

TABATABAI:2:258#2/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:258#2/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:258#2/r6.claim: Nimrod also did not mention the other gods, since his aim was to claim that he alone outranked them.
TABATABAI:2:258#2/r6.anchor: ولم يقل أيضا والآلهة تحيي وتميت

TABATABAI:2:258#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:258#3/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:258#3/r1.claim: Nimrod answers by deception, not a valid counterproof: Abraham meant the observable literal origin and removal of life in conscious, willing creatures.
TABATABAI:2:258#3/r1.anchor: ولم يعارض إبراهيم عليه السلام بالحق، بل بالتمويه والمغالطة وتلبيس الأمر على من حضر

TABATABAI:2:258#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:258#3/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:258#3/r2.claim: The nature of life is unknown, but only a possessor of life can originate it; inert nature and other living beings cannot explain it, since no thing creates or annihilates itself.
TABATABAI:2:258#3/r2.anchor: فإن هذه الحياة المجهولة لكنه لا يستطيع أن يوجدها إلا من هو واجد لها

TABATABAI:2:258#3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:258#3/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:258#3/r3.claim: Nimrod equivocated by taking life and death metaphorically or broadly: he ordered two prisoners brought, killed one, released the other, and presented this as giving death and life.
TABATABAI:2:258#3/r3.anchor: وعند ذلك أمر بإحضار رجلين من السجن فأمر بقتل أحدهما وإطلاق الآخر فقتل هذا واطلق ذاك فقال أنا أحيي وأميت

TABATABAI:2:258#3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:258#3/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:258#3/r4.claim: Abraham could not expose the equivocation because he saw Nimrod's sham and the audience's blind acceptance; he therefore changed to a proof the obstinate opponent could not answer.
TABATABAI:2:258#3/r4.anchor: فوجد أنه لو بين وجه المغالطة لم يصدقه أحد، فعدل إلى حجة أخرى لا يدع المكابر أن يعارضه بشيء

TABATABAI:2:258#3/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:258#3/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:258#3/r5.claim: Even if Nimrod's people treated the sun as a god, its rising and setting ultimately depend on the Lord of lords; a voluntary agent can choose otherwise, so Nimrod must bring it from the west.
TABATABAI:2:258#3/r5.anchor: وذلك ان الشمس وإن كانت من جملة الآلهة عندهم أو عند بعضهم

TABATABAI:2:258#3/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:258#3/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:258#3/r6.claim: Nimrod could not call the sun's regular eastern rising accidental, attribute it to the sun independently of God, or claim to cause it himself; he was silenced and confounded.
TABATABAI:2:258#3/r6.anchor: ما كان يسعه أن يقول إن هذا الأمر المستمر الجاري على وتيرة واحدة وهو طلوعها من المشرق دائما أمر اتفاقي

TABATABAI:2:258#4/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:258#4/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:258#4/r1.claim: The phrase an atahu Allah al-mulk has an omitted lām of causation, and uses a favor as the apparent cause of Nimrod's aggression to express complaint and accusation.
TABATABAI:2:258#4/r1.anchor: الجملة أعني قوله أن آتاه الله الملك بتقدير لام التعليل

TABATABAI:2:258#4/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:258#4/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:258#4/r2.claim: Nimrod's tyranny should have been attributed to the opposite of divine beneficence, but only God's kindness and gift of kingship is named, exposing his ingratitude.
TABATABAI:2:258#4/r2.anchor: فإن عدوان نمرود وطغيانه في هذه المحاجة كان ينبغي أن يعلل بضد إنعام الله عليه

TABATABAI:2:258#4/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:258#4/r3.speaker: الشاعر
TABATABAI:2:258#4/r3.claim: The cited verse says the sons repaid Abu al-Ghaylan's advanced age and good deed as Sanmar was repaid, illustrating the ironic reversal of kindness.
TABATABAI:2:258#4/r3.anchor: جزى بنوه أبا الغيلان عن كبر وحسن فعل كما يجزى سنمار

TABATABAI:2:258#4/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:258#4/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:258#4/r4.claim: The same reversal appears in Pharaoh's family taking Moses as a child so that he would become their enemy and grief.
TABATABAI:2:258#4/r4.anchor: فهو بوجه كقوله تعالى فالتقطه آل فرعون ليكون لهم عدوا وحزنا

TABATABAI:2:258#4/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:258#4/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:258#4/r5.claim: Another purpose of mentioning the gift is to expose the claim's weakness: Nimrod's authority came from God, and as a person he was otherwise unremarkable, hence the text leaves him unnamed.
TABATABAI:2:258#4/r5.anchor: إنما كان نمرود الملك ذا السلطة والسطوة بنعمة من ربه

TABATABAI:2:258#4/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:258#4/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:258#4/r6.claim: Kingship is a divinely bestowed capacity and innate human aspiration: used rightly it brings felicity, but exceeding its bounds turns it into ruin.
TABATABAI:2:258#4/r6.anchor: فإن الملك وهو نوع سلطنة منبسطة على الأمة كسائر أنواع السلطنة والقدرة نعمة من الله وفضل يؤتيه من يشاء

TABATABAI:2:258#4/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:258#4/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:258#4/r7.claim: Attributing a thing to God is appropriate from its good aspect, not its evil or harmful aspect.
TABATABAI:2:258#4/r7.anchor: لكل شيء نسبة إليه تعالى على ما يليق بساحة قدسه تعالى وتقدس من جهة الحسن الذي فيه دون جهة القبح

TABATABAI:2:258#4/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:258#4/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:258#4/r8.claim: The author rejects exegetes who take the pronoun in 'that God gave him kingship' to refer to Abraham and the kingship to be Abraham's.
TABATABAI:2:258#4/r8.anchor: ومن هنا يظهر سقوط ما ذكره بعض المفسرين ان الضمير في قوله أن آتاه الله الملك،

TABATABAI:2:258#5/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:258#5/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:258#5/r1.claim: Abraham did not argue from the world's dependence on its creator as he had when first recognizing God, because the people could not understand that proof adequately; their misunderstanding of his simpler life-and-death argument shows this.
TABATABAI:2:258#5/r1.anchor: فإن القوم على اعترافهم بذلك بفطرتهم إجمالا كانوا أنزل سطحا من أن يعقلوه على ما ينبغي أن يعقل عليه

TABATABAI:2:258#5/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:258#5/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:258#5/r2.claim: Nimrod means, 'I am your Lord,' the one who possesses the life-and-death power Abraham attributed to his Lord.
TABATABAI:2:258#5/r2.anchor: أي فأنا ربك الذي وصفته بأنه يحيي ويميت

TABATABAI:2:258#5/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:258#5/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:258#5/r3.claim: After the first proof was twisted, Abraham builds the solar challenge on Nimrod's own claim, signaled by fa; he says Allah rather than 'my Lord' to block another misapplication of the wording.
TABATABAI:2:258#5/r3.anchor: إلا أنه بنى هذه الحجة الثانية على دعوى الخصم في الحجة الأولى كما يدل عليه التفريع بالفاء

TABATABAI:2:258#5/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:258#5/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:258#5/r4.claim: The final clause explains Nimrod's defeat: God did not guide him, so he was confounded; it does not say lack of guidance caused his disbelief, and the context concerns the debate.
TABATABAI:2:258#5/r4.anchor: وبعبارة أخرى معناه أن الله لم يهده فبهت لذلك ولو هداه لغلب على إبراهيم في الحجة

TABATABAI:2:258#5/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:258#5/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:258#5/r5.claim: Calling them wrongdoers suggests that their wrongdoing is the cause of God's withholding guidance, as in other occurrences of this Qur'anic wording.
TABATABAI:2:258#5/r5.anchor: ومن هنا يظهر أن في الوصف إشعارا بالعلية أعني أن السبب لعدم هداية الله الظالمين هو ظلمهم

TUSTARI:2:258/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:2:258/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:2:258/r1.claim: One reading has Abraham wish to witness God giving life and death so that, when challenged, he could answer with certainty; direct witnessing reassures the heart.
TUSTARI:2:258/r1.anchor: فيطمئن قلبي إلى الإجابة بنعم إذا شاهدت ذلك

TUSTARI:2:258/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:2:258/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TUSTARI:2:258/r2.claim: The Prophet is cited to affirm that direct witnessing is not like receiving a report.
TUSTARI:2:258/r2.anchor: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

TUSTARI:2:258/r3.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:2:258/r3.speaker: author
TUSTARI:2:258/r3.claim: Another reading is that Abraham asked to see the dead restored to life as reassurance that God had taken him as an intimate friend.
TUSTARI:2:258/r3.anchor: أنه سأله أن يريه إحياء الموتى طمأنينة له في أنه اتخذ خليلا

TUSTARI:2:258/r4.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:2:258/r4.speaker: author
TUSTARI:2:258/r4.claim: A further reading makes this the elect's stance: asking God earns no claim on Him beyond what He makes real, and Abraham sought the revival of the dead to reassure his heart.
TUSTARI:2:258/r4.anchor: أن سؤالي إياك لا أستحق به عليك إلا ما تحققه لي، وذلك موقف الخواص من خلقه

TABRISI:2:258/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:258/r1.speaker: أهل المدينة
TABRISI:2:258/r1.claim: The people of Medina retain the alif in ana when the following word begins with hamza carrying fatḥa or ḍamma; before hamza with kasra, readers unanimously drop it.
TABRISI:2:258/r1.anchor: قرأ أهل المدينة أنا أحيي بإثبات الألف في أنا والمد إذا كان بعدها همزة مضمومة

TABRISI:2:258/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:258/r2.speaker: author
