TABRISI:2:258/r2.claim: The alif of ana is originally a pause marker, like the pause hāʾ in muslimūnah, and normally drops in connected speech.
TABRISI:2:258/r2.anchor: الأصل في أنا الهمزة والنون وإنما يلحقها الألف في الوقف كما أن الهاء تلحق للوقف

TABRISI:2:258/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:258/r3.speaker: الأعشى
TABRISI:2:258/r3.claim: Al-Aʿsha and another poet give examples of retaining the alif of ana in connected speech.
TABRISI:2:258/r3.anchor: نحو قول الأعشى: فكيف أنا وانتحال القوافي

TABRISI:2:258/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:258/r4.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:2:258/r4.claim: Abu Ali knows no distinction between hamza and other letters that would justify retaining an alif normally used only at pause.
TABRISI:2:258/r4.anchor: قال أبو علي وما روي في إثبات الألف في أنا إذا كان بعد الألف همزة

TABRISI:2:258/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:258/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:258/r5.claim: Buhita has four Arabic forms; the passive form buhita is the most eloquent and the reading used here.
TABRISI:2:258/r5.anchor: في بهت أربع لغات بهت على وزن ظرف وبهت على وزن حذر وبهت على وزن ذهب

TABRISI:2:258/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:258/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:258/r6.claim: Buhita means to be stopped and bewildered; the active verb can also mean confronting someone with a lie, since a defeated liar is confounded by proof.
TABRISI:2:258/r6.anchor: يقال بهت الرجل يبهت بهتا إذا انقطع وتحير

TABRISI:2:258/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:258/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:258/r7.claim: The root links bewilderment under proof with false accusation; the same word appears in 4:20.
TABRISI:2:258/r7.anchor: فالبهت الحيرة عند استيلاء الحجة لأنها كالحيرة للمواجه بالكذب

TABRISI:2:258/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:258/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:258/r8.claim: “Have you not seen” uses ila to express wonder at the disbeliever’s extraordinary false argument; sight reaches an unusual endpoint, almost functioning like a simile marker.
TABRISI:2:258/r8.anchor: إنما أدخلت إلى في الكلام للتعجب من حال الكافر المحاج بالباطل

TABRISI:2:258/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:258/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:258/r9.claim: After describing God as believers’ patron and the disbelievers’ patron as taghut, the passage consoles the Prophet with Abraham’s story.
TABRISI:2:258/r9.anchor: لما بين تعالى أنه ولي المؤمنين وإن الكفار لا ولي لهم سوى الطاغوت تسلية لنبيه

TABRISI:2:258/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:258/r10.speaker: مجاهد وغيره
TABRISI:2:258/r10.claim: The disputant is Nimrod son of Canaan, whom Mujahid and others call the first tyrant and claimant to divinity.
TABRISI:2:258/r10.anchor: وهو نمرود بن كنعان وهو أول من تجبر وادعى الربوبية عن مجاهد وغيره

TABRISI:2:258/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:258/r11.speaker: الصادق
TABRISI:2:258/r11.claim: Al-Sadiq places the dispute before Abraham’s idols were broken and before he was thrown into the fire made cool and safe for him.
TABRISI:2:258/r11.anchor: عند كسر الأصنام قبل إلقائه في النار وجعلها عليه بردا وسلاما عن الصادق

TABRISI:2:258/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:258/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:258/r12.claim: “About his Lord” means the Lord of Abraham, who called people to divine unity and worship.
TABRISI:2:258/r12.anchor: أي: في رب إبراهيم الذي يدعو إلى توحيده وعبادته

TABRISI:2:258#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:258#2/r1.speaker: الحسن والجبائي
TABRISI:2:258#2/r1.claim: Al-Hasan and al-Jubbaʾi take the pronoun as Nimrod: God gave him worldly rule and abundant wealth, and arrogance over this favor drove him to challenge Abraham.
TABRISI:2:258#2/r1.anchor: الهاء من أتاه تعود إلى المحاج لإبراهيم أي أعطاه الله الملك وهو نعيم الدنيا وسعة المال

TABRISI:2:258#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:258#2/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:258#2/r2.claim: Worldly kingship may be granted to anyone, but God entrusts lawful rule, command, and binding obedience only to someone who calls to righteousness, never to a known corrupter.
TABRISI:2:258#2/r2.anchor: فأما الملك بتمليك الأمر والنهي وتدبير أمور الناس وإيجاب الطاعة على الخلق فلا يجوز

TABRISI:2:258#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:258#2/r3.speaker: أبو القاسم البلخي
TABRISI:2:258#2/r3.claim: Abu al-Qasim al-Balkhi takes the pronoun to refer to Abraham; Nimrod’s imprisoning and releasing people were coercive, while lawful authority belonged to Abraham from God.
TABRISI:2:258#2/r3.anchor: إلى إبراهيم عن أبي القاسم البلخي

TABRISI:2:258#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:258#2/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:258#2/r4.claim: The speech omits Nimrod’s question, “Who is your Lord?”, to which Abraham answers that his Lord gives life and death.
TABRISI:2:258#2/r4.anchor: في الكلام حذف وهو إذ قال له نمرود من ربك فقال ربي الذي يحيي ويميت

TABRISI:2:258#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:258#2/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:258#2/r5.claim: Life is named first as God’s first blessing; giving life and taking the soul without bodily injury or an action upon the body exceed human power and belong to God.
TABRISI:2:258#2/r5.anchor: بدأ بذكر الحياة لأنها أول نعمة ينعم الله بها على خلقه ثم يميتهم

TABRISI:2:258#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:258#2/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:258#2/r6.claim: Nimrod claimed to give life by releasing a condemned prisoner and cause death by execution; this confuses words with creating life and death, which only God can do.
TABRISI:2:258#2/r6.anchor: أنا أحيي بالتخلية من الحبس من وجب عليه القتل وأميت بالقتل

TABRISI:2:258#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:258#2/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:258#2/r7.claim: One explanation says Abraham did not abandon his first proof: a wise speaker may add a confirming argument once the initial proof is complete and no effective objection remains.
TABRISI:2:258#2/r7.anchor: إيراد حجة أخرى على سبيل التأكيد بعد تمام ما ابتدأ به

TABRISI:2:258#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:258#2/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:258#2/r8.claim: Another explanation says Abraham chose the clearer sign because listeners might mistake life and death for ordinary acts; prophets clarify truth rather than merely seek debate victory.
TABRISI:2:258#2/r8.anchor: أن إبراهيم إنما قال ذلك ليبين أن من شأن من يقدر

TABRISI:2:258#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:258#2/r9.speaker: الصادق
TABRISI:2:258#2/r9.claim: Al-Sadiq says Abraham first challenged Nimrod to revive someone he had killed if truthful, then overcame him with the sun challenge.
TABRISI:2:258#2/r9.anchor: عن الصادق ع أن إبراهيم ع قال له

TABRISI:2:258#2/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:258#2/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:258#2/r10.claim: The disbeliever was confounded when the decisive proof became manifest and he could not answer.
TABRISI:2:258#2/r10.anchor: أي تحير عند الانقطاع بما بان

TABRISI:2:258#2/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:258#2/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:258#2/r11.claim: One answer to why Nimrod did not ask Abraham’s Lord to bring the sun from the west is that he knew the miracle would affirm Abraham and expose him further.
TABRISI:2:258#2/r11.anchor: لما علم بما رأى من الآيات أنه لو اقترح ذلك

TABRISI:2:258#2/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:258#2/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:258#2/r12.claim: A second answer is that God forsook Nimrod and favored Abraham, leaving Nimrod unable to produce even a specious objection.
TABRISI:2:258#2/r12.anchor: أن الله خذله ولطف لإبراهيم حتى إنه لم يأت بشبهة

TABRISI:2:258#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:258#3/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:258#3/r1.claim: One reading is that God does not assist wrongdoers in reaching their corrupt aims.
TABRISI:2:258#3/r1.anchor: بالمعونة على بلوغ البغية من الفساد

TABRISI:2:258#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:258#3/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:258#3/r2.claim: Another reading is that God does not guide wrongdoers in argument as He guides His prophets and friends.
TABRISI:2:258#3/r2.anchor: لا يهديهم إلى المحاجة كما يهدي أنبياءه وأولياءه

TABRISI:2:258#3/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:258#3/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:258#3/r3.claim: A third reading is that God withholds His grace and support once He knows no gracious aid will benefit them.
TABRISI:2:258#3/r3.anchor: لا يهديهم بألطافه وتأييده إذا علم أنه لا لطف لهم

TABRISI:2:258#3/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:258#3/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:258#3/r4.claim: A fourth reading takes the phrase to mean that God does not guide them to Paradise.
TABRISI:2:258#3/r4.anchor: لا يهديهم إلى الجنة وهذا لا يعارض قوله

TABRISI:2:258#3/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:258#3/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:258#3/r5.claim: This does not contradict that God guided Thamud: guidance has several senses, some general to all responsible people and some specific to believers, as explained at 2:26 and 41:17.
TABRISI:2:258#3/r5.anchor: معاني الهداية ووجوهها قبل عند قوله يضل به كثير ويهدى به كثيرا

TABRISI:2:258#3/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:258#3/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:258#3/r6.claim: The disputation shows that knowledge of the Creator is not innate or necessary; otherwise argument to establish the Creator would have no force.
TABRISI:2:258#3/r6.anchor: دلالة على أن المعارف غير ضرورية إذ لو كانت كذلك لما صحت المحاجة

TABRISI:2:258#3/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:258#3/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:258#3/r7.claim: The verse rejects blind imitation and affirms rational argument.
TABRISI:2:258#3/r7.anchor: دلالة على فساد التقليد وحسن الحجاج

TABRISI:2:258#3/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:258#3/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:258#3/r8.claim: God is known through His acts that no one else can perform.
TABRISI:2:258#3/r8.anchor: وأنه تعالى إنما يعلم بأفعاله التي لا يقدر عليها غيره

TABRISI:2:258#3/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:258#3/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:2:258#3/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas says God sent a mosquito against Nimrod; it entered his nostril and brain, tormented him for forty nights, and killed him.
TABRISI:2:258#3/r9.anchor: وفي تفسير ابن عباس: أن الله سبحانه سلط على نمرود بعوضة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p373/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p373/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p373/r1.claim: The phrase means because God gave him kingship: the man disputed with Abraham because of the dominion, which made him arrogant.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p373/r1.anchor: أي: لأن أتاه الله، وتأويله: ألم تر إلى الذي حاج إبراهيم في ربه للملك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p373/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p373/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p373/r2.claim: When Abraham spoke, he answered an unstated question, namely who is your Lord? The answer makes the question understood and it is omitted.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p373/r2.anchor: هذا جواب سؤال سابق غير مذكور، وتقديره (¬3): إذ قال له: من ربك؟

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p373/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p373/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p373/r3.claim: The enemy shifts to verbal equivocation, substituting ordinary killing and sparing for God’s creative power to give life and death.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p373/r3.anchor: اعتمد عدو الله على المعارضة على الإشراك (¬7) في العبادة (¬8) في العبارة، عادلا عن وجه الحجة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p373/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p373/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p373/r4.claim: An unnamed report says the king summoned two men, killed one and spared the other, then called sparing the man giving life.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p373/r4.anchor: لأنه روي أنه دعا برجلين؛ فقتل أحدهما واستحيا الآخر، فسمى ترك القتل إحياء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p373/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p373/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p373/r5.claim: Readers omit the alif of ana in connected recitation; only a report from Nafiʿ retains it before hamza, and the author calls omission correct.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p373/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p373/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p373/r6.claim: The pronoun’s letters are hamza and nūn; its alif is added only in pause, like pausal hāʾ, and drops in connection as with hamzat al-waṣl.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p373/r6.anchor: لأن (أنا) ضمير المتكلم، والاسم الهمزة والنون، فأما الألف فإنما تلحقها في الوقف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p373/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p373/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p373/r7.claim: Nafiʿ’s connected alif is very weak because it treats connection as pause; such forms are poetic necessities, not appropriate in Qurʾanic recitation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p373/r7.anchor: وأما قراءة نافع فهي ضعيفة جدا (¬8)، لأنه أجرى الوصل مجرى الوقف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p375/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p375/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p375/r1.claim: Poets extend pause forms into connected speech for meter or rhyme, as in the pausal hāʾ examples; this license does not apply outside poetry.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p375/r1.anchor: الهاء فيه هاء الوقف التي تلحق في: مسلمونه وصالحونه، فألحق الهاء حرف اللين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p375/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p375/r2.speaker: الأعشى
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p375/r2.claim: Al-Aʿsha’s verse retains the alif of ana in connected speech, illustrating poetic license.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p375/r2.anchor: فمما (¬1) جاءت ألف (أنا) مثبته فيه وصلا من الشعر قول الأعشى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p375/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p375/r3.speaker: الكسائي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p375/r3.claim: A verse transmitted by al-Kisaʾi also retains the alif of ana as poetic license.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p375/r3.anchor: وما أنشده الكسائي: أنا شيخ العشيرة فاعرفوني

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p375/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p375/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p375/r4.claim: A further unnamed poem retains the alif of ana before a line break.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p375/r4.anchor: وقول آخر: أنا عبيد الله ينميني عمر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p375/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p375/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p375/r5.claim: Abraham could have demanded that the king revive his victim, but instead ends the dispute with an unanswerable proof that exposes inability and models argument against equivocation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p375/r5.anchor: إنما انتقل إبراهيم من الحجة الأولى مع إمكانه أن يناقضه بأن يقول له: أحيي من قتلته

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p375/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p375/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p375/r6.claim: If the king objected that Abraham’s Lord should bring the sun from the west, he had seen Abraham survive the fire; another view says God prevented the objection to aid His prophet.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p375/r6.anchor: فإن قيل: كان للنمرود أن يقول لإبراهيم: فليأت بها ربك من المغرب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p378/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p378/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p378/r1.claim: The root originally means confronting someone with a false accusation; bewilderment under decisive proof is figuratively called bahat because it resembles the accused person's confusion. ʿUrwa's verse uses it for being stunned and falling silent.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p378/r1.anchor: فما هو إلا أن أراها فجاءة ... فأبهت حتى ما أكاد أجيب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p378/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p378/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p378/r2.claim: The verb has three forms: bahita with passive participle mabhuut, and the alternatives bahata and bahuta.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p378/r2.anchor: وفيه ثلاث لغات: بهت الرجل فهو مبهوت، وبهت، وبهت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p378/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p378/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p378/r3.claim: Here the disbeliever was defeated by the argument, stopped speaking, and fell silent.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p378/r3.anchor: وتأويل قوله (¬4): فبهت أي: انقطع وسكت

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p93#5/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p93#5/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p93#5/r1.claim: The ruler disputed with Abraham because God had given him kingship; he became impressed with himself and his power.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p93#5/r1.anchor: أي: حاجه لأن آتاه الله الملك؛ فأعجب بنفسه وملكه فقال: {أنا أحيي وأميت}

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p93#5/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p93#5/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p93#5/r2.claim: His claim to give life means pardoning someone liable to execution; to give death means killing whomever he chooses.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p93#5/r2.anchor: أي: أعفو عمن استحق القتل فأحييه؛ و "أميت": أقتل من أريد قتله فيموت.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p93#5/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p93#5/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p93#5/r3.claim: Buhita means that the disbeliever's argument was cut off.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p93#5/r3.anchor: فبهت الذي كفر} أي: انقطعت حجته.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:258/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:258/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:258/r1.claim: The opening asks whether one has seen the dispute and its proof.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:258/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:258/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:258/r2.claim: To dispute means to argue and quarrel; the king asked Abraham who his Lord was.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:258/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:258/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:258/r3.claim: The kingdom God gave him made him arrogant and provoked the dispute; the king was Nimrod son of Canaan.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:258/r3.anchor: يريد: بطر الملك حمله على ذلك، وهو نمروذ بن كنعان

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:258/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:258/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:258/r4.claim: Abraham identified his Lord as the one who gives life and death; the enemy merely echoed the wording without actually causing life or death.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:258/r4.anchor: فقال عدو الله: { أنا أحيي وأميت } فعارضه بالاشتراك

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:258/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:258/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:258/r5.claim: When Nimrod blurred the argument by claiming the same power, Abraham gave an argument Nimrod could not imitate: command the sun to rise from the west.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:258/r5.anchor: فلما لبس في الحجة بأن قال: أنا أفعل ذلك

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:258/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:258/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:258/r6.claim: Nimrod was confounded and fell silent before Abraham’s challenge.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:258/r6.anchor: فبهت الذي كفر } أي: انقطع وسكت

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:258/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:258/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:258/r1.claim: People are tested by poverty and by wealth and power; those resisting religion often forget the source of their privilege, claim self-sufficiency or divine powers, and exploit the weak.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:258/r1.anchor: İnsanlar yokluk ve yoksullukla imtihan edildikleri gibi varlık ve iktidar verilerek de imtihan edilirler.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:258/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:258/r2.speaker: bazı kaynaklar
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:258/r2.claim: Some sources identify the ruler in Abraham’s time as Nimrod, founder of Babylon and builder of its tower.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:258/r2.anchor: bazı kaynaklar bunun, Bâbil şehrini kuran ve kulesini yapan Nemrud olduğunu kaydetmiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:258/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:258/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:258/r3.claim: God-given wealth and power led Nimrod-like rulers to unbelief and oppression, while David and Solomon used such gifts for gratitude and service to God’s servants.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:258/r3.anchor: Bu nimet ve imkânlar, Nemrud gibilerinde inkâra ve zulme, Dâvûd ve Süleyman aleyhisselâm gibilerinde ise şükre ve Allah’ın kullarına hizmet etmeye vesile olmaktadır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:258/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:258/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:258/r4.claim: Nimrod knew he lacked the real power to kill and give life, but used sophistry to oppose Abraham’s call out of attachment to sovereignty and fear of losing his oppressive rule.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:258/r4.anchor: Şüphe yok ki Nemrud insanları öldürme ve diriltme gücüne sahip bulunmadığını bilmektedir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:258/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:258/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:258/r5.claim: Nimrod equivocated by calling pardon of a condemned prisoner “giving life” and execution of an innocent person “killing the living,” or claimed divine acts as his own despite knowing he had no part in them.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:258/r5.anchor: Nemrud, idam mahkûmunu affetmeyi “insanı diriltmek”, suçsuz bir insanı idam ettirmeyi de “diriyi öldürmek” sayarak

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:258/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:258/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:258/r6.claim: God’s giving life and death has a different, true meaning: neither Nimrod nor anyone else can truly resurrect or kill, or escape death when their time comes.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:258/r6.anchor: rabbin hayat vermesi ve öldürmesinin mânası başkadır ve bu mânada Nemrud da, başkaları da ne diriltmeye ne de öldürmeye kadirdirler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:258/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:258/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:258/r7.claim: Seeing that the life-and-death dispute was hard to resolve, Abraham moved to a second proof based on an observable fact.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:258/r7.anchor: tartışmada sonuç almanın güçlüğünü gören Hz. İbrâhim, herkesin gözleriyle gördüğü bir vâkıadan hareket ederek ikinci bir delil getirmiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:258/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:258/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:258/r8.claim: The sunrise in the east and sunset in the west predated Nimrod, so he could not claim to cause them; if his claim were true, he could reverse their directions.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:258/r8.anchor: Güneşin doğudan doğması ve batıda kaybolması te’vil götürmez bir gerçektir. Nemrud’dan önce de bu böyle olduğundan

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:258/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:258/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:258/r9.claim: Abraham challenged Nimrod to make the sun rise from the west; Nimrod had no answer, exposing his claim as false.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:258/r9.anchor: Hz. İbrâhim de bunu teklif etmiş, Nemrud söyleyecek söz bulamamış ve iddiasının asılsız olduğu ayan beyan ortaya çıkmıştır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:258/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:258/r10.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:258/r10.claim: The account shows that debate is permissible to persuade people about religion or defend belief, and the authors say kalām arose from such debates.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:258/r10.anchor: din ve inanç konusunda insanları ikna etmek veya inancı savunmak için tartışma yapmanın câiz olduğunu göstermektedir. Kelâm ilmi de işte bu nevi tartışmalardan doğmuştur

BURHAN:v4p112/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p112/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p112/r4.claim: “Or like the one” coordinates a genitive phrase with the phrase governed by ilā according to meaning, since “Have you seen the one?” means “Have you seen someone like him?”
BURHAN:v4p112/r4.anchor: عطف المجرور بالكاف على المجرور ب إلى حملا على المعنى لان قوله إلى الذي في معنى

BURHAN:v4p112/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p112/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p112/r7.claim: Conjunction normally marks difference, but a thing can be coordinated with itself when the purpose is emphasis.
BURHAN:v4p112/r7.anchor: الاصل في العطف التغاير وقد يعطف الشئ على نفسه في مقام التاكيد

BURHAN:v4p112/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p112/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p112/r8.claim: In a long account of dialogue, successive “he said” clauses can omit waw or fa; the author cites Abraham’s debate and Pharaoh’s exchange.
BURHAN:v4p112/r8.anchor: يجوز في الحكاية عن المخاطبين اذا طالت قال زيد قال عمرو من غير إن تاتي بالواو وبالفاء

BURHAN:v1p45/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p45/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p45/r3.claim: The story of Abraham’s opponent is joined to the passerby’s story because ألم تر functions like “Have you seen someone like the one who…?” and thus supplies the needed parallel for conjunction.
BURHAN:v1p45/r3.anchor: ووجه ما بينهما من المشابهة أن

ITQAN:v4p359/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p359/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p359/r4.claim: الانتقال switches to a new proof when an opponent misses or evades the first: Abraham moves from the life-and-death argument to the sunrise challenge, which leaves the ruler speechless.
ITQAN:v4p359/r4.anchor: فانقطع الجبار وبهت ولم يمكنه أن يقول أنا الآتي بها من المشرق

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p222/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p222/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p222/r1.claim: Because al-Nābigha speaks in daylight after invoking daylight’s catching him, the apt parallel is the expected night arriving after that day and reaching him anywhere.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p222/r1.anchor: إذا كان يكلمه وهو في النهار بعد أن يضرب المثل بإدراك النهار له وكان الظاهر أن يمثل بإدراك الليل

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p222/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p222/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p222/r2.claim: Comparing a benefaction to the sun chiefly conveys its universality; its comfort and brightness for hearts are secondary associations that can also be made primary in familiar praise.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p222/r2.anchor: وههنا شىء آخر وهو أن تشبيه النعمة في البيت بالشمس وإن كان من حيث الغرض الخاص وهو الدلالة على العموم

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p222/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p222/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p222/r3.claim: Calling a praised person’s anger ‘night’ is disliked because darkness and gloom make it naturally blameworthy; instead say day becomes night for the one he angers.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p222/r3.anchor: وليس كذلك الحكم في الليل لأن تجريده لوصف الممدوح بالسخط مستكره حتى لو قلت أنت في حال السخط ليل

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p222/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p222/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p222/r4.claim: ‘You are my night and day’ can praise the beloved as the one who makes the world light or dark through approval and anger.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p222/r4.anchor: وقد يقول الرجل لمحبوبه أنت ليلي ونهاري أي بك تضئ الدنيا وتظلم

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p232/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p232/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p232/r1.claim: Reading the poem as if it merely omitted مثل before moon, willow, amber, and gazelle reduces its expression to banal comparison and strips away its rhetorical force.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p232/r1.anchor: نخرج إلى الغثاثة ، وإلى شيء يعزل البلاغة عن سلطانها ، ويخفض من شأنها

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p232/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p232/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p232/r2.claim: The metaphor uses expansive hyperbole: the she-camel is imagined as wholly embodied by the qualities of coming and going, rather than as a plain omitted-noun construction.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p232/r2.anchor: أن تجعل الناقة كأنها قد صارت بجملتها إقبالا وإدبارا

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p232/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p232/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p232/r3.claim: He rejects treating the poem as though it had literally been composed with the full underlying phrase, unlike the idiomatic example about mistaking a camel's groan for a doe's call.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p232/r3.anchor: فأما أن يكون الشعر الآن موضوعا على إرادة ذلك ، وعلى تنزيله منزلة المنطوق به

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p274/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p274/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p274/r1.claim: The order of 'قفا نبك' depends on its grammatical meanings: the verb answers the command, من governs ذكرى, and the following genitive and coordination complete the relations.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p274/r1.anchor: كون ' نبك ' جوابا للأمر ، وكون ' من ' معدية له إلى ' ذكرى '

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p274/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p274/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p274/r2.claim: An intended arrangement must realize a particular form that would fail if elements were moved; its design is achieved in meanings, not in the words themselves, while meter is outside this argument.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p274/r2.anchor: ليس ذلك في الألفاظ وإنما الذي يتصور أن يكون مقصودا في الألفاظ هو الوزن

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p306/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p306/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p306/r1.claim: The unity of a verse is unity among its meanings, not a fusion of its words; in Bashshar's line, syntax creates it through the subject of كأن, its attached phrase, coordination, and a predicative noun phrase qualified by a clause.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p306/r1.anchor: لم نجدها اتحدت إلا بأن جعل مثار النقع اسم كأن ، وجعل الظرف الذي هو ' فوق رؤوسنا ' معمولا لمثار

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p306/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p306/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p306/r2.claim: Imagining inner speech while thinking does not prove that thought is in words, just as mentally picturing a seen object does not make it physically present or currently seen.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p306/r2.anchor: كما لا يوجب هذا أن يكون رائيا له ، وأن يكون الشيء موجودا في نفسه

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p306/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p306/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p306/r3.claim: Human thought concerns intelligible relations—predicating, describing, relating, sharing or excluding a judgment, and making one existence conditional on another—which exceed the wording.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p306/r3.anchor: وهذا كله فكر في أمور معلومة معقولة زائدة على اللفظ

DAMGHANI:v1p78/r4.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p78/r4.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p78/r4.claim: In the debate with Abraham, buht means being dazed and confounded; al-mabḥūt is the bewildered person.

BURHAN:v1p102/r16.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p102/r16.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p102/r16.claim: Here God's not guiding wrongdoers means not guiding them to the proof in Abraham's argument.

BURHAN:v1p155/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p155/r9.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p155/r9.claim: The unnamed disputant who argued with Abraham is Nimrod, identified as the king to whom the message was sent.

BURHAN:v3p299/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p299/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p299/r3.claim: Nimrod’s claim to give life and death was sophistry: he killed one man and released another.
BURHAN:v3p299/r3.anchor: وكذلك قول نمروذ ﴿ أنا أحيي وأميت ﴾ 2 أتى باثنين فقتل أحدهما وأرسل الآخرة فإن هذه مغالطة

BURHAN:v4p227/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p227/r9.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p227/r9.claim: The source gives أن the sense إذ with a past verb, though it also reports a causal reading for بل عجبوا أن جاءهم; with a present verb it reports “when you believe,” but prefers مصدرية.

BURHAN:v4p227/r10.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p227/r10.speaker: الزمخشري
BURHAN:v4p227/r10.claim: Al-Zamakhshari allows أن to substitute for a time adverb like ما, and cites Ibrahim’s debate with the king after God gave him sovereignty.
BURHAN:v4p227/r10.anchor: واجاز الزمخشري إن تقع إن مثل ما

BURHAN:v3p176/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p176/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p176/r1.claim: The examples يحيي ويميت and Moses’ question about worshipping what neither hears nor sees omit objects because the point is God’s power to give life and death and the idol’s lack of senses.
BURHAN:v3p176/r1.anchor: والمراد أن الله تعالى له الإحياء والإماتة وأن إلههم ليس له سمع ولا بصر

BURHAN:v2p339/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p339/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p339/r3.claim: An interrogative may function as an alerting command: reflect on these matters and take heed, as in several ألم تر passages.
BURHAN:v2p339/r3.anchor: الخامس التنبيه وهو من أقسام الأمر كقوله تعالى ﴿ ألم تر إلى الذي حاج إبراهيم في ربه ﴾

ITQAN:v2p410/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p410/r12.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p410/r12.claim: In the passage about Abraham’s dispute, huda means a proof or argument: God does not give the wrongdoers an argument.
ITQAN:v2p410/r12.anchor: 12 والحجة ﴿ لا يهدي القوم الظالمين ﴾ بعد قوله تعالى ﴿ ألم تر إلى الذي حاج إبراهيم في ربه ﴾ أي لا يهديهم حجة

ITQAN:v4p384/r16.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p384/r16.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p384/r16.claim: Abraham’s disputant is Nimrod ibn Canaan.

ITQAN:v3p134/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p134/r9.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p134/r9.claim: Qasr qalb corrects a mistaken attribution: the statement my Lord gives life and death answers Nimrod, who claimed that he did so.
ITQAN:v3p134/r9.anchor: خوطب به نمرود الذي اعتقد أنه هو المحيي المميت دون الله

ITQAN:v2p543#2/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p543#2/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p543#2/r6.claim: The majority read fa-buhita passively; active readings are also given in the patterns of ḍaraba, ʿalima, and ḥasuna.
ITQAN:v2p543#2/r6.anchor: ﴿ فبهت الذي كفر ﴾ قراءة الجماعة بالبناء للمفعول وقرئ بالبناء للفاعل بوزن ضرب وعلم وحسن

DAMGHANI:v1p472/r16.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p472/r16.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p472/r16.claim: The phrase ‘does not guide’ can mean does not guide to the proof or argument.
DAMGHANI:v1p472/r16.anchor: الثاني عشر لا يهدي يعني إلى الحجة قوله تعالى في سورة البقرة فبهت الذي كفر والله لا يهدي القوم الظالمين

NASHR:v2p236/r27.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p236/r27.speaker: حمزة
NASHR:v2p236/r27.claim: Ḥamza gives the yāʾ in ربي sukūn.

NASHR:v2p170/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p170/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p170/r1.claim: Across fourteen disputed yāʾs before hamzat waṣl plus the definite article, Ḥamza alone sukunizes every yāʾ.
NASHR:v2p170/r1.anchor: والمختلف فيه من ذلك أربع عشرة ياء: في البقرة ثنتان لا ينال عهدي الظالمين،

NASHR:v2p170/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p170/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p170/r5.claim: The readers agree to fatḥa on the remaining eighteen yāʾs in this section.
NASHR:v2p170/r5.anchor: على فتح ما بقي من هذا الفصل، وهو ثماني عشرة ياء
